The two sides exchanged in-depth views on the current global economic and trade situation, follow-up work after the 14th Ministerial Conference (MC14) of the WTO, and issues related to WTO reform. Wang Wentao stated that China is firmly committed to upholding the multilateral trading system and safeguarding fundamental WTO principles such as the most-favored-nation treatment. China supports the WTO in playing a more important role in improving global economic governance and stabilizing the international economic and trade order. Under the current volatile global trade situation, MC14 achieved multiple practical outcomes, demonstrating the value and resilience of the multilateral trading system and reflecting the firm determination of the majority of members to work together and overcome difficulties. In the next step, members should quickly reach consensus on unresolved issues such as the temporary exemption of tariffs on electronic transmissions.

summary: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) warns that without intervention, the EU's public debt could follow an unsustainable path. Under the current policy trajectory, by 2040, the average debt level of European countries could reach 130% of GDP - nearly double today's level. To prevent this adverse scenario, EU member states must increase incentives to promote labor mobility within the 27-nation economic bloc and encourage cross-border hiring by companies. The EU should also deepen integration of its energy market, break down barriers, allow citizens' savings to flow more smoothly across borders, and transform them into high-return investments. It should also work towards harmonizing often vastly different regulations across member states.

title: Which Assets Will Benefit from the El Niño Phenomenon?
summary: According to market sources, the probability of El Niño in 2026 exceeds 82%, with potential for an extreme tail risk. Sugar prices are at a six-year cycle bottom, palm oil and natural rubber lag behind ONI peak by 4-5 quarters before reaching price highs, cotton is constrained by demand and inventory, and thermal power coal faces a summer electricity window - but the 2023 example has shown that weather-driven gains do not necessarily translate into price gains. Whether production cuts can penetrate inventory and trade channels is the real deciding factor.
content:
The weather variable in 2026 is no longer just meteorological news. The National Climate Center's April monitoring estimates that 2026 May will enter an El Niño state and form a moderate or stronger El Niño event during the summer and autumn, lasting at least until the end of this year. NOAA's May forecast also shows a high probability: the likelihood of El Niño occurring between May and July 2026 is over 82%, with a 96% chance of continuing through the Northern Hemisphere winter, and a probability of exceeding 30% of developing into an extreme category in November.

Analysts from Guosheng Securities, including Xu Wenhui, pointed out in their report on May 20 that 'The 2026 El Niño event will cause climatic disturbances in major agricultural producing areas such as sugar, palm oil, rubber, and cotton, potentially driving reduced production and thus pushing up prices.' This same climatic chain will also affect summer electricity demand in China: northern drought and southern flooding, rising temperatures, may increase thermal power generation and demand for power coal.

The most notable point is not simply 'El Niño comes, commodities rise.' Sugar is also combined with its own approximately six-year price cycle, showing signs of a cycle bottom in 2026; palm oil and natural rubber often do not immediately reach their peaks, but rather see price highs about four quarters after the ONI index peaks, 4-5 quarters later; cotton is more constrained by demand and inventory, and in 2023-2024, prices reached peaks before the ONI index did.

Therefore, historical maximum price increases cannot be directly extrapolated into 2026 returns. What truly needs attention are three things: whether the weather in the main producing areas translates into actual production cuts, whether the production cuts enter the inventory and trade channels, and whether the price response lags and is fulfilled.

The probability of this round of El Niño is not low, and the intensity also has tail risks

The definition of El Niño is not complicated: when the three-month moving average of the NINO3.4 index reaches or exceeds 0.5°C and lasts for at least five months, it can be classified as an El Niño event. According to peak intensity, events with 0.5°C to below 1.3°C are weak, those between 1.3°C to below 2.0°C are moderate, those between 2.0°C to below 2.5°C are strong, and those above 2.5°C are extreme.

Since 1980, there have been 13 El Niño events, including six moderate events and three extreme events. The duration of nine events of moderate or higher intensity ranges from seven to 19 months, mostly peaking during the Northern Hemisphere winter.

The direction of climate impact is relatively clear: Southeast Asia and Australia are more prone to high temperatures and droughts, increasing the risk of forest fires; China is more likely to experience northern drought and southern flooding; South America and the southern part of North America are prone to heavy rain; the central and eastern parts of North America are more prone to high temperatures.

This explains why agricultural products, thermal power, and coal have simultaneously entered the observation list. The former looks at supply disruptions, while the latter looks at summer electricity demand.

Sugar is not purely a weather trade, but also on a six-year cycle

Sugar is the most special type of asset in this review. Global sugar production mainly occurs in Brazil, India, the EU, Thailand, and China, accounting for about 60% of global output. Its price shows a clear six-year complete cycle feature.

In the past three cycles:

  • After the bottom in 2008, sugar prices rose to 2011, then fell to 2014;

  • After the bottom in 2014, they rose to 2017, then adjusted to 2020;

  • After the bottom in 2020, they rose to 2023, then entered a downward phase, with signs of a bottom in 2026.

Historically, El Niño has repeatedly coincided with sugar price upswings. The maximum price increase in the 2009-2011 period was about 78%; in 2014-2016, it was about 55%; in 2020-2023, it was about 39%.

The underlying supply disruption is not abstract. In 2009-2010, the sugarcane crushing season in Brazil encountered wet weather, and India experienced reduced rainfall, leading to a decline in sugarcane yield per unit area. In the 2008/09 sugar year, India's sugar production fell by 24% year-on-year, and in the 2009/10 sugar year, it continued to drop to 18 million to 18.5 million tons; less rainfall in central Thailand and continuous drought in Guangxi, China's main sugarcane production area.

In 2014-2016, the sugarcane crushing peak period in Brazil saw increased rainfall, affecting harvesting and sugar yield; the main sugarcane production areas in India experienced high temperature and drought, reducing sugar production by 9.18% year-on-year in the 2015/16 sugar year, reaching a seven-year low, and shifting from a net sugar exporter to a net importer; Thailand's sugar production decreased by 13%.

However, the 2023-2024 period provided a counterexample: Brazil's abundant rainfall led to a significant increase in production, offsetting some of the production reduction pressure in certain regions, and sugar prices peaked before the ONI index did. This indicates that sugar has a large elasticity, but it also relies more on the yield hedging relationship between main producing areas.

Palm oil and natural rubber pay more attention to the lag effect

The main producing areas of palm oil are highly concentrated, with Malaysia and Indonesia accounting for about 80% of global production year-round. Historically, the peak price of palm oil usually lags behind the ONI index peak by about four quarters.

In three El Niño events, the maximum price increases of palm oil futures were as follows:

  • 2009-2010: About 71%;

  • 2014-2016: About 48%;

  • 2023-2024: About 45%.

In 2009, rainfall in Southeast Asia sharply decreased, and Indonesia's palm oil production for 2010 was revised down from an expected 24.5 million tons to a final 21.96 million tons, while Malaysia was revised down from an expected 20.5 million tons to 16.99 million tons, which was a period with a strong price reaction.

In the 2014-2016 period, although it was an extreme El Niño, the price elasticity of palm oil was weaker than the previous period, due to the global supply of bean oils being loose, and the import volume of major demanders such as the EU, India, and China decreased, leading to inventory accumulation. Similarly, in 2023, Malaysia's palm oil production did not decrease but increased, with rising inventory in the producing areas, and monthly rainfall did not significantly decrease, so the weather impact was not fully realized.

Natural rubber has a stronger El Niño characteristic, and the lag is even more obvious. In the past five events, the peak price of natural rubber generally occurred 4-5 quarters after the ONI peak.

The maximum price increases in the five periods were as follows:

  • 1997-1998: About 33%;

  • 2002-2003: About 118%;

  • 2009-2010: About 167%;

  • 2014-2016: About 101%;

  • 2023-2024: About 54%.

The main producing areas of natural rubber are concentrated in the Asia-Pacific region, and it is naturally affected by drought in Southeast Asia. In 2002-2003, prolonged drought was unfavorable for rubber tree growth, causing latex to dry up, coupled with global economic growth and overselling of forward orders, leading to a sharp rise in prices. In 2009, the natural rubber production of ANRPC member countries was 8.917 million tons, a decrease of 3.5% year-on-year. In 2016, the production of ANRPC member countries was 10.77 million tons, a decrease of 2.5% year-on-year.

In the 2023-2024 period, the combination of El Niño, aging rubber trees, and a shortage of tapping workers affected supply; in 2024, both domestic and foreign producing areas were affected by high temperatures and drought, making the tapping process difficult. On the demand side, downstream tire companies maintained stable demand, and semi-steel tire exports performed well, amplifying the price elasticity from both supply and demand sides.

The difficulty with cotton lies in the fact that weather-driven gains may be suppressed by demand

Cotton will also be affected by El Niño, but its price path is more complex. Major producing areas include Asia-Pacific, North America, Latin America, and Africa, involving China, India, Pakistan, Australia, the US, and Brazil.

Historically, the maximum price increases of cotton futures in three related events were as follows:

  • 2009-2010: About 149%;

  • 2014-2016: About 54%;

  • 2023-2024: About 30.7%.

The 2009-2010 period was a supply and demand resonance. Reduced rainfall in the western Pacific led to severe droughts in South Asia, Southeast Asia, and Australia, affecting cotton planting and production; India imposed a cotton export ban; and the Chinese textile and apparel industry rebounded. At that time, global cotton consumption exceeded production by 15 percentage points, and inventories rapidly declined, amplifying price elasticity.

The 2014-2016 period first experienced inventory pressure. In the 2014/15 season, global cotton ending inventory reached 23.531 million tons, increasing for five consecutive years, setting a new high since 1960. Subsequently, insufficient demand led to production cuts, with reduced planting areas in the US, Australia, and China, and El Niño further impacted Xinjiang, India, and Australia. Cotton prices rose continuously after reaching a bottom in March 2016.

The 2023-2024 period was another warning. On the demand side, it was weak, with increased supply due to the release of reserve cotton and the issuance of sliding tax quota allocations, which lowered spinning capacity utilization. On the supply side, although the US experienced consecutive droughts, Brazil had a significant bumper crop, offsetting part of the US cotton production risk. As a result, cotton prices peaked before the ONI index did.

This means that whether cotton can show strong elasticity in 2026 depends not only on the weather but also on whether demand and inventory align.

Thermal power and power coal look at the summer window

Agricultural products look at production cuts, while thermal power and power coal look at electricity demand.

During the three El Niño events from 2009-2010, 2014-2016, and 2023-2024, when the ONI index reached its peak, the national thermal power generation typically increased, and power coal demand also increased in tandem.

The logic is straightforward: El Niño drives global temperature increases, and China's summer is prone to northern drought and southern flooding, with rapid temperature rises increasing electricity demand; apart from hydropower, thermal power output and power coal consumption also increase accordingly.

Therefore, coal and power are not an extension of the agricultural product production cut logic, but another weather transmission chain: high temperatures — electricity demand — thermal power — power coal.

Trading this line, the key is not the El Niño itself, but the realization of production cuts

Historical reviews clearly indicate the list: sugar, palm oil, natural rubber, cotton, as well as coal and power-related companies and industry ETFs, are all directions to track in the 2026 El Niño framework.

But avoid treating 'El Niño' as a one-click button for price increases. The 2023-2024 period has already demonstrated that even with a moderate-level El Niño, sugar and cotton may peak before the ONI index does; palm oil may also have limited reactions if the rainfall in the producing areas does not significantly decrease and inventory accumulates.

A more realistic tracking sequence is: first, watch for abnormal weather in the main producing areas, then see if production expectations are revised downward, followed by changes in inventory and trade flows, and finally, whether the price enters a delayed upward phase.

Meteorological changes themselves can disrupt supply, and changes in dollar liquidity can affect the performance of major asset classes; more importantly, historical calculations rely on past samples, and if the market structure undergoes drastic changes, asset performance will also change.

Sugar prices are at a six-year cycle bottom, palm oil and natural rubber lag behind ONI peak by 4-5 quarters before reaching price highs, cotton is constrained by demand and inventory, and thermal power coal faces a summer electricity window - but the 2023 example has shown that weather-driven gains do not necessarily translate into price gains. Whether production cuts can penetrate inventory and trade channels is the real deciding factor.

title: The 'Impossible Triangle' of the Strait of Hormuz
summary: Global markets are betting on a dangerous 'impossible triangle': financial risk premiums near a 20-year low, oil inventories potentially reaching critical levels in June, and a 30% probability of the Strait of Hormuz reopening. Bank of America Merrill Lynch warns that these three cannot coexist - once inventory buffers are exhausted, demand destruction will trigger an oil price shockwave impacting the global economy, while macroeconomic cracks hidden by the AI boom are widening, and the market's calm may just be a prelude to a storm.
content:
Global markets are simultaneously betting on three conflicting propositions - risk premiums at a 20-year low, oil inventories about to run out, and the strait remaining closed indefinitely. Bank of America Merrill Lynch warns that this 'impossible triangle' means the market severely underestimates the risk of demand destruction.

According to market observers, Bank of America Merrill Lynch strategists Sebastian Raedler and others in a report released on May 22 noted that since the Iranian conflict began in late February, European equities have only fallen 2%, while global equities have risen 4% and reached record highs.

The calm in the market mainly relies on three pillars: relatively moderate increases in oil prices (due to ample prior inventory), resilient U.S. macroeconomic data (supported by early-year large-scale tax refunds), and an AI investment boom driving global earnings momentum far beyond what the macroeconomic fundamentals imply. However, these supports are gradually weakening.

Three Propositions, One Contradiction

The report characterizes the current market pricing as three incompatible propositions, calling it the 'impossible triangle of the Strait of Hormuz.'

The first proposition: financial risk premiums are approaching a 20-year low. The recent rebound in asset prices has compressed financial risk premiums back to near年初's 20-year low. The European equity risk premium (ERP) is currently 4.75%, just 25 basis points above its recent low; the U.S. high-yield credit spread is 275 basis points, only 15 basis points above its recent low. With global growth momentum as the main driver, the current risk premium level implies the market expects global PMI to moderately recover from current levels, rather than being dragged down by energy supply shocks.

The second proposition: oil inventories will fall to critical levels. Given that oil inventories have been significantly depleted, 'it is crucial to quickly restore energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz to prevent a major economic recession.' Several market participants believe that, at the current rate of consumption, global oil inventories may reach operational pressure levels around June. If the inventory buffer is exhausted, supply-demand imbalance will only be adjusted through demand destruction - that is, oil prices will further rise until demand is suppressed, which aligns with historical experiences of energy price shocks.

Some investors believe demand destruction will primarily occur in emerging markets, with the U.S., as a net energy exporter, able to remain unaffected. However, oil is a globally priced commodity, and demand destruction will impact all economies through higher gasoline prices, further depressing U.S. household real income growth.

The third proposition: the market predicts a low probability of the strait reopening in the short term. According to the prediction market platform Kalshi, the probability of the Strait of Hormuz resuming navigation before the end of June has dropped from 75% in mid-April to about 30%, and the probability of resuming before early August is also only 40%.

Different from the previous trade war, this confrontation around the Strait of Hormuz is a multi-party game - both the U.S. and Iran believe waiting for the other side to bear more pain is beneficial for themselves, which could extend the duration of the conflict beyond investors' expectations. The Iranian regime can maintain fiscal operations through limited oil exports and has the capacity to sustain the situation.

The tension between the three propositions is evident: if the strait remains closed as predicted by the market and inventory buffers are depleting, the current pricing of demand destruction risk is overly optimistic.

Macro Resilience Is Fading

Despite the calm in the market, macroeconomic data has shown divergence. In the U.S., labor market, consumer, and capital expenditure data have remained strong so far, but the support effect from the early-year large-scale tax refunds has already faded, and "the true test of consumer and labor market resilience may not have arrived yet." U.S. real labor income growth has fallen to a recession level due to inflation pressures from rising energy prices, and the core PCE inflation in the U.S. is expected to remain slightly above 3% over the next few months.

The situation in the eurozone is even more severe. The eurozone composite PMI new orders index fell to a two-year low of 47.1 in May, and the eurozone private final demand growth is expected to slow significantly over the next few quarters. European natural gas prices have continued to rise since the Iranian conflict began, adding extra pressure on the eurozone PMI.

Notably, global earnings momentum is still significantly exceeding the level implied by macroeconomic fundamentals - the 3-month change in forward earnings per share for the U.S. is 8%, and for Europe, it is 5%, both the strongest since 2021, driven mainly by financial, resource, and technology sectors fueled by the AI investment boom. However, Bank of America Merrill Lynch expects that as macroeconomic pressures take effect, the 12-month forward earnings per share of the Stoxx 600 will decline by about 5% from the current historical high, corresponding to a 2026 earnings growth rate of -1%, below the market's bottom-up consensus forecast.

title: The Contradictory Trends of US Equities and Treasuries: Who Will Win Next?
summary: The divergence between US equities and Treasuries is approaching a critical point. A BCA Research chief strategist warns that the S&P 500's up-and-down line has diverged from the index's movement, with only 55% of its components above the 200-day moving average, indicating that the tech sector's dominance is unsustainable. Rising bond yields, persistently high inflation, and the Federal Reserve's difficult policy choices have created three pressures, suggesting that a substantial market correction may be imminent, with emerging markets likely to be hit first.
content:
US equities and Treasuries are heading toward an unavoidable collision. With persistent inflation and limited monetary policy space, the simultaneous rise in stock prices and bond yields is unsustainable, and the gap between them will eventually be closed by a significant decline in one of them.

Recently, Arthur Budaghyan, chief strategist at BCA Research, released a report stating that the current rally in the US stock market is heavily concentrated in the technology sector, and the internal structure of the market has clearly deteriorated. The sustained increase in bond yields could serve as the trigger for a substantive market correction.

He argues that only a clear decline in the US stock market can lower bond yields and thus release anti-inflationary forces on the economic level. The report also warns that global risk assets, especially emerging markets, will face significant volatility in the coming months.

This implies that the risk-reward ratio of current global risk assets has significantly deteriorated. US equities, emerging market stocks, and high-yield credit bonds all face downward pressure, while the dollar may remain strong in the short term but remains in a weak trend in the medium term.

The Fed Faces a Dilemma, and Bond Market Pressure Remains

The Federal Reserve now faces a difficult decision on whether to raise interest rates, and neither choice will be favorable for the market.

According to a BCA Research report, the yield on the two-year US Treasury note has recently risen above the federal funds rate. Historical data shows that over the past 30 years, whenever the two-year yield crossed above the federal funds rate, the Fed subsequently raised rates. This indicates that expectations for rate hikes have significantly increased.

At the same time, inflation data continues to exceed target levels. Core CPI in the United States is significantly above 2%, and the PPI for final demand (excluding energy and food) has surged to 5.25%, with its six-month annualized change rate reaching 6.6% in April. The report also points out that the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz is unlikely to be resolved in the short term, and oil price upward risks are significant. Oil prices and US Treasury yields have shown a strong correlation this year, further compressing the space for a significant decline in bond yields.

The report emphasizes that even if the new Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh persuades the Federal Open Market Committee to delay raising rates, the Fed's policy statements and inclinations will become significantly more hawkish. More importantly, when inflation rises and the central bank delays action, the market often expects larger future rate hikes, which could lead to further selling in the bond market. "The central bank falling behind the inflation curve is bearish for both stocks and bonds," the report states.

Market Structure Deteriorates, Rally Hides Concerns

title: Dingdong Maicai Awaits Integration into Meituan, Front-End Warehouses Still Contributing Growth
summary: Transition Period Report
content:
Dingdong Maicai released its first financial report after Meituan announced the acquisition of its China business.

In the first quarter, Dingdong Maicai's GMV reached 6.33 billion yuan, up 6.3% year-on-year; total revenue was 5.893 billion yuan, up 7.5% year-on-year; it has achieved consecutive growth in GMV and revenue for the ninth quarter in a row.

During the reporting period, Dingdong Maicai's total net profit was 165 million yuan, and its Non-GAAP net profit was 172 million yuan.

However, due to the accounting treatment related to Meituan transactions, the company classified long-term assets related to its China business as assets held for sale and ceased depreciation and amortization, which increased net profit by approximately 138 million yuan.

Excluding this impact, the actual operating net profit was approximately 28 million yuan, a 2.4-fold increase compared to 80 million yuan in the same period last year.

This financial report therefore carries a special transitional character. Currently, the transaction where Meituan acquired Dingdong Maicai's China business for an initial consideration of 717 million USD is still awaiting approval from the State Administration for Market Regulation's antitrust review.

Under U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, Dingdong Maicai has classified its China business as a discontinued operation, while its overseas business is classified as a continuing operation; related China business assets and liabilities are classified as assets and liabilities held for sale.

In other words, before the transaction is completed, the China business remains the main source of revenue and profit for Dingdong Maicai; however, from an accounting presentation and future structure perspective, this business has entered a divestiture process.

In the first quarter, Dingdong Maicai's China business revenue reached 5.753 billion yuan, up 5.9% year-on-year. The overall gross margin was 29.9%, flat with the same period last year; the fulfillment cost ratio decreased from 22.9% to 20.6% compared to the same period last year.

The company stated that the growth of the China business mainly came from an increase in monthly active users, higher order frequency leading to increased order volume, and improved site density and market penetration in the East China region following the opening of new front-end warehouses. However, the decline in CPI for major categories such as pork also partially offset the revenue growth rate.

This aligns with Dingdong Maicai's adjustment direction over the past few years.

The advantage of the front-end warehouse model lies in its proximity to consumers and faster delivery, making it suitable for high-frequency fresh product demand; however, the challenges include heavy costs for rent, labor, delivery, and waste.

Once order density is insufficient, revenue growth can easily be eroded by fulfillment costs. Over the past few years, Dingdong Maicai has shifted from nationwide expansion to regional focus, essentially rebalancing scale and efficiency.

East China is a core market that Dingdong Maicai has long focused on, with relatively mature user habits, supply chain organization, warehouse network density, and fulfillment efficiency.

This is one of the backgrounds for Meituan's acquisition of Dingdong Maicai's China business. For Meituan, the value of Dingdong Maicai is not just a fresh e-commerce brand, but also a front-end warehouse network and fresh supply chain capability that has been operating in the East China market for many years with a certain level of order density. If the transaction is completed, these assets are likely to be integrated into Meituan's instant retail system, enhancing its fresh product fulfillment capabilities.

The overseas business, although still small in scale but growing rapidly, has begun to become an important clue for external observers to track Dingdong Maicai's post-transaction direction.

In the first quarter, Dingdong Maicai's overseas business revenue grew 195.2% year-on-year to 139 million yuan, but the net loss also expanded 199.6% year-on-year to 71.4 million yuan, still in a phase of high growth and high investment.

From public information, Dingdong Maicai's overseas business roughly includes two categories: one is import supply chain, meaning bringing overseas products into the domestic market through a global direct procurement system; the other is channel expansion, selling ready-made meals, fresh products, refrigerated food, and other goods to overseas markets.

Previously, the company had chosen Saudi Arabia as its first overseas expansion destination, attempting to sell ready-made meals, fresh products, refrigerated food, and general merchandise to the local market. Essentially, it was replicating its domestic experience in product development, supply chain organization, and front-end warehouse operations overseas.

The China business awaits transfer, while the overseas business is still immature. Dingdong Maicai is still in a true transition period.

title: AMD's Lisa Su: Global CPU Supply Shortage Continues, Company Expands Production Every Quarter
summary: Surging CPU demand has exceeded all expectations, with AMD CEO Lisa Su stating the market is facing a 'supply tightness.' The rise of agent AI is extending demand from GPUs to CPUs. AMD has locked production capacity in Taiwan through 2029, invested over $1 billion in advanced packaging, and has already mass-produced TSMC's 2nm Venice chips.
content:
Global CPU demand has exceeded expectations, and AMD is accelerating capacity expansion to address the supply gap.

According to Reuters, AMD Chief Executive Lisa Su stated on Friday that the CPU market is currently experiencing supply tightness, with demand strength far exceeding predictions from a year ago.

She said, AMD expects supply volumes to continue increasing each quarter this year, with supply scale significantly expanding in 2027 and beyond. Su attributed this demand growth to the rapid adoption of AI inference and agent AI.

Previously, AMD announced an investment of over $1 billion in the AI sector to deepen strategic partnerships and expand advanced AI chip assembly and manufacturing capabilities. This investment covers advanced packaging, substrates, and rack-level system manufacturing, involving multiple companies including ASE, SPIL, PTI, Wiwynn, Wistron, Inventec, Unimicron, AIC, Nan Ya PCB, and Kinsus.

CPU Demand Surpasses Expectations, Market Supply Remains Tight

She clearly stated at a forum in Taipei: "Overall CPU market demand is much higher than any of our predictions a year ago, and I believe the CPU market is currently tight."

Su pointed out that the core driver of this demand expansion lies in the rise of agent AI. Unlike GPUs used for training large models, CPUs are regaining focus as enterprises and institutions shift toward autonomous function-enabled agent AI systems, with demand boundaries expanding from GPUs to CPUs.

Taiwan Production Layout, Investment Locked Through 2029

AMD stated that the current investment in Taiwan focuses on advanced packaging, substrates, and rack-level system manufacturing. Su explained that due to the long delivery cycles of some investments, partners need to lock land, factories, and manufacturing capacity in advance, so AMD is investing jointly with partners to ensure production capacity through 2026 and beyond until 2029.

In terms of process technology, AMD announced on Thursday that it has begun mass-producing the 2nm Venice CPU using TSMC's process.

Su said that AMD's bet on TSMC was a "very correct decision," and that AMD's second important strategic judgment—that increasingly complex chip technology requires splitting chips into smaller units and integrating them through advanced packaging technology—has now become the mainstream path in the semiconductor industry.

Additionally, she revealed that China accounts for about 20% of AMD's revenue and is an "important" market. She said she will continue to maintain close cooperation with Chinese customers. Su stated: "Frankly speaking, considering the market size and our product portfolio, we will continue to maintain very close collaboration with Chinese customers."

title: Will Google Ruin the Internet? When Search Becomes an AI Assistant, You'll Never Need to Click Any Website Again
summary: Google launched a new search function deeply integrated with AI, allowing users to receive direct answers and personalized push notifications instead of traditional link redirection. This move has raised concerns among content publishers about significant traffic loss and the potential zeroing out of search traffic. Critics argue that it transforms the internet from an open exploration platform into a closed community filtered by AI, which may fundamentally weaken the diversity and serendipity of information access.
content:
Google's next-generation search function with deep AI integration is sparking deep concerns about the internet ecosystem.

At this week's I/O Developer Conference, Google demonstrated its new search vision: the system will no longer return lists of links but will directly generate AI answers, custom animations, and personalized news updates. Demonstration scenarios include: when an athlete releases a new pair of sneakers, the AI agent will proactively send reminders; when a student asks about black holes, Google not only generates a textual answer but also automatically creates a corresponding animation, and finally provides a link for further reading.

Robby Stein, Vice President of Google Search Products, said at the event, "We believe the best search experience is tailored specifically for you."

For content publishers, these changes mean severe traffic pressure. The extreme scenario where Google search traffic disappears is called "Google Zero" in the industry. In recent years, as the AI Overviews feature was launched and tools like ChatGPT became popular, the search referral traffic for news media from Google has been continuously declining. According to technology reporter Katie Notopoulos from Business Insider, when a search engine can fully answer user questions within its own interface, users' motivation to click on external websites will significantly decrease, and "Google Zero" may accelerate.

From Keywords to AI Butler: A Fundamental Shift in Search Paradigm

For decades, Google Search followed a simple logic: users enter keywords, and the system returns relevant website links for users to judge and click on. This process is not only a path for users to obtain information but also the traffic foundation supporting publishers, blogs, and various websites.

Google's new features fundamentally change this logic. In the black hole example, a student's question directly triggers the AI to generate a textual explanation and a customized animation. The system's role shifts from being a "directory" to a "teacher." In the hiking trail example, when users seek routes that combine restaurants and parking lots nearby, the AI integrates multiple sources of information to provide recommendations without users needing to switch to any third-party platform.

Personalization is another core element of this update. Google states that AI agents can perceive user preferences and actively push alerts when relevant content appears. This capability relies on Google's extensive user data accumulated over many years. Robby Stein defines this experience as the "best form" of search, but critics argue that it is essentially just an AI chatbot disguised as a search tool.

The Shadow of "Google Zero": Structural Impact on Publishers

"Google Zero" is not alarmist. In recent years, as Google began presenting AI summaries directly on search result pages, many users no longer need to click on original websites to get answers, leading to substantial erosion of traffic for publishers. At the same time, more and more users are starting to use AI tools like ChatGPT instead of traditional search, further diverting potential traffic.

If the new AI search function is widely implemented, it will further intensify these trends. When the Google interface itself becomes the endpoint of information rather than an entry point to external websites, the search referral traffic that content publishers rely on will face fundamental challenges. For media that depend on advertising revenue or paid subscriptions, this directly affects their revenue foundation.

It is worth noting that Google has not completely abandoned external links - in the new AI search results, links still exist but have been pushed to a secondary position. This design reflects Google's balancing dilemma between advancing AI capabilities and maintaining the publisher ecosystem, but whether this balance can be sustained remains uncertain.

Closed Community or Open City - Who Defines "Your Internet"

The deeper controversy of this update lies in how it changes the fundamental relationship between users and the internet.

Katie Notopoulos compares the traditional internet to a city where users can freely explore - Google is the entrance, and users get a map and then explore independently. The new AI search, however, resembles a closed community with strict management, where information is filtered before being presented to users, deliberately shielding the chaos and serendipity of the outside world.

The cost of this "personalized" experience is that users increasingly cannot access information deemed irrelevant by the algorithm, and the sense of exploration and serendipity on the internet will disappear. Critics argue that part of the value of the internet lies in those "imperfect frictions" - unexpected websites, unfamiliar links, and the process of self-navigation. Outsourcing these experiences to AI means losing a unique way of accessing information.

Criticism is not limited to "old-fashioned" users. A clear resistance exists among Gen Z toward AI, which may affect their acceptance of the new Google search product. As the next generation of internet users, Gen Z's attitudes will directly influence the commercial success of Google's transformation.

Google maintains full confidence in its new product, believing that personalization and AI-driven efficiency improvements will be the core competitiveness of future search. However, the paradigm battle over the search experience will ultimately be decided by the actual behavior of billions of users.

title: Nomura Report: From Silicon to Glass, from GPU to Optical Communication, AI is Reshaping the Entire Semiconductor Supply Chain
summary: AI computing power is forcing a reconfiguration of semiconductor manufacturing processes, shifting growth logic from simple transistor scaling to 3D transistors, backside power delivery, and combinations of new materials. Starting in 2027, advanced packaging, lithography materials, photonic SOI, and glass substrates will enter volume production, driving a revaluation of the entire supply chain. TSMC's expansion and localization procurement will become the core driver of order transmission, as the semiconductor manufacturing industry enters a synchronized cycle of structural, packaging, and material upgrades.
content:
The demand for AI computing power is changing the way the semiconductor industry grows. For decades, chip performance improvements were mainly driven by Moore's Law: making transistors smaller and denser. However, after continued scaling of advanced processes, metal pitch, power consumption, leakage, heat dissipation, yield, and cost have begun to approach their limits, and simply betting on 'smaller nodes' is no longer sufficient.

According to market observers, Nomura Securities' APAC tech analyst Donnie Teng team highlighted in a report that the growth logic of the semiconductor industry has shifted from increasing transistor density to 'a combination of 3D transistors, backside power delivery, and diverse new materials.' This statement is the core of the entire study: AI is not only driving demand for GPUs but is also forcing a rewrite of the fundamental manufacturing processes of chips.

A more direct investment implication is that materials, consumables, substrates, specialty gases, and compound semiconductors, once considered supporting segments, are now becoming key variables determining the performance of advanced chips. Especially starting in 2027, technologies such as backside power delivery, wafer bonding NAND, glass core substrates, and photonic SOI will enter volume production, potentially leading to a systematic revaluation of the materials segment.

TSMC remains the most important amplifier in this chain. Advanced capacity expansion, SoIC hybrid bonding, high-NA EUV introduction, and increased localization procurement will transmit orders to equipment, materials, and component companies. Unlike the previous semiconductor cycle, this one is not just about a single process upgrade but involves simultaneous transitions in structure, packaging, and materials.

Moore's Law is not失效, but 'just shrinking' is no longer enough

The issues with advanced processes are not that they cannot continue forward, but that the costs are getting higher.

From 7nm to 3nm, and then to the next node, further compression of metal pitch will bring more serious power consumption, leakage, and heat dissipation problems. The patterning capability of low-NA EUV and DUV is also limited, and multiple exposure can solve some precision issues, but at the cost of increased costs and yield pressure.

Therefore, advanced logic chips are turning to more complex structural innovations. GAA gate-all-around transistors will continue to evolve toward stacked cFETs, with the core goal of improving gate control over the channel while increasing integration.

Backside power delivery is more like a 'redesign of wiring.' The power network moves from the front of the wafer to the back, separating it from the signal network, and using wider, lower-resistance metal lines for power delivery, reducing IR voltage drop and decreasing backend wiring congestion. This leaves space for further shrinking standard cells.

These changes are not just concepts; they have direct impact on process usage. The number of CMP steps for advanced process chips will increase from 45-55 in traditional processes to 55-70, an increase of 20%-30%. Backside power delivery also requires two wafers to be stacked, doubling wafer consumption, and simultaneously increasing demand for wafer thinning, grinding, and bonding.

The timing is also critical: related equipment and material demand will start in 2026, enter a rapid volume phase in 2027, and by 2030 could become a standard for advanced chips.

High-NA EUV Truly Opens the Door for Lithography Material Upgrades

High-NA EUV is the core equipment for the next generation of advanced processes. The numerical aperture increases from 0.33 to 0.55, resolution reaches 8nm, and aims to eliminate the need for multi-patterning at nodes below 3nm, with mass production expected as early as 2029. Each machine costs over $400 million.

However, high-NA EUV is not just about buying equipment. A higher numerical aperture means photons hit the wafer at a shallower angle, requiring thinner photoresist layers, otherwise shadow effects occur. Traditional chemical amplification photoresists lack sufficient etch resistance, photon absorption efficiency, and pattern accuracy under ultra-thin conditions.

Metall oxide photoresists therefore become the key material. They use metal oxides as the core, offering stronger etching selectivity, higher resolution, and better roughness control, making them more suitable for high-NA processes.

The change in value is clear: existing EUV photoresist prices are around $5,000 per gallon, while high-NA EUV-specific metall oxide photoresists can reach $10,000 to $40,000 per gallon, with unit price increases of 2 to 8 times.

Lithography material upgrades go beyond photoresists. Reticle materials also need to be replaced. Traditional tantalum-based absorbers struggle to adapt to the reflection angle requirements of high-NA processes, with ruthenium and molybdenum-based materials emerging as alternatives. Supporting materials such as developers, cleaning solutions, bottom anti-reflective coatings, and edge removal liquids will also upgrade accordingly.

The Next Competition in Advanced Packaging May Be on Glass Substrates

AI chips increasingly rely on advanced packaging because continuing to scale up single chips and stack computing power hits multiple limitations in power consumption, interconnects, heat dissipation, and manufacturing yield.

SoIC hybrid bonding will see a surge in demand between 2026 and 2027, primarily used for high-density integration of AI chips and HBM. Compared to traditional micro bump processes, hybrid bonding achieves Cu-Cu direct connection, increasing interconnect density by an order of magnitude, with bandwidth rising from 200GB/s to 1TB/s.

It has high process requirements: wafer surface flatness must be controlled at the nanometer level, making CMP a key step; bonding equipment precision must be less than 0.2 microns; cleaning, surface activation, and alignment must also be upgraded. BESI, a leader in chip-level and wafer-level hybrid bonding equipment, has seen orders rapidly rebound since 2026, driven by AI chips, optical communication, and HBM.

Package substrates are also changing materials. Glass core substrates offer lower thermal expansion coefficient, higher flatness, better heat dissipation, and lower signal loss compared to traditional ABF organic substrates, making them more suitable for large-size, high-power, high-speed signal chips.

In scenario assumptions, Broadcom is expected to adopt glass core substrates for switch ASICs in 2027, while Intel is advancing its development of glass substrates as core materials for next-generation advanced packaging. However, glass substrates are not yet fully mature, and large-scale mass production still faces challenges including high costs, RDL dielectric layer delamination and stratification, and yield improvement.

The real process challenge lies in TGV glass vias. Laser drilling, etching, metal filling, and planarization determine final performance. Ingentec, which holds TGV patent technology, is entering this supply chain.

Optical Communication Puts Compound Semiconductors in the Spotlight

The bottleneck in AI data centers is not only in GPUs but also in communication. High-speed optical modules and CPO co-packaged optics are driving upward movement in the optical communication supply chain, with 1.6T module adoption and silicon photonic migration as two main trends.

Indium phosphide substrates are used for EML and CW laser chips, which are core materials for optical modules. Due to restrictions on indium metal exports and production yield bottlenecks, indium phosphide will remain in short supply from 2025 to 2027, keeping prices high.

Another route is photonic SOI wafers, used for silicon photonic integrated chips (PIC). Its cost is only 25% of that of indium phosphide substrates, making it more suitable for mass production, and it is the core material for CPO solutions. Soitec holds 70% of the global market share for photonic SOI wafers, while GlobalWafers and Shanghai Silicon Industry are following suit.

By 2027, demand for photonic SOI will enter a rapid growth phase, becoming the most important growth driver in the SOI wafer sector.

12-inch Silicon Wafers, Supply and Demand Tighten from 2027 Onward

With the manufacturing process changes brought by AI, silicon wafer demand will rise again.

Regular market demand grows at an annual rate of about 5%. TSMC, Samsung, and Intel expanding production adds another 2-3 percentage points of demand annually. Three new technologies—backside power delivery, wafer bonding NAND, and photonic SOI—will add another 2-3 percentage points of demand each year.

Combined, the overall annual demand growth rate for 12-inch silicon wafers approaches 10%.

Supply side is not catching up quickly. Silicon wafer capacity expansion is limited by equipment delivery timelines and capital expenditure rhythms, making it difficult to immediately match demand. Starting in 2027, supply-demand gaps will gradually emerge, and leading companies such as GlobalWafers, Shin-Etsu, and SUMCO will see improved pricing power, with long-term prices continuously rising. Ancillary businesses such as wafer regeneration and test wafers will also benefit.

TSMC Expansion and Localization Procurement Are Catalysts for Supply Chain Volume Growth

TSMC's capital expenditures in 2027 are expected to reach $70 billion, with 26 advanced wafer fabrication plants and packaging bases worldwide moving forward with expansion, 18 of which are located in Taiwan, with U.S., Japanese, and German factories also ramping up.

Advanced capacity release will directly drive demand for equipment, materials, and components. More importantly, TSMC continues to increase the proportion of local and regional procurement for equipment, components, and materials, covering raw materials, components, consumables, and factory equipment categories.

This opens certification and entry windows for regional suppliers. Photoresist, CMP consumables, specialty gases, silicon wafers, and packaging materials are key areas for localization procurement. Taiwanese and mainland Chinese material companies that pass certification will see significantly faster share gains than in normal cycles.

Clear Industrial Implementation Timeline, 2027 Becomes the Industry-wide Turning Point

The rhythm of this supply chain can be compressed into several time points:

2026, GAA transistors, SoIC hybrid bonding, and InP substrates start, with small-volume shipments beginning to appear.

2027, backside power delivery, wafer bonding NAND, and glass core substrates concentrate on volume production, entering larger-scale mass production stages.

2028, DRAM-on-logic architecture enters large-scale application, with edge AI and automotive electronics becoming drivers.

2029 to 2030, high-NA EUV mass production, with metall oxide photoresists and new reticle materials fully introduced.

Materials have lagged behind equipment for the past decade, partly because AI chips' high unit prices make it easier to boost revenue along the entire system and equipment chain, and partly because the Moore's Law era favored equipment, with material demand fluctuating more during industry downturns. Now the situation has changed: 3D structures, new materials, and advanced packaging are all progressing, and both material consumption and value are rising.

The most significant aspect of this change is that AI has not only brought a round of GPU prosperity, but has pushed semiconductor manufacturing from 'process scaling' to 'structural innovation + material replacement + advanced packaging'. From silicon wafers to glass substrates, from GPUs to optical communication, the value distribution across the supply chain is being rewritten once again.

content:
Main Ideas

  1. Initial Labor Agreement Eases Strike Risk
    Samsung Electronics reached a preliminary agreement with its union on wages, benefits, and a new 10-year performance bonus plan for the DS division. The deal includes a base pay raise of 4.1% and a performance-based raise of 2.1%, along with higher salary caps and improved benefits. A special operating performance bonus will allocate 10.5% of the DS division's operating profit, paid in stock and released in three installments: one-third immediately available, one-third locked for one year, and one-third locked for two years. The bonus payment conditions require the DS division's annual operating profit to exceed 200 trillion KRW from 2026E to 2028E and 100 trillion KRW from 2029E to 2035E. If the agreement is finalized, Citigroup estimates a 43 trillion KRW employee incentive charge in 2026E. Citigroup believes this agreement will alleviate market concerns about the negative impact of strikes.
  2. Maintaining Buy Rating, Target Price of 460,000 KRW
    Citigroup maintains a Buy rating for Samsung Electronics with a 12-month target price of 460,000 KRW, based on SOTP valuation (sum-of-the-parts) using 2026E EBITDA. The EV/EBITDA multiples for each segment are: memory 7.9x, foundry 4.1x, display panels 0.5x, mobile communications 4.8x, and consumer electronics 2.0x. The current share price is 299,500 KRW, with an expected return of 53.6%, a dividend yield of 0.6%, and a total expected return of 54.1%.

Facts

  1. According to Hankyung Economic News on May 20, Samsung Electronics reached a preliminary agreement with its union on wages, benefits, and a 10-year performance bonus plan for the DS division.
  2. The agreement includes a base wage increase of 4.1%, a performance-based raise of 2.1%, and a new bonus plan that draws 10.5% of the DS division's operating profit, paid in stock and released in three installments. The bonus payment conditions require the DS division's annual operating profit to reach 200 trillion KRW (2026E-2028E) and 100 trillion KRW (2029E-2035E).
  3. Citigroup estimates that if the agreement is implemented, it will result in a 43 trillion KRW employee incentive charge in 2026E, representing 12% of total operating profit (1.5% OPI and 10.5% performance incentive).
  4. Citigroup's SOTP valuation model for Samsung Electronics: memory business at 7.9x EV/EBITDA, foundry at 4.1x, display panels at 0.5x, mobile communications at 4.8x, and consumer electronics at 2.0x, based on global peer multiples.
  5. Historical ratings and target prices: Citigroup has repeatedly raised its target price since May 2023, with the latest target price increased from 300,000 KRW to 460,000 KRW.
  6. Catalyst observation: Citigroup added a 90-day upside catalyst observation on May 11, 2026, expecting the stock price to rise within 90 days.

Summary

Citigroup released a flash report on May 21, 2026, on Samsung Electronics (005930.KS), maintaining a Buy rating with a 12-month target price of 460,000 KRW, offering an expected return of 53.6% over the current share price of 299,500 KRW. The core event in the report was Samsung Electronics reaching a preliminary labor agreement with its union before planned strikes, covering wages, benefits, and a new 10-year performance bonus plan for the DS division. The plan will incentivize employees with a portion of the DS division's operating profit in the form of stock, with an estimated 43 trillion KRW in employee incentive charges in 2026E. Citigroup believes the agreement will eliminate uncertainty regarding strike risks and positively impact the stock price.

The valuation uses a sum-of-the-parts (SOTP) approach based on 2026E EBITDA, with reasonable multiples assigned to each segment (memory at 7.9x, foundry at 4.1x, display panels at 0.5x, mobile communications at 4.8x, and consumer electronics at 2.0x). The report also highlights downside risks, including delays in HBM shipments, lower-than-expected demand for PCs and NAND, competitive expansion impacting pricing, intensified competition in the smartphone market, and a stronger Korean won.

Citigroup also set up an upside catalyst observation (90-day period), further reinforcing its short-term bullish view. Historical rating changes show analysts have consistently raised the target price, with the latest adjustment from 300,000 KRW to 460,000 KRW.

Key Data

  • Target price for Samsung Electronics: 460,000 KRW, with a current share price of 299,500 KRW and an expected return of 53.6%.
  • Estimated 2026E employee incentive charge: 43 trillion KRW, representing 12% of operating profit (OPI 1.5% + performance 10.5%).
  • Wage increase: Base raise of 4.1%, performance-based raise of 2.1%.
  • New bonus plan profit threshold: 200 trillion KRW annually for 2026E-2028E and 100 trillion KRW annually for 2029E-2035E.
  • SOTP valuation multiples: Memory 7.9x, foundry 4.1x, display panels 0.5x, mobile communications 4.8x, and consumer electronics 2.0x.
  • Market data: Total market cap of 1,750,960,411 million KRW (approximately 1,169,037 million USD).

Recommended Assets

  • Samsung Electronics (005930.KS): Citigroup maintains a Buy rating with a target price of 460,000 KRW. Reasons include the labor agreement reducing strike risk, the high-level incentive plan for the DS division potentially improving capacity and yield, and the valuation based on SOTP being attractive.

Key Terms and Events

  • OPI (Operating Profit Incentive): Operating profit incentive, one of Samsung Electronics' employee bonus systems linked to operating profit.
  • SOTP (Sum-of-the-Parts): Sum-of-the-parts valuation method, where different business segments of a company are valued separately and then summed to determine total value.
  • HBM (High Bandwidth Memory): High bandwidth memory, primarily used in AI accelerators, is a key growth driver for Samsung's DS division.

  • SOTP (Sum-of-the-Parts): Sum-of-the-parts valuation method, where different business segments of a company are valued separately and then summed to determine total value.
  • HBM (High Bandwidth Memory): High bandwidth memory, primarily used in AI accelerators, is a key growth driver for Samsung's DS division.

title: Warsh's First Day Under Pressure: Markets Expect Rate Hikes This Year
summary: Warsh officially assumed the role of Federal Reserve Chair, but faced immediate market pressure on his first day. Fed Governor Waller delivered a hawkish speech, stating that inflation is the 'driving force' behind policy decisions, with a 50-50 chance of rate hikes or cuts, pushing the two-year Treasury yield to a high since February, as futures markets fully priced in a 25-basis-point rate hike this year.
content:
Warsh formally took over the Federal Reserve, but was immediately met with market pressure on his first day.

On Friday, May 22, Trump hosted an inauguration ceremony at the White House, officially passing the Federal Reserve's leadership to Warsh. As Warsh took over the central bank, rising energy and transportation costs from the Iran conflict continued to feed into inflation.

According to financial media reports, Fed Governor Waller delivered a hawkish speech on the same day, explicitly stating that inflation is the 'driving force' behind future policy decisions, and that the likelihood of rate hikes and cuts is 'fifty-fifty,' a statement that directly fueled a sharp increase in rate hike expectations.

The U.S. bond market saw selling pressure, with the two-year Treasury yield rising four basis points, hitting a high since February this year.

（Trends in yields across major maturities this week）

Futures markets have already fully priced in a 25-basis-point rate hike this year.

（Market expectation of a 25-basis-point rate hike by the Fed this year）

TS Lombard economist Steven Blitz said that if Warsh does not raise rates at his first FOMC meeting in June, the market will give him no room for leniency.

Waller Takes a Hard Line, Inflation as Policy 'Driving Force'

At the same time as Warsh was sworn in, Fed Governor Waller gave a speech in Frankfurt titled "Policy Risks Have Changed," sending the most hawkish signal to date, with a significant shift in stance that caught the market's attention.

Waller said:

Inflation is not moving in the right direction, and I support removing the 'pro-monetary easing' language from the policy statement to clearly signal that the possibility of rate hikes and cuts is now equal.

He further stated:

I can no longer rule out the possibility that, if inflation does not come down soon, we may need to raise rates.

Waller admitted that recent labor market reports and inflation data had changed his long-held view of monetary easing.

He also said that while the oil price shock might soon subside, he emphasized this does not mean "considering rate hikes in the near term," and rate hikes would require conditions where inflation expectations become "unanchored."

Earlier Fed minutes showed that "many" officials had leaned toward dropping the monetary easing bias, including three regional Fed presidents who had previously opposed the issue in April, and Waller's latest comments align with this trend.

Warsh's Debut Looms, Pressure at June Meeting Intense

Warsh will preside over his first Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in mid-June, and market observers are not optimistic about his situation.

The Fed's preferred inflation indicator has risen to its highest level in three years, with overall price growth reaching 6% in April. Market-implied one-year inflation expectations are around 4%.

Blitz from TS Lombard said, if Warsh decides not to raise rates in June, even if economic growth remains strong and is far from overheating, the market will interpret it as a de facto easing move. Blitz said:

Given the widespread rise in inflation risks, failing to raise rates in June effectively amounts to easing.

KPMG US Chief Economist Diane Swonk noted that the Middle East situation has added to existing price pressures. She said:

This is one of many reasons why the Fed cannot ignore the war and its inflation impact.

The current market expectation of a 25-basis-point rate hike contrasts sharply with the widespread bets at the start of the year for multiple rate cuts.

（Comparison of market expectations for the Fed's interest rate trajectory before and after February this year）

Although energy prices fell this week, the 10-year Treasury yield did not see a significant increase.

However, Goldman Sachs' George Cole pointed out that long-term Treasuries are slightly undervalued relative to their fair value, but the valuation has not deviated enough to support a deeper rebound.

（Long-term Treasuries appear slightly undervalued relative to fair value）

George Cole emphasized that until the macro risk landscape undergoes a substantive change, long-term yields still face structural upward risks from supply pressures and debt financing cycles.

Independence Test, Hidden Concerns Behind a Historic Inauguration

Warsh is the first Fed Chair to be sworn in at the White House since Greenspan, a detail that has been viewed by the market as a signal.

Trump hoped that this former Fed governor, whom he nominated in January, would be more compliant with calls for rate cuts. Warsh defeated Trump's economist Hassett, Waller, and BlackRock executive Rick Rieder in the nomination race.

The independence of the Fed has been under particular pressure recently.

According to financial media reports, Trump ally and U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro had launched a criminal investigation into Powell over the $25 billion Fed headquarters renovation project. The investigation was later dropped, but Powell said it was an excuse to pressure officials into cutting rates.

Warsh's four-year term as chair makes him the 17th chairman of the Fed.

Nevertheless, the market has made it clear: regardless of the political environment, inflation is the most pressing issue at hand, and this new chairman has little time to plan carefully.
