title: Bloomberg Daily Brief | May 23, 2026
summary: Five minutes to understand global markets, all in the financial breakfast.
content:
Early Morning Voice

Market Overview

AI tech stocks lifted U.S. equities, with the S&P 500 up 0.37%, extending its eight-week consecutive rise, marking the longest streak since 2023. The Dow rose 0.58% and continued to hit new highs.

NVIDIA fell 1.9%, with a weekly decline of 4.4%. The tech seven giants underperformed the broader market, while utilities outperformed tech, and energy and materials lagged. Qualcomm surged over 11%. Strong performance from Lenovo Group boosted U.S. computer manufacturers, with Dell Technologies rising 17% to a new high and HP up 15%. U.S. quantum computing stocks surged again. Estee Lauder rose 12% after terminating potential merger talks with Puig.

Federal Reserve official Waller's hawkish remarks pressured U.S. Treasuries, pushing the two-year Treasury yield up 4 basis points to a two-month high.

The dollar remained stable around 99.2. Bitcoin dropped over 2% intraday and fell below $76,000. Ethereum fell over 3%.

Gold declined 0.72% to about $4,500. Spot silver fell 1.54%, and spot platinum dropped 2.13%. Crude oil initially fell 3.8% from its daily high but later recovered. WTI crude futures rose 0.26%, and Brent crude futures gained 0.94%.

In Asia, the ChiNext Index rose over 2%, with computing hardware surging, PCB and optical modules both gaining. The Hang Seng Tech Index rose over 2%, Lenovo jumped 20%, and Zhipu soared over 30%.

Key News

China

Eight Chinese departments including the CSRC announced a comprehensive crackdown on illegal cross-border securities, futures, and fund activities, setting a two-year concentrated rectification period. The CSRC plans to impose a total fine of 1.85 billion yuan on Futu, and Tiger Securities will be penalized approximately 410 million yuan.

Overseas

Trump said Iran is eager to reach an agreement, while Iran stated current negotiations do not involve nuclear issues and there are significant differences. The UAE and Saudi Arabia urgently urged Trump to avoid restarting the U.S.-Iran war.

Sworn in as Federal Reserve Chair! Warsh: The Fed will focus on reform, bringing unparalleled prosperity to the U.S. in the coming years. Trump said tell Warsh to act freely, expecting him to be a great Fed chair, hoping he remains fully independent.

Federal Reserve official Wheeler took a hawkish stance, stating that future rate hikes and cuts are “fifty-fifty,” with market expectations pointing to a rate hike by year-end. The "New Fed Whisperer": Trump chose Warsh for rate cuts, but the market has begun betting on rate hikes.

Report: Anthropic's valuation may exceed $900 billion, surpassing OpenAI, with a $30 billion funding round expected to close as early as next week. OpenAI "earns one, loses two," while Anthropic has started generating profits.

Single month absorbs 1.3 billion USD! SpaceX's IPO ignited Wall Street, with U.S. space-themed ETFs being heavily bought. SpaceX successfully launched Starship.

Microsoft canceled internal authorization for Claude Code due to high token billing costs.

Market Close

U.S. Equities: S&P 500 rose 0.37% to 7,473.47, with a weekly gain of 0.88%, marking the longest consecutive rise since 2023. The Dow rose 0.58% to 50,579.70, continuing to set a new closing high, with a weekly gain of 2.13%. Nasdaq rose 0.19% to 26,343.97, with a weekly gain of 0.45%.

A-shares: The Shanghai Composite closed at 4,112.90, up 0.87%. The Shenzhen Composite closed at 15,597.30, up 2.30%. The ChiNext Index closed at 3,938.50, up 2.84%.

Bond Market: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield fell 1.18 basis points to 4.5578%, with a weekly decline of 3.55 basis points. The two-year U.S. Treasury yield rose 3.79 basis points to 4.1210%, with a weekly increase of 5.22 basis points.

Commodities: Spot gold fell 0.76% to 4,508.32 USD per ounce, with a weekly decline of 0.70%. Spot silver fell 1.54% to 75.4955 USD per ounce, with a weekly decline of 0.66%. WTI June crude oil futures closed up 0.26% at 96.60 USD per barrel. Brent crude rose 0.94% to 103.54 USD per barrel.

Key News Details

Global Highlights

China

CSRC and eight departments announce comprehensive crackdown on illegal cross-border securities, futures, and fund activities, setting a two-year concentrated rectification period. After two years of concentrated rectification, all illegal cross-border operations by foreign institutions will be completely eliminated, with severe penalties for serious violations, creating a strong deterrent. Regarding the cleanup of illegal existing business, a two-year concentrated rectification period is set to clean up illegal existing business. During the concentrated rectification period, foreign institutions are prohibited from providing buying transactions and fund transfers for existing investors within China, allowing only one-way selling transactions and fund transfers.

CSRC: Intends to impose strict penalties on Tiger, Futu, and Changqiao. The CSRC announced that it intends to confiscate all illegal gains of Tiger, Futu, and Changqiao both domestically and overseas, and impose strict penalties due to their illegal cross-border operations. The State Council approved an eight-department joint plan to clean up illegal existing business during the two-year concentrated rectification period. Investor rights remain unaffected, and they can still conduct overseas investments through legitimate channels such as Hong Kong Stock Connect and QDII.

CSRC plans to impose fines totaling approximately 1.85 billion yuan on Futu, and Tiger Securities faces fines of approximately 410 million yuan. The CSRC plans to order relevant companies to correct or stop such behavior, confiscate illegal gains, and impose fines, with the total fines estimated at approximately 1.85 billion yuan (about 271 million USD). Additionally, the CSRC plans to impose individual fines of 1.25 million yuan (about 183,575 USD) on the company's founder and CEO Li Hua. Beijing CSRC imposed administrative fines totaling approximately 308.1 million yuan on Tiger Securities and confiscated approximately 103.1 million yuan in illegal gains.

Exit illegal cross-border stock trading, existing investors can sell within two years. The rectification plan sets a two-year transition period. During this period, existing investors can continue to log in to their accounts but can only perform selling operations and transfer funds, prohibiting buying transactions and fund inflows. After two years, foreign institutions will fully shut down domestic websites, trading software, and related services, and existing investors' accounts in China will no longer be able to trade, but will not be forcibly liquidated or closed.

Overseas

Trump says Iran wants to reach an agreement, Iran says current negotiations don't involve nuclear issues, and differences are significant. Trump said Iran wants to reach an agreement. A U.S. Senate military committee chairman stated that the U.S. military should destroy Iran's conventional military capabilities rather than seek an agreement. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei stated that the U.S.-Iran differences remain significant and it cannot expect results from several rounds of back-and-forth discussions within weeks or months; the current negotiations focus on ending the war, and nuclear-related topics will not be discussed at this stage.

The UAE and Saudi Arabia urgently urge Trump: Don't restart the U.S.-Iran war. The UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar jointly pressured Trump against restarting military action, with core concerns being the potential impact on the Strait of Hormuz and economic losses in the Gulf. The biggest change comes from the UAE—its shift from previously advocating a tough strike against Iran to actively mediating, due to the high economic costs already incurred from conflict. Although the three countries differ in the intensity of pressure on Iran, their common bottom line is clear: avoid a second round of military confrontation.

Saudi media reports获悉 U.S.-Iran agreement draft, including immediate, comprehensive, and unconditional ceasefire on all fronts. According to reports, the draft of the "near-achieved" agreement between the U.S. and Iran includes an immediate, comprehensive, and unconditional ceasefire on all fronts. The draft also mentions "negotiations on unresolved issues within seven days" and "gradual lifting of U.S. sanctions on Iran in exchange for compliance with the agreement."

U.S.-Iran peace talks have hit a 'dead end'? Four core obstacles are difficult to overcome. Since the ceasefire in April, U.S.-Iran negotiations have been stuck. Despite the "near-achieved" draft emerging, four core obstacles remain before the Strait of Hormuz control, uranium enrichment ownership, Lebanon front lines, and sanctions and asset release. Any progress or breakdown in this conflict affecting global markets will impact asset prices.

Sworn in as Federal Reserve Chair! Warsh: The Fed will focus on reform, bringing unprecedented prosperity to the U.S. in the coming years. Warsh was sworn in as the Federal Reserve Chair. He delivered a brief speech, saying it was "an honor to return to public service," and promised to lead a reform-oriented Fed, learning from past successes and mistakes, moving away from rigid frameworks and models while maintaining clear integrity and performance standards. Warsh emphasized the Fed's responsibility to "maintain price stability and achieve maximum employment." He also stated that the Fed's mission is "to maintain price stability and achieve maximum employment."

Trump: Tell Warsh to go ahead, expect him to be a great Fed chair, hope he remains fully independent. Trump said at the swearing-in ceremony, "I expect Warsh to be a great Fed chair, who will lead the Fed starting today, and I hope he remains fully independent, doing his job well. Don't look at me, don't look at anyone else, just go ahead and do your job well. He will defend the Fed's integrity. He understands that when the economy thrives, that's good." Trump said after the U.S. stock market closed on Friday, "Now I have a great Fed chair, Warsh, and we will quickly lower interest rates."

Federal Reserve official Wheeler takes a hawkish stance, stating that future rate hikes and cuts are "fifty-fifty," with market expectations pointing to a rate hike by year-end. Federal Reserve official Wheeler clearly stated that for the Fed's next interest rate move, the probability of a rate hike is equal to that of a cut. If inflation does not slow down soon, he would not rule out the possibility of future rate hikes; he also stated he would support removing the "easy bias" language from the policy statement. Wheeler warned that if inflation expectations lose their anchor, he would not hesitate to support a rate hike. After Wheeler's comments, the swap market first fully priced in the expectation of a 25-basis-point rate hike by the Fed before December.

The "New Fed Whisperer": Trump chose Warsh for rate cuts, but the market has begun betting on rate hikes. In the context of rising energy prices due to the Iran conflict, AI-driven demand growth, and ongoing inflation, market expectations have rapidly reversed, beginning to bet on the Fed's next move likely being a rate hike rather than a cut. Bond yields continue to rise, reflecting the market's reassessment of a "high-interest-rate新常态." Warsh's biggest challenge after taking office is not only to manage inflationary pressures but also to establish his own credibility between Trump's political influence and the Fed's independence.

Report: Anthropic's valuation may exceed $90 billion, surpassing OpenAI, with a $3 billion funding round expected to close as early as next week. Sequoia Capital, Dragoneer Investment Group, Altimeter Capital, and Greenoaks Capital Partners are expected to lead the round, with each party planning to invest approximately $2 billion. Peter Thiel's Founders Fund and General Catalyst, among other existing investors, also plan to participate.

OpenAI "earns one, loses two," while Anthropic has started making money. The divergence stems from customer structure: Anthropic generates about 85% of its revenue from enterprise customers, with a healthier model; OpenAI generates about 85% of its revenue from consumer subscriptions, with a low conversion rate from 90 million weekly active users, leading to structural losses.

Single month absorbs 1.3 billion USD! SpaceX's IPO ignites Wall Street, with U.S. space-themed ETFs being heavily bought. The SpaceX IPO is expected to ignite a space investment boom, with U.S. space-themed ETFs absorbing 1.3 billion USD in the past month, increasing the fund size to 3.3 billion USD, with six new products launching in quick succession. Rocket Lab and other概念股提前 surged, but the fund holding overlap rate exceeds 50%, analysts warn that pursuing the SpaceX narrative carries risks of homogeneity and overvaluation.

Microsoft cancels internal authorization for Claude Code due to high token billing costs. Despite Microsoft's heavy investment in OpenAI and providing cloud resources to Anthropic, the real bill for usage led to a decision to "cut ties." Behind this decision, both the AI usage cost far exceeding expectations and the fact that Claude Code is eroding its own product GitHub Copilot's market share played a role.

Research Highlights

Reverse selling signal! BofA: U.S. equity market shows typical signs of peak enthusiasm. BofA's Bull-Bear indicator rose to 8.0 this week, triggering a reverse selling signal. The report indicates that the U.S. equity market exhibits characteristics of a bubble, with strong price performance, retail enthusiasm, and low volatility. The market concentration represented by the top ten AI stocks has exceeded multiple historical bubble periods. Fund flows show that tech stocks attracted 9 billion USD in a single week, with BofA private clients' stock allocation reaching a historical high. Historical data shows that after the selling signal is triggered, global stock markets face short-term pressure for a correction.

"Roaring Twenties" returning! BofA's Hartnett warns: SpaceX's super IPO will trigger a historic bubble. BofA strategist Hartnett warns that super IPOs like SpaceX and OpenAI could push the technology sector's weight beyond 48%, surpassing the market concentration levels of previous major bubbles such as the 1920s "Roaring Twenties," 1970s "Nifty Fifty," 1980s Japanese bubble, and 1990s dot-com bubble. Historical experience shows that super IPOs are not necessarily catalysts but may become the peak of the bubble.

UBS's 100-page deep report: China's chemical industry is standing at the beginning of a new cycle. 2026 may mark the start of a new cycle for China's chemical industry. UBS points out that slowing capital spending, strict policies on new capacity, and the exit of high-cost overseas capacity are driving the industry from the profit bottom in 2025 into a recovery phase. Rising oil prices due to the Middle East situation have also strengthened the advantages of low-cost routes such as coal-based olefins and light hydrocarbon cracking. The current sector valuation and holdings are still low, with the focus of funds shifting toward enterprises with global competitiveness, scale effects, and cost moats, with segments such as polyurethane, agrochemicals, and refrigerants showing strong elasticity.

Morgan Stanley's重磅 report: From silicon to glass, from GPU to optical communication, AI is reshaping the entire semiconductor supply chain! AI computing power is forcing a reconfiguration of semiconductor processes, with growth logic shifting from simple transistor scaling to 3D transistors, backside power delivery, and combinations of new materials. Starting from 2027, advanced packaging, lithography materials, photonic SOI, and glass substrates will enter a volume production phase, driving a revaluation of the entire supply chain. TSMC's expansion and localization procurement will become the core driver of order transmission, and the semiconductor manufacturing industry is entering a synchronized upgrade cycle in structure, packaging, and materials.

Domestic Macro

Minister Wang Wentao meets with U.S. Deputy Trade Representative Sweetser. Both sides exchanged views on Sino-U.S. economic and trade relations. Wang Wentao stated that the Chinese side is willing to work with the U.S. side to strengthen communication, expand cooperation, and add value in economic and trade outcomes, contributing more to a constructive strategic stability relationship. Sweetser stated that the U.S. side is willing to implement the consensus of the two heads of state, leverage the U.S.-China government-to-government trade council, enhance dialogue, manage differences, and maintain the sustained and stable development of bilateral economic and trade relations.

Regarding the "six networks", artificial intelligence, and embodied intelligence, the National Development and Reform Commission provides the latest response. At the May news conference, the National Development and Reform Commission revealed that it will use macroeconomic policies to stabilize employment, enterprises, the market, and expectations. During the 15th Five-Year Plan period, it plans to invest over 5 trillion yuan to build new power grids and about 5 trillion yuan to renovate underground pipelines, accelerating the coordinated construction of the "six networks." At the same time, it is planning to issue supporting documents to accelerate the implementation of "artificial intelligence +" and conduct research on artificial intelligence legislation; using key infrastructure construction as a lever, comprehensively promoting the high-quality development of embodied intelligence.

Domestic Companies

Lenovo reported annual revenue of 590 billion yuan, with all three business segments achieving double-digit growth, and the stock price rose 13% to a record high in 26 years. Lenovo Group released its best performance in fiscal year 2026, with total revenue growing 20% to 589.9 billion yuan, and adjusted net profit attributable to shareholders increased 42%. AI-related revenue doubled annually, accounting for 33% of total revenue. All three business groups achieved profitability: Smart Devices revenue reached 418.5 billion yuan, up 17%; Infrastructure revenue reached 136.2 billion yuan, up 32% and turned profitable; Solution Services revenue reached 71 billion yuan, up 19% and reached a new high.

  • Three engines all ignited, the structural turning point behind Lenovo's 83.1 billion USD revenue. Lenovo Group's FY25/26 full-year revenue reached 83.1 billion USD, setting a new record. AI-related revenue doubled year-on-year, and the infrastructure business, previously seen as a "profit burden," achieved profitability for the first time in the full year. The fourth quarter saw all lines significantly exceeding expectations, with the Hong Kong stock market rising over 13% and the stock price hitting a new high since March 2000. What is most worth noting about this report is not how beautiful a number is, but that all three business groups achieved profitability for the first time in history.

Overseas Macro

Over 900 billion USD in pressure is coming! The largest IPO in U.S. history is coming, but Mag7 is in danger. SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic are preparing for IPOs, combined with NASDAQ's "fast index inclusion" mechanism, which allows SpaceX to be included in the index after 15 days of listing, potentially causing unprecedented capital shifts. Morgan Stanley estimates that passive funds will have to sell approximately 95 billion USD of existing tech stock holdings on Wall Street to make room, affecting areas overlapping with "Mag7".

Highi Haruna urges the Bank of Japan: hopes for "appropriate policy". Bank of Japan Governor Hashimoto stated that Prime Minister Highi Haruna expressed in a routine meeting her hope that the central bank would combine government price measures with appropriate monetary policy, without discussing specific policy details. Analysts believe that this meeting may intensify two market expectations: Hashimoto is laying the groundwork for a rate hike, or Highi hopes to delay action. This adds uncertainty to the June interest rate decision.

Excluding Samsung and SK Hynix, the KOSPI dynamic P/E ratio is 12 times! UBS: valuations are reasonable, optimistic about KOSPI. UBS raised its KOSPI target price by 26% to 9,200 points. The firm calculated that excluding Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, the KOSPI dynamic P/E ratio is 12 times, considering valuations reasonable because non-tech sectors are expected to grow 68% in 2026, and the overall EPS growth of the index is predicted at 258%, with the breadth of earnings improvement exceeding expectations. Although foreign investors have net outflows of 58 billion USD since the beginning of the year, retail investors and local institutions have continued to make net purchases.

Indonesia's aggressive rate hike: Southeast Asian central banks are shifting hawkishly. Indonesia's central bank suddenly implemented a 50-basis-point rate hike, shocking the market - this is the largest single increase since 2022, far exceeding economists' expectations. The Indonesian rupiah has fallen 5.5% year-to-date, the stock market has plummeted 29%, and sovereign credit ratings outlook has been downgraded, prompting the central bank to reclaim its independence. This rate hike storm is sweeping across Southeast Asia, with the Philippines and Singapore following suit, and a regional currency defense battle has fully erupted.

Indonesia's commodity restrictions cause panic, palm oil spot prices fall over 30% in two days. President Prabowo of Indonesia announced that state-owned enterprises will monopolize the export of commodities such as palm oil and coal. The policy shock immediately hit - Indonesia's palm oil spot prices fell more than 30% in two days, and listed palm oil stocks on the London market fell 20% in a single day. Buyers are观望, sellers are panicking and selling, and the market is in chaos.

After three years of fueling the AI revolution, OpenAI is "forced" to go public. Altman brought ChatGPT into the world, sparking this AI revolution. raw.title: Bloomberg Daily Brief | May 23, 2026
raw.summary: Five minutes to understand global markets, all in the financial breakfast.
raw.content:
Early Morning Voice

Market Overview

AI tech stocks lifted U.S. equities, with the S&P 500 up 0.37%, extending its eight-week consecutive rise, marking the longest streak since 2023. The Dow rose 0.58% and continued to hit new highs.

NVIDIA fell 1.9%, with a weekly decline of 4.4%. The tech seven giants underperformed the broader market, while utilities outperformed tech, and energy and materials lagged. Qualcomm surged over 11%. Strong performance from Lenovo Group boosted U.S. computer manufacturers, with Dell Technologies rising 17% to a new high and HP up 15%. U.S. quantum computing stocks surged again. Estee Lauder rose 12% after terminating potential merger talks with Puig.

Federal Reserve official Waller's hawkish remarks pressured U.S. Treasuries, pushing the two-year Treasury yield up 4 basis points to a two-month high.

The dollar remained stable around 99.2. Bitcoin dropped over 2% intraday and fell below $76,000. Ethereum fell over 3%.

Gold declined 0.72% to about $4,500. Spot silver fell 1.54%, and spot platinum dropped 2.13%. Crude oil initially fell 3.8% from its daily high but later recovered. WTI crude futures rose 0.26%, and Brent crude futures gained 0.94%.

In Asia, the ChiNext Index rose over 2%, with computing hardware surging, PCB and optical modules both gaining. The Hang Seng Tech Index rose over 2%, Lenovo jumped 20%, and Zhipu soared over 30%.

Key News

China

Eight Chinese departments including the CSRC announced a comprehensive crackdown on illegal cross-border securities, futures, and fund activities, setting a two-year concentrated rectification period. The CSRC plans to impose a total fine of 1.85 billion yuan on Futu, and Tiger Securities will be penalized approximately 410 million yuan.

Overseas

Trump said Iran is eager to reach an agreement, while Iran stated current negotiations do not involve nuclear issues and there are significant differences. The UAE and Saudi Arabia urgently urged Trump to avoid restarting the U.S.-Iran war.

Sworn in as Federal Reserve Chair! Warsh: The Fed will focus on reform, bringing unparalleled prosperity to the U.S. in the coming years. Trump said tell Warsh to act freely, expecting him to be a great Fed chair, hoping he remains fully independent.

Federal Reserve official Wheeler took a hawkish stance, stating that future rate hikes and cuts are “fifty-fifty,” with market expectations pointing to a rate hike by year-end. The "New Fed Whisperer": Trump chose Warsh for rate cuts, but the market has begun betting on rate hikes.

Report: Anthropic's valuation may exceed $900 billion, surpassing OpenAI, with a $30 billion funding round expected to close as early as next week. OpenAI "earns one, loses two," while Anthropic has started generating profits.

Single month absorbs 1.3 billion USD! SpaceX's IPO ignited Wall Street, with U.S. space-themed ETFs being heavily bought. SpaceX successfully launched Starship.

Microsoft canceled internal authorization for Claude Code due to high token billing costs.

Market Close

U.S. Equities: S&P 500 rose 0.37% to 7,473.47, with a weekly gain of 0.88%, marking the longest consecutive rise since 2023. The Dow rose 0.58% to 50,579.70, continuing to set a new closing high, with a weekly gain of 2.13%. Nasdaq rose 0.19% to 26,343.97, with a weekly gain of 0.45%.

A-shares: The Shanghai Composite closed at 4,112.90, up 0.87%. The Shenzhen Composite closed at 15,597.30, up 2.30%. The ChiNext Index closed at 3,938.50, up 2.84%.

Bond Market: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield fell 1.18 basis points to 4.5578%, with a weekly decline of 3.55 basis points. The two-year U.S. Treasury yield rose 3.79 basis points to 4.1210%, with a weekly increase of 5.22 basis points.

Commodities: Spot gold fell 0.76% to 4,508.32 USD per ounce, with a weekly decline of 0.70%. Spot silver fell 1.54% to 75.4955 USD per ounce, with a weekly decline of 0.66%. WTI June crude oil futures closed up 0.26% at 96.60 USD per barrel. Brent crude rose 0.94% to 103.54 USD per barrel.

Key News Details

Global Highlights

China

CSRC and eight departments announce comprehensive crackdown on illegal cross-border securities, futures, and fund activities, setting a two-year concentrated rectification period. After two years of concentrated rectification, all illegal cross-border operations by foreign institutions will be completely eliminated, with severe penalties for serious violations, creating a strong deterrent. Regarding the cleanup of illegal existing business, a two-year concentrated rectification period is set to clean up illegal existing business. During the concentrated rectification period, foreign institutions are prohibited from providing buying transactions and fund transfers for existing investors within China, allowing only one-way selling transactions and fund transfers.

CSRC: Intends to impose strict penalties on Tiger, Futu, and Changqiao. The CSRC announced that it intends to confiscate all illegal gains of Tiger, Futu, and Changqiao both domestically and overseas, and impose strict penalties due to their illegal cross-border operations. The State Council approved an eight-department joint plan to clean up illegal existing business during the two-year concentrated rectification period. Investor rights remain unaffected, and they can still conduct overseas investments through legitimate channels such as Hong Kong Stock Connect and QDII.

CSRC plans to impose fines totaling approximately 1.85 billion yuan on Futu, and Tiger Securities faces fines of approximately 410 million yuan. The CSRC plans to order relevant companies to correct or stop such behavior, confiscate illegal gains, and impose fines, with the total fines estimated at approximately 1.85 billion yuan (about 271 million USD). Additionally, the CSRC plans to impose individual fines of 1.25 million yuan (about 183,575 USD) on the company's founder and CEO Li Hua. Beijing CSRC imposed administrative fines totaling approximately 308.1 million yuan on Tiger Securities and confiscated approximately 103.1 million yuan in illegal gains.

Exit illegal cross-border stock trading, existing investors can sell within two years. The rectification plan sets a two-year transition period. During this period, existing investors can continue to log in to their accounts but can only perform selling operations and transfer funds, prohibiting buying transactions and fund inflows. After two years, foreign institutions will fully shut down domestic websites, trading software, and related services, and existing investors' accounts in China will no longer be able to trade, but will not be forcibly liquidated or closed.

Overseas

Trump says Iran wants to reach an agreement, Iran says current negotiations don't involve nuclear issues, and differences are significant. Trump said Iran wants to reach an agreement. A U.S. Senate military committee chairman stated that the U.S. military should destroy Iran's conventional military capabilities rather than seek an agreement. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei stated that the U.S.-Iran differences remain significant and it cannot expect results from several rounds of back-and-forth discussions within weeks or months; the current negotiations focus on ending the war, and nuclear-related topics will not be discussed at this stage.

The UAE and Saudi Arabia urgently urge Trump: Don't restart the U.S.-Iran war. The UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar jointly pressured Trump against restarting military action, with core concerns being the potential impact on the Strait of Hormuz and economic losses in the Gulf. The biggest change comes from the UAE—its shift from previously advocating a tough strike against Iran to actively mediating, due to the high economic costs already incurred from conflict. Although the three countries differ in the intensity of pressure on Iran, their common bottom line is clear: avoid a second round of military confrontation.

Saudi media reports获悉 U.S.-Iran agreement draft, including immediate, comprehensive, and unconditional ceasefire on all fronts. According to reports, the draft of the "near-achieved" agreement between the U.S. and Iran includes an immediate, comprehensive, and unconditional ceasefire on all fronts. The draft also mentions "negotiations on unresolved issues within seven days" and "gradual lifting of U.S. sanctions on Iran in exchange for compliance with the agreement."

U.S.-Iran peace talks have hit a 'dead end'? Four core obstacles are difficult to overcome. Since the ceasefire in April, U.S.-Iran negotiations have been stuck. Despite the "near-achieved" draft emerging, four core obstacles remain before the Strait of Hormuz control, uranium enrichment ownership, Lebanon front lines, and sanctions and asset release. Any progress or breakdown in this conflict affecting global markets will impact asset prices.

Sworn in as Federal Reserve Chair! Warsh: The Fed will focus on reform, bringing unprecedented prosperity to the U.S. in the coming years. Warsh was sworn in as the Federal Reserve Chair. He delivered a brief speech, saying it was "an honor to return to public service," and promised to lead a reform-oriented Fed, learning from past successes and mistakes, moving away from rigid frameworks and models while maintaining clear integrity and performance standards. Warsh emphasized the Fed's responsibility to "maintain price stability and achieve maximum employment." He also stated that the Fed's mission is "to maintain price stability and achieve maximum employment."

Trump: Tell Warsh to go ahead, expect him to be a great Fed chair, hope he remains fully independent. Trump said at the swearing-in ceremony, "I expect Warsh to be a great Fed chair, who will lead the Fed starting today, and I hope he remains fully independent, doing his job well. Don't look at me, don't look at anyone else, just go ahead and do your job well. He will defend the Fed's integrity. He understands that when the economy thrives, that's good." Trump said after the U.S. stock market closed on Friday, "Now I have a great Fed chair, Warsh, and we will quickly lower interest rates."

Federal Reserve official Wheeler clearly stated that for the Fed's next interest rate move, the probability of a rate hike is equal to that of a cut. If inflation does not slow down soon, he would not rule out the possibility of future rate hikes; he also stated he would support removing the "easy bias" language from the policy statement. Wheeler warned that if inflation expectations lose their anchor, he would not hesitate to support a rate hike. After Wheeler's comments, the swap market first fully priced in the expectation of a 25-basis-point rate hike by the Fed before December.

The "New Fed Whisperer": Trump chose Warsh for rate cuts, but the market has begun betting on rate hikes. In the context of rising energy prices due to the Iran conflict, AI-driven demand growth, and ongoing inflation, market expectations have rapidly reversed, beginning to bet on the Fed's next move likely being a rate hike rather than a cut. Bond yields continue to rise, reflecting the market's reassessment of a "high-interest-rate新常态." Warsh's biggest challenge after taking office is not only to manage inflationary pressures but also to establish his own credibility between Trump's political influence and the Fed's independence.

Report: Anthropic's valuation may exceed $90 billion, surpassing OpenAI, with a $3 billion funding round expected to close as early as next week. Sequoia Capital, Dragoneer Investment Group, Altimeter Capital, and Greenoaks Capital Partners are expected to lead the round, with each party planning to invest approximately $2 billion. Peter Thiel's Founders Fund and General Catalyst, among other existing investors, also plan to participate.

OpenAI "earns one, loses two," while Anthropic has started making money. The market concentration represented by the top ten AI stocks has exceeded multiple historical bubble periods. Fund flows show that tech stocks attracted 9 billion USD in a single week, with BofA private clients' stock allocation reaching a historical high. Historical data shows that after the selling signal is triggered, global stock markets face short-term pressure for a correction.

"Roaring Twenties" returning! BofA's Hartnett warns: SpaceX's super IPO will trigger a historic bubble. BofA strategist Hartnett warns that super IPOs like SpaceX and OpenAI could push the technology sector's weight beyond 48%, surpassing the market concentration levels of previous major bubbles such as the 1920s "Roaring Twenties," 1970s "Nifty Fifty," 1980s Japanese bubble, and 1990s dot-com bubble. Historical experience shows that super IPOs are not necessarily catalysts but may become the peak of the bubble.

UBS's 100-page deep report: China's chemical industry is standing at the beginning of a new cycle. 2026 may mark the start of a new cycle for China's chemical industry. Rising oil prices due to the Middle East situation have also strengthened the advantages of low-cost routes such as coal-based olefins and light hydrocarbon cracking. The current sector valuation and holdings are still low, with the focus of funds shifting toward enterprises with global competitiveness, scale effects, and cost moats, with segments such as polyurethane, agrochemicals, and refrigerants showing strong elasticity.

AI computing power is forcing a reconfiguration of semiconductor processes, with growth logic shifting from simple transistor scaling to 3D transistors, backside power delivery, and combinations of new materials. Starting from 2027, advanced packaging, lithography materials, photonic SOI, and glass substrates will enter a volume production phase, driving a revaluation of the entire supply chain. TSMC's expansion and localization procurement will become the core driver of order transmission, and the semiconductor manufacturing industry is entering a synchronized upgrade cycle in structure, packaging, and materials.

Minister Wang Wentao meets with U.S. Deputy Trade Representative Sweetser. Both sides exchanged views on Sino-U.S. economic and trade relations. Wang Wentao stated that the Chinese side is willing to work with the U.S. side to strengthen communication, expand cooperation, and add value in economic and trade outcomes, contributing more to a constructive strategic stability relationship. Sweetser stated that the U.S. side is willing to implement the consensus of the two heads of state, leverage the U.S.-China government-to-government trade council, enhance dialogue, manage differences, and maintain the sustained and stable development of bilateral economic and trade relations.

Regarding the "six networks", artificial intelligence, and embodied intelligence, the National Development and Reform Commission provides the latest response. At the May news conference, the National Development and Reform Commission revealed that it will use macroeconomic policies to stabilize employment, enterprises, the market, and expectations. During the 15th Five-Year Plan period, it plans to invest over 5 trillion yuan to build new power grids and about 5 trillion yuan to renovate underground pipelines, accelerating the coordinated construction of the "six networks." At the same time, it is planning to issue supporting documents to accelerate the implementation of "artificial intelligence +" and conduct research on artificial intelligence legislation; using key infrastructure construction as a lever, comprehensively promoting the high-quality development of embodied intelligence.

AI-related revenue doubled annually, accounting for 33% of total revenue. All three business groups achieved profitability: Smart Devices revenue reached 418.5 billion yuan, up 17%; Infrastructure revenue reached 136.2 billion yuan, up 32% and turned profitable; Solution Services revenue reached 71 billion yuan, up 19% and reached a new high.

What is most worth noting about this report is not how beautiful a number is, but that all three business groups achieved profitability for the first time in history.

SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic are preparing for IPOs, combined with NASDAQ's "fast index inclusion" mechanism, which allows SpaceX to be included in the index after 15 days of listing, potentially causing unprecedented capital shifts. Morgan Stanley estimates that passive funds will have to sell approximately 95 billion USD of existing tech stock holdings on Wall Street to make room, affecting areas overlapping with "Mag7".

This adds uncertainty to the June interest rate decision.

title: Trump Says Iran Aims for Agreement, Iran Says Current Talks Not Involving Nuclear Issues, Major Disputes Remain
summary: Trump stated that Iran is eager to reach an agreement. The chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee said that US forces should complete the destruction of Iran's conventional military capabilities rather than seek an agreement. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei stated that the differences between the US and Iran remain serious, and it is not expected that results could be seen within weeks or months through a few rounds of negotiations; the current talks focus on promoting the end of the war, and nuclear issues are not discussed at this stage.
content:
Uncertainties surrounding the Iran-US nuclear talks resurfaced, with Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei clearly stating that the differences between the two sides are 'deep and extensive,' and the current negotiations do not involve nuclear issues, focusing only on ending the war.

On Friday, May 22, according to Xinhua News Agency, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei stated that it is currently impossible to assert that an agreement between Iran and the US is close to being reached, and the differences between the two sides remain serious. It is not expected that results could be seen within weeks or months through a few rounds of back-and-forth negotiations. He emphasized that diplomatic negotiations are a long process, and both sides are using various opportunities to convey their positions.

According to CCTV News, Baghaei emphasized that the current focus of the negotiations is to promote the end of the war, and topics related to nuclear issues will not be discussed at this stage. He stated that issues such as 'ending all fronts of the war, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, and ending the US' maritime 'plundering activities' remain the core content of the negotiations.

On the US side: According to reports, Trump stated that Iran is eager to reach an agreement, and we will see. Roger Wicker, chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee and a Republican senator, stated that US forces should 'complete the destruction of Iran's conventional military capabilities and reopen the strait.' President Trump is being influenced by 'bad advice' to seek a worthless agreement.

Earlier that day, according to media reports, Iran's negotiations had reached an understanding on the general framework of nuclear issues, with arrangements for Iran to transfer (or hand over) uranium materials linked to sanctions relief, and the process would be gradual. This news briefly pushed oil prices down, but later rebounded as Iran's Foreign Ministry denied the report.

Iran's Foreign Ministry Spokesperson: Major Disputes Remain Between Iran and the US, Current Talks Not Involving Nuclear Issues

According to Xinhua News Agency and CCTV News, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei stated that the visit of Pakistan's Chief of Army Staff Munir to Iran is a continuation of the current diplomatic process, which does not mean the situation has entered a decisive phase, nor does it indicate that Iran and the US are close to reaching an agreement. The differences between Iran and the US are 'deep and extensive,' and it is unlikely that final results could be achieved through a few rounds of back-and-forth negotiations or a few weeks of talks.

Baghaei also stated that the current focus of the negotiations is to promote the end of the war, and topics related to nuclear issues will not be discussed at this stage. Iran's current priority is to end the war, and it first needs to achieve a ceasefire under a framework that safeguards Iran's concerns and interests. Whether other issues will be discussed in the next phase is a matter for the future.

Regarding the nuclear issue, Baghaei reiterated that Iran is a party to the Non-Proliferation Treaty and has the right to use nuclear energy for peaceful purposes.

The Qatari delegation visited Iran that day and held talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Zarif. On the evening of May 22, Pakistan's Chief of Army Staff Munir arrived in Tehran, the capital of Iran.

title: Kevin Warsh Sworn in as Federal Reserve Chair: Emphasizes Reform and Unprecedented Prosperity for the US
summary: Kevin Warsh was sworn in as the new Federal Reserve Chair on Friday. In a brief speech, he described it as 'a lifelong honor to be recalled to public service,' and stated that he would lead a Fed focused on reform, learning from past successes and failures while breaking free from rigid frameworks and models. Warsh emphasized that the Fed should fulfill its mandate of controlling inflation and achieving full employment with 'independence, clear judgment, and firm resolve.' He also reiterated the Fed's mission to 'maintain price stability and achieve maximum employment.'
content:
Kevin Warsh was sworn in as the Federal Reserve Chair on Friday, at a critical moment for monetary policy and the U.S. economy. His broad criticism of current Fed officials, his approach to rate cuts, and his relationship with President Trump helped him stand out among competitors in the race to lead the Fed.

Warsh, dressed in a dark suit and tie, was accompanied by his wife, Jane Lauder, an heir to the Estee Lauder fortune, as he took the oath administered by Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas. The event was preceded by a long introduction by Trump, with high-ranking officials from the administration, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, and several of Warsh's old friends, such as former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, in attendance.

Trump, who has consistently criticized former Fed Chair Jerome Powell, said Warsh would receive 'full support from my administration' and hoped he would act independently in his new role, while also urging him to recognize that 'growth does not mean inflation.'

Warsh then delivered a brief speech, calling it 'a lifelong honor to be recalled to public service,' and said, 'To fulfill this mission, I will lead a Fed focused on reform, drawing lessons from past successes and failures, while breaking free from rigid frameworks and models, yet upholding clear standards of integrity and performance.'

Warsh emphasized that the Fed should fulfill its responsibility to control inflation and achieve full employment with 'independence, clear judgment, and firm resolve.' He also stated that the Fed's mission is 'to maintain price stability and achieve maximum employment.'

The challenges facing Warsh include an ongoing technological revolution in artificial intelligence. Fed officials say this wave is reshaping the economy, with potentially deep impacts on workers, businesses, and consumers, but Warsh and his colleagues will find it difficult to assess in real time. At the same time, inflation remains elevated and could rise further as the U.S. economy deals with multiple shocks, including the war between the U.S. and Israel with Iran pushing oil prices above $100 per barrel, high import tariffs, and increased utility and other costs due to AI adoption.

Debates over Fed policy have reached a fever pitch. Christopher Waller, a Fed governor appointed by Trump and who had interviewed Warsh for the position, made a significant shift in his views on Friday, aligning with a group of dissenting officials who argue the Fed should abandon its 'relaxed bias' in its outlook and leave the door open for potential rate hikes.

Given recent data showing inflation is spreading and intensifying across the economy, Waller said shortly before Warsh's swearing-in that the Fed should clearly indicate that the likelihood of rate cuts is not greater than that of rate hikes. These comments intensified market sentiment toward tighter monetary policy and the possibility of rate hikes this year.

At 56 years old, Warsh won Trump's support after a year-long public 'audition' among top candidates. During this period, the new chairman proposed ambitious reform goals for the Fed, arguing that when he left his post in 2011 over his opposition to Fed bond purchases, the central bank had already begun to lose its way. However, his first few months in office may be dominated by a more urgent dilemma: whether to raise rates to prevent inflation from moving further away from the Fed's 2% target or risk his credibility as an inflation fighter from the start.

Warsh previously told Senate confirmation hearings that inflation is a choice for the Fed. The central bank's control over short-term interest rates is a lever that can be used to boost or curb spending, aiming to keep inflation at its target level. The Fed has failed to meet its goal for more than five years, with current inflation levels more than one percentage point above its target.

How to bring inflation down may involve difficult decisions that sometimes conflict with the Trump administration's policies and goals and at other times contradict the Fed's other objective of full employment. As the 11th Fed chair, Warsh will have to balance competing pressures from the start of his term: on one hand, global bond markets are already pushing up rates, reflecting growing inflation concerns; on the other hand, colleagues like Waller are beginning to create expectations for potential rate hikes; and there is also Trump, who has long viewed rate hikes as a political attack on his economic plans and has sharply criticized Powell for not lowering borrowing costs.

Warsh's statements and handling of ongoing controversies surrounding the Fed, including the upcoming Supreme Court ruling on Trump's unsuccessful attempt to remove Fed Governor Lisa Cook, will be closely watched and compared to Powell's steadfast defense of the Fed's independence.

The Fed's next meeting is scheduled for June 16-17, when policymakers will vote on interest rates and a new policy statement and submit updated economic projections.

One of Warsh's earliest substantive decisions will be whether to submit a 'dot'—the level he believes interest rates will be by year-end. This move will reveal whether his views are significantly different from those of his colleagues whom he has previously criticized for groupthink, or whether he will become a lone voice, potentially further disrupting markets already pushing up long-term U.S. rates.

The Fed's monetary policy decisions affect a range of consumer-facing and politically sensitive rates, such as mortgage rates; and its choices on inflation are being made against the backdrop of rising prices, such as $4.50 per gallon for gasoline, which are beyond its direct control.

These developments serve as a stark reminder of Trump's lack of progress on a key presidential promise—that he would 'end inflation and make America affordable from day one'—a responsibility now falling on Warsh.

title: Trump: Tell Wash to Go Ahead, Expects Him to Be a Great Fed Chairman, Hopes He Remains Fully Independent
summary: At the swearing-in ceremony, Trump stated, 'I expect Wash to be a great Federal Reserve chairman. He will lead the Fed starting today. No one is more suited to lead the Fed than Wash. His respect for the Fed is the deepest. I hope Kevin remains fully independent. I hope he acts independently and does his job well. Don't look at me, don't look at anyone, just go ahead and do your job well. He will defend the integrity of the Fed. He understands that when the economy is booming, it's a good thing.'
content:
On Friday, U.S. President Trump emphasized that he hopes Kevin Wash would lead the Federal Reserve independently, aiming to ease investors' concerns. Market participants worried that Trump might pressure the new Fed head on policy decisions.

Wash promised to carry out the largest restructuring of the Federal Reserve in decades. On Friday, he was sworn in as the 17th chairman of the Federal Reserve at a ceremony held at the White House.

At the swearing-in ceremony, Trump said:

I expect Wash to be a great Federal Reserve chairman. Wash will lead the Fed starting today. No one is more suitable to lead the Fed than Wash. His respect for the Fed is the deepest.

I hope Kevin remains fully independent. I hope he acts independently and does his job well. Don't look at me, don't look at anyone, just go ahead and do your job well.

Kevin will defend the integrity of the Fed. They will make their own decisions and hope they do well, but they will listen to Kevin throughout.

Wash took over the helm at a tense moment for the U.S. economy and the Federal Reserve. Recently, inflation pressures have accelerated again due to the impact of the Middle East war on energy supplies. The latest data released on Friday showed that consumer expectations for long-term inflation rose to the highest level in seven months, and investors now expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates before December.

Meanwhile, over the past year, the Federal Reserve has been criticized by Trump for not cutting rates quickly enough. During the ceremony, Trump criticized the Fed for being distracted by issues such as climate change and diversity initiatives, which he claimed were far from its core mission and responsibilities, but he did not comment on interest rate decisions.

The ongoing inflation and political pressures have raised concerns among investors and analysts about potential threats to the independence of the Federal Reserve. During the confirmation hearing for the Federal Reserve chair position, Wash repeatedly pledged to act independently, despite criticizing the Fed for what he called 'mission drift' and dissatisfaction with its approach to the surge in inflation during the pandemic.

Some of Trump's allies are eager to help Wash avoid repeating the mistakes of outgoing chairman Powell (Jerome Powell). Since Trump's first term, Powell has been one of his favorite targets. Officials sensitive to market volatility and aware of the importance of the Fed's independence for bond traders, such as U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Fox Business Channel's Larry Kudlow, have publicly expressed support for keeping interest rates unchanged temporarily for Wash.

Media sources indicated that similar messages have also been conveyed through private channels, and this effort may be working, at least for now.

Even though Trump expressed hope that Wash would remain independent, he subtly encouraged Wash not to interfere when the economy was expanding rapidly:

Different from some of his predecessors, Wash understands that when the economy is booming, it's a good thing. We don't need to overreact; let it boom. We hope it booms.

The Federal Reserve is the pillar of the global financial system.

Notable figures attending the ceremony highlighted the new Federal Reserve chairman's connections with the conservative movement.

One of the most right-leaning Supreme Court justices, Clarence Thomas, administered the oath of office to Wash. The Supreme Court is currently considering a case challenging Trump's attempt to remove Lisa Cook from her position as a Federal Reserve governor.

In his speech, Wash also mentioned his time working together with Brett Kavanaugh, a Supreme Court justice who was also present, in George W. Bush's White House. He told Trump, 'We feel incredibly honored and grateful to serve a country we love, and it is in your building, sir.'

Wash is not the first Federal Reserve chairman to take the oath in the presence of a sitting president. George W. Bush attended Ben Bernanke's swearing-in ceremony at the Federal Reserve headquarters in 2006, while Reagan presided over Alan Greenspan's swearing-in ceremony at the White House in 1987.

The U.S. Senate confirmed Wash as chairman in early May with a vote of 54 to 45. This was the closest vote in history for the confirmation of a Federal Reserve chairman, reflecting the partisan divisions in Congress and the concern of Democratic lawmakers that Wash might accept Trump's interest rate demands.

Wash is one of the wealthiest Federal Reserve officials. He has pledged to divest some of his assets before taking office. Documents released by the Office of Government Ethics earlier this week showed that he had sold most of his assets, but these documents did not indicate whether he had sold all of his holdings. It is currently unclear whether he has divested all of his assets.

Wash has promised a 'regime change' for the Federal Reserve, including reducing the central bank's $6.7 trillion balance sheet, establishing a new framework for analyzing inflation, and changing the way the institution communicates with the public.

After being sworn in, Wash said there was potential for unprecedented prosperity, raising living standards across all sectors of American society. He said:

Our responsibility at the Federal Reserve is to promote price stability and maximum employment. When we pursue these goals with wisdom, clarity, independence, and determination, inflation can be lower, growth stronger, and real incomes higher.

However, Wash will face an urgent challenge in policy-making. Before being nominated as chairman, Wash had argued that interest rates could be lower. However, under inflation concerns, Federal Reserve officials currently have little willingness to implement recent rate cuts - inflation accelerated at the fastest pace since 2023 in April.

The Federal Reserve policymakers left interest rates unchanged in the range of 3.5% to 3.75% last month. The minutes from that meeting showed that most officials warned that if inflation continued to exceed the 2% target, they might need to consider raising rates.

One of the most influential policymakers, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller, said on Friday that he now believes the likelihood of the Federal Reserve taking either a rate hike or cut is equal. The next Federal Open Market Committee meeting will be held in Washington on June 16-17.

Powell decided to remain on the Federal Reserve Board, breaking the tradition that chairmen typically leave the institution after completing their terms. His tenure as a governor will continue until January 2028.

Powell said that the continuous legal threats against him and the Federal Reserve left him no choice but to stay. Powell stated that he remained to support the Fed's independence from political interference, not to weaken his successor. The last chairman to remain on the board after leaving the chairmanship was Marriner Eccles, who served as a policymaker until 1951 after his Fed chairmanship ended in 1948.

The Trump administration's Department of Justice launched a criminal investigation into a $250 million renovation project at the Federal Reserve's Washington headquarters. This investigation once delayed Wash's confirmation, but it was dropped by federal prosecutor Jeanine Pirro.

On the same day, U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent, when asked about whether Wash would cut rates, said, 'He will do the right thing on inflation and growth.' Bessent made the statement after a swearing-in ceremony for Wash at the White House.

title: Zhang Kun Adds New Team Members, Yifangda Blue Chip Announces Additional Fund Managers
summary: The industry's largest active equity fund transitions to a team-based management model
content:
Another well-known fund manager has begun implementing a 'team-based' management model for their products.

On the night of May 22, Yifangda Fund announced that it had appointed He Yicheng and Yang Siliang as fund managers for the Yifangda Blue Chip Select Fund, who will jointly manage the fund with Zhang Kun.

As of the end of the first quarter of 2026, Yifangda Blue Chip Select Fund remained the largest single active equity fund in terms of scale, with a size of nearly 26.793 billion yuan. After this adjustment, Zhang Kun remains the fund manager with the largest management scale in the active equity fund sector.

Some analysts believe that introducing fund managers with different capability circles to jointly manage the fund can help the team leverage complementary strengths across multiple perspectives, thereby optimizing investors' investment experience.

Zhang Kun Still Manages Products Independently

After the recent change in fund managers for the Yifangda Blue Chip Select Fund, Zhang Kun still participates in the management of five funds.

Among them, he independently manages Yifangda High-Quality Selection (QDII), Yifangda High-Quality Enterprise Three-Year Period, and Yifangda Asia Select. He also manages Yifangda Blue Chip and Yifangda New Silk Road with a team.

According to data from TianTian Fund Network, the total scale of the portfolios he manages currently exceeds 41.6 billion yuan. However, 29.3 billion yuan of the public fund scale is now under team-based management.

Who Were Added?

To maximize the enhancement of investment strength, the fund managers added by Yifangda for the Blue Chip Select Fund have diverse styles, but all are among the most successful in the industry in recent years.

He Yicheng previously served as an assistant analyst at Shanghai Shenying Wanguo Securities Research Co., Ltd., and has long focused on the TMT sector, with a preference for technology growth stocks. He joined Yifangda Fund in August 2019 and became a fund manager in August 2024. He currently manages equity funds including Yifangda Growth Drive Fund and Yifangda New Normal Flexible Allocation Fund, with the latter achieving a return of over 260% in the past year.

Yang Siliang was recruited by Yifangda from Baoying Fund. After joining Yifangda in September 2025, he took over the Yifangda Long-Term Value Fund in March 2026. He has deep expertise in consumer and value investing styles, and is skilled at identifying investment opportunities in high-quality companies over long-term cycles.

Team-Based Management and Performance Turning Point

Recently, there has been a clear shift toward team-based management within the industry. Not long ago, large-scale products managed by Liu Yanchun also announced the addition of fund managers. Now, Zhang Kun has also added fund managers, reflecting the management's emphasis on team-based approaches.

Team-based management is a different approach from individual responsibility. In the former, the company typically assigns multiple fund managers to jointly manage a product, while the latter involves a single fund manager handling the investment operations alone.

During the bull market in the 6000-point era, the industry saw a surge in team-based management for ultra-large funds due to unprecedented fund sizes. The current trend, however, focuses on strengthening the performance of large funds that were heavily raised in 2021.

From this perspective, the future performance of these products deserves close attention.

title: HOKA's DTC Is Back on Track
summary: More Stores to Open
content:
HOKA's DTC is back on track.

For the fourth fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2026, HOKA's parent company Deckers reported revenue of $1.119 billion, a year-over-year increase of 9.6%. Full-year revenue for fiscal 2026 reached $5.47 billion, up 9.8% year-over-year.

HOKA remains the most important growth driver. In fiscal 2026, HOKA's revenue increased 15.9% to $2.587 billion; for the fourth quarter, revenue rose 14.5% to $671 million, setting a new single-quarter record for the brand.

Over the past few years, HOKA has rapidly expanded its reach by leveraging thick-soled running shoes, trail running, marathons, and outdoor lifestyle scenarios, establishing strong recognition between professional sports and everyday fashion.

However, as the brand grows in scale, market focus has shifted toward the resilience and quality of its growth: whether it can maintain demand热度, channel efficiency, and full-price selling capabilities at a larger scale.

DTC is a key indicator for measuring this.

In the first half of fiscal 2026, HOKA's DTC channel faced pressure. In the first quarter, global DTC sales grew only 3%, significantly lower than the 30% growth in wholesale sales during the same period; in the second quarter, DTC sales growth rebounded to 8%, still below the 13% growth in wholesale sales.

This was partly due to high base effects, as well as more cautious consumer sentiment in the U.S. and a shift in some demand toward multi-brand offline retail channels.

The situation changed in the second half of the year. Through direct-to-consumer websites, e-commerce platforms, membership systems, and running communities, brands can more directly collect consumer feedback, organize product release schedules, and reduce reliance on external channels and discount promotions.

Especially after running shoe consumption has become more specialized and segmented, how to retain runners, trail users, and lifestyle consumers within its own ecosystem directly affects HOKA's repurchase rate, average order value, and full-price selling capabilities.

Deckers is also accelerating the expansion of HOKA's direct stores. Management stated at the earnings call that they plan to open 20 to 25 HOKA-owned stores annually, focusing on major cities and international markets, and will continue to open stores in Asia, especially in China.

These stores are not just sales points but also serve as product displays, trial experiences, consumer relationship building, and online DTC conversion entry points.

Looking ahead to fiscal 2027, Deckers expects revenue to reach between $5.86 billion and $5.91 billion, with HOKA revenue achieving low double-digit growth and UGG revenue achieving mid-single-digit growth.

In particular, HOKA's DTC growth is expected to outpace wholesale, and international market growth is also expected to continue to exceed that of the U.S. domestic market.

Profitability requires caution. In fiscal 2026, Deckers' gross margin was 57.7%, down 20 basis points from the previous year. Management noted that this included approximately 80 basis points of tariff impact, but about 60 basis points of underlying gross margin expansion offset some pressure, mainly from product structure optimization and lower freight costs.

For fiscal 2027, the company's guidance for gross margin and operating profit margin is lower than in fiscal 2026. Gross margin guidance is approximately 56.5%, and operating profit margin is around 21.5%, below 23.1% in fiscal 2026.

Compared to the temporary fluctuations in the U.S. market, China remains one of the more promising regions for HOKA's international expansion.

Management stated that HOKA has expanded its premium brand presence in China and maintained strong full-price selling performance across existing stores, new retail locations, and partner channels, driving market share growth.

In international markets such as China, whether HOKA can consolidate core users through DTC, maintain pricing systems during wholesale expansion, and continue to deliver product and community value in the premium running shoe competition remains critical for the future.

title: U.S.-Iran Talks Stuck in a Dead End? Four Core Obstacles Remain Unresolved
summary: Since the ceasefire agreement in April, U.S.-Iran negotiations have remained stalled. Although a draft reportedly 'close to agreement' has emerged, four core issues—control of the Strait of Hormuz, ownership of enriched uranium, the Lebanon front, and sanctions and asset release—remain significant obstacles. This conflict affecting global markets could impact asset prices with any progress or breakdown in negotiations.
content:
Since the ceasefire agreement this year, U.S.-Iran negotiations have been stuck, with no comprehensive agreement reached on ending the conflict. A draft reportedly 'close to agreement' is emerging, but four core issues remain as major obstacles on the path to lasting peace.

Xinhua News Agency reported on May 22 citing Saudi Arabia TV that the U.S. and Iran are close to reaching an agreement. The draft includes immediate, comprehensive, and unconditional ceasefire across all fronts. It also includes commitments not to attack military, civilian, or infrastructure targets; to stop military actions and media campaigns; to respect sovereignty and territorial integrity and non-interference; to ensure freedom of navigation in the Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, and the Oman Sea; and to establish a joint monitoring and conflict resolution mechanism.

However, whether this framework will be implemented remains uncertain. According to Bloomberg, the control of the Strait of Hormuz, nuclear issues, the Lebanon conflict, and sanctions remain the four core points of contention in the talks. For investors, this war has already plunged the global energy market into turmoil, and any progress or breakdown in negotiations could impact commodity prices.

Strait of Hormuz: Global Energy Lifeline Becomes a Key Negotiation Point

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical artery for about one-fifth of global oil trade. After the war broke out, restricted passage directly pushed up energy prices and exacerbated global inflation. According to vessel data tracked by Bloomberg, commercial ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped to very low levels.

According to a report this Thursday, Iran is currently negotiating with Oman on establishing a permanent toll collection mechanism to formally secure its control over commercial maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

Subsequently, Trump stated that he is paying attention to the issue of tolls in the Strait of Hormuz. Trump reiterated that the U.S. fully controls the Strait of Hormuz, stating that the U.S. naval blockade against Iran is 100% effective. He also said that no ship can pass through Iran without U.S. approval.

Mohammad Amin-Nejad, Iran's ambassador to France, stated, the negotiations between Iran and Oman on establishing a permanent toll mechanism show Iran's unwillingness to easily give up control of the strait. The market is now worried that if the U.S.-Iran talks break down or military tensions escalate again, the Strait of Hormuz may once again become one of the biggest risk factors in the global energy market.

Nuclear Standoff: Ownership of Enriched Uranium Becomes the Biggest Dispute

The nuclear issue is the most complex topic in the negotiations.

The U.S. demands Iran abandon its nuclear capabilities, retaining only the Bushehr nuclear power plant to ensure it cannot produce nuclear weapons. Iran has long denied any intention to develop nuclear weapons and insists on its right to enrich uranium for civilian purposes.

Trump reiterated "we will not allow Iran to have nuclear weapons," and stated that the U.S. will eventually obtain Iran's enriched uranium. This statement contrasts sharply with Iran's position. Earlier on Thursday, according to Xinhua News Agency citing media reports, Iran's Supreme Leader has instructed that enriched uranium should not be exported from the country.

According to reports, two Iranian sources said: "The Supreme Leader's instructions and the consensus within the authorities are that enriched uranium stocks should not be sent out of Iran. Iranian senior officials believe that moving nuclear materials abroad would make Iran more vulnerable to attacks from the U.S. and Israel in the future."

Analysts point out that the U.S. has long sought to move high-enriched uranium out of Iran to reduce its ability to achieve a "weapon-grade breakthrough" in the short term; while Iran insists on retaining local control. Now, Trump's public declaration that "the U.S. will get enriched uranium" indicates that the differences between the two sides on key issues remain significant.

Lebanon Impasse: Diplomatic Mediation vs. On-the-Ground Fighting

The Lebanon front is another difficult issue in reaching an agreement.

Iran insists that any final peace agreement must also end Israel's military operations in Lebanon. According to China Central Television, on April 16, Iran's Islamic Parliament Speaker Qalibaf spoke with Lebanon's National Assembly Speaker Berri and said, "ceasefire in Lebanon is as important as ceasefire in Iran." Pakistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said on April 16 that Lebanon is part of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire negotiation process, and a calming of the situation in Lebanon would help advance the ceasefire negotiation process.

On the diplomatic level, the U.S. has actively promoted a ceasefire. According to Xinhua News Agency, under U.S. mediation, the Israeli and Lebanese sides held two rounds of ambassador-level talks in Washington on April 14 and 23. The Israeli and Lebanese sides began a 10-day temporary ceasefire on April 17, and President Trump announced on April 23 that the ceasefire would be extended for three weeks. On May 15, Lebanon stated that the third round of talks between Lebanon, the U.S., and Israel in Washington achieved "diplomatic progress favorable to Lebanon," and the parties agreed to extend the ceasefire period by 45 days.
Since the ceasefire took effect, the Israeli military has almost daily bombed southern Lebanon, citing violations of the ceasefire by Hezbollah, and has dismantled and destroyed so-called "Hezbollah military infrastructure" in the areas it occupies in southern Lebanon.

Iran's Red Lines: Lifting Sanctions and Releasing Frozen Funds

Regarding sanctions and asset releases, it is another core demand for the agreement, which Iran repeatedly emphasizes as non-negotiable.

According to China Central Television, on April 18, Iran's Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Baghaei said at a press conference that in the negotiations with the U.S., Iran demanded the release of frozen funds and the lifting of sanctions.

Baghaei said that for years, Iran's assets have been frozen in several banks, and Iran has been unable to access these assets. Regarding the issue of lifting sanctions, this is also one of Iran's demands. These two demands are always raised by Iran's delegation in each negotiation.

On April 22, Iran's Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Baghaei said in an interview that Iran does not require any "concessions" from the U.S., but only its legitimate rights. Baghaei emphasized that Iran's demands are for the U.S. to stop its "evil acts" against the Iranian people, and related sanctions must be lifted, and Iran's frozen assets must be unfrozen and returned to Iran.

title: Fed Governor Waller Signals Policy Uncertainty, Says Chances of Rate Hikes and Cuts Are 'Evenly Matched'
summary: Fed Governor Waller explicitly stated that the likelihood of a rate hike is now equal to the probability of a rate cut for the Fed's next interest rate move. If inflation does not quickly begin to slow, he does not rule out the possibility of future rate hikes; he also said he would support removing the 'policy bias toward easing' language from the statement. Waller warned that if inflation expectations start to lose their anchor, he would not hesitate to support a rate hike.
content:
On Friday, Fed Governor Waller stated that as the energy shock from the Iran conflict pushes up prices, he supports making it clear that the chances of a rate hike are equal to those of a rate cut for the Fed's next interest rate action.

Waller said his current stance is to remain patient and hold rates steady until the impact of the war becomes clearer, but he warned on Friday that if inflation does not quickly begin to ease, he cannot rule out the possibility of a rate hike in the future.

Waller delivered a speech titled "Policy Risks Have Changed" at a meeting in Frankfurt, during which he stated:

Inflation is not moving in the right direction. I would support removing the "bias toward easing" language from our policy statement to clearly indicate that the likelihood of a rate cut is not greater than that of a rate hike.

Waller said the oil shock may soon subside, but he added that if inflation does not quickly ease, I cannot rule out the possibility of a rate hike at some point in the future.

At the April policy meeting, the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee (FOMC) decided to keep the benchmark federal funds rate unchanged in the range of 3.5% to 3.75%. However, this decision drew objections from three policymakers who disagreed with the so-called "bias toward easing" language in the post-meeting statement—language that implied the Fed would eventually resume rate cuts.

The minutes from that meeting showed that most Fed officials warned that if inflation continued to stay above the 2% target, the Fed might need to consider raising rates. Since the April decision, stronger-than-expected job data and faster-than-expected inflation data have reinforced the view that price pressures pose a greater risk from this conflict than a sharp economic slowdown.

New survey data released on Friday showed that the May Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index fell to a record low, with Americans expecting annual inflation of 3.9% over the next five to ten years, higher than 3.5% in April, the highest level in seven months. They also expect costs to rise by 4.8% over the next year.

In the Q&A session following his speech, Waller said recent economic data had prompted him to reconsider his view of the Fed's policy statement. "I have long supported a bias toward easing, but recent labor market reports and inflation data have changed my mind," he said.

He added that recent spikes in U.S. government bond yields are tightening financial conditions, which could help the Fed's fight against inflation. Waller described the labor market as stabilizing but not booming, and said he believes the current level of the Fed's benchmark rate is restrictive for the U.S. economy.

Waller sees the current inflation outlook as the core driver of monetary policy. He said the greater factor driving current policy is the inflation outlook, which depends on how long the conflict lasts. "If I believe inflation expectations start to lose their anchor, I will not hesitate to support raising the federal funds rate target range. But at this stage, such action is premature. What should be done now is to watch how the conflict and data evolve," he said.

Waller also mentioned during his speech that the Fed can no longer return to the small balance sheet size seen in 2008, and may reduce its balance sheet by $300 billion to $500 billion.

Waller made his remarks as Kevin Warsh was expected to be sworn in at a ceremony at the White House for his new role as Fed Chair.

President Trump has put significant pressure on the Fed to cut rates more quickly and has explicitly stated he will only choose a new chair who agrees with his views. This has led some critics of Warsh to question whether he would accept the president's demands and whether the Fed can maintain its independence under his leadership. Warsh dismissed these concerns during his confirmation hearing for the chairmanship.

Waller warned on Friday that any perceived threat to the Fed's independence could trigger bond market volatility, which cannot be ignored, but he expressed optimism about maintaining independence. "I believe, at the critical moment, the institution will step up and recognize the necessity of Fed independence and protect it," he said.

After Waller's speech, traders increased their bets on rate hikes, with the swap market fully pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike before December for the first time.

  • Bloomberg Dollar Index hit a daily high.
  • U.S. Treasury yields made a V-shaped reversal, rising above 4.57%, and had fallen to 4.5241% earlier at 21:16, hitting a daily low. The two-year U.S. Treasury yield rose to 4.1231%, hitting a daily high, with a daily increase of about 3.7 basis points, and had also hit a daily low of 4.0505% at 21:16.
  • The S&P 500 index rose more than 0.4%, the Dow rose 287 points, or 0.57%, the Nasdaq rose 0.28%, the semiconductor index rose 1.88%, and the bank index rose 0.47%.
