title: Party Over? Strongest Earnings Season Peaks, Major Macroeconomic Data Next Week May Trigger Treasury Storm
summary: Next week, US equities will face key macroeconomic tests: the April PCE, first-quarter GDP revisions, and consumer confidence data will be released. With Treasury yields already at multi-year highs and markets beginning to discuss 're-hiking,' any unexpected inflation signals could further push up yields, putting pressure on equity valuations near historical highs. As the strongest earnings season loses momentum, macro risks are once again becoming the core of market pricing.
content:
As the first-quarter earnings season approaches its end, the US equity market is shifting from an earnings-driven phase to a sensitive stage dominated by macro variables. Inflation, oil prices, bond yields, and Federal Reserve policy expectations have once again become the core of market pricing.

From the market perspective, although the S&P 500 index has been volatile this week, it remains less than 1% below its all-time high, and has risen more than 8% year-to-date. Strong corporate earnings initially helped the market ignore rising yields, higher oil prices, and geopolitical risks, but this buffer is weakening.

Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise, noted: "Company earnings have basically concluded." Investors are shifting their focus from earnings to the macro environment . Next week, due to the Memorial Day holiday, trading hours will be shortened, and market sensitivity to data may increase further.

Treasury selling has triggered market tension. The 10-year Treasury yield hit a new high since January 2025, while the 30-year yield reached its highest level since 2007. The upcoming release of April PCE, first-quarter GDP revisions, and consumer confidence data will be critical tests. In a context of elevated long-term yields and discussions about 're-hiking,' any unexpected inflation signals could further push up yields, putting pressure on US equity valuations near historical highs.

The Earnings High Point Approaches, Macro Risks Reprice

The key support for this round of US equity gains has been outperforming corporate earnings. According to LSEG IBES data, over 90% of companies in the S&P 500 index have reported results, with first-quarter overall earnings expected to grow more than 28% year-over-year.

This allowed the market to absorb pressure from higher yields and higher energy prices for a period. Scott Wren, senior global market strategist at Wells Fargo Investment Institute, said that market expectations for earnings and economic growth are "very high," and these expectations are already reflected in current stock prices.

This is the core issue the market currently faces. The positive tailwinds from the earnings season are fading, while stock prices remain high. If macroeconomic data shows more persistent inflation or a more hawkish interest rate path, equity valuations may face reevaluation.

Treasury Sell-Off Intensifies, Yields Become the Equity Market's "Ceiling"

The bond market is becoming the most direct pressure source for US equities. Rising yields mean falling bond prices, which also suppress stock valuations and increase financing costs for consumers and businesses, constraining risk assets.

Jim Baird, chief investment officer at Plante Moran Financial Advisors, said, "Inflation concerns are still rising, and the upward trend in long-term Treasury yields is challenging the bond market. If it continues for some time, it could create an 'effective ceiling' for the overall stock market."

title: Bearish Signal! Bank of America: U.S. Equity Market Shows Typical Signs of Peak Optimism
summary: The Bank of America's Bull & Bear Indicator rose to 8.0 this week, triggering a bearish signal. The report indicates that the U.S. equity market shows characteristics of a bubble, including strong price momentum, retail investor enthusiasm, and low volatility. Market concentration, led by the AI Big 10 stocks, has exceeded levels seen in multiple historical bubbles. Fund flows show technology stocks attracting $9 billion in net inflows in one week, while Bank of America private client stock allocation reached an all-time high. Historical data shows that after a sell signal is triggered, global markets face pressure for short-term corrections.
content:
U.S. equity market sentiment has reached an extremely optimistic range, with Bank of America warning of potential short-term pressure on risk assets.

According to the latest report from Bank of America Securities, The Flow Show, its core sentiment indicator, the Bull & Bear Indicator, rose to 8.0, officially triggering a bearish signal for risk assets. This is the 17th time the indicator has issued a sell signal since 2002. Historical data shows that in the 2-3 months following such signals, global markets have averaged a decline of 2% to 3%, with maximum drawdowns reaching 15% to 20%.

In the report, strategist Michael Hartnett noted that the current market exhibits the characteristics of a bubble, with strong price movements, retail investor enthusiasm, and low volatility. Market concentration, led by the AI Big 10 (Magnificent 7 plus Broadcom, AMD, and Micron), has reached 48%, surpassing levels seen during the 1920s 'Roaring Twenties,' the 1970s 'Nifty Fifty,' the 1980s Japanese bubble, and the 1990s tech bubble period.

At the same time, fund flows showed clear divergence this week: Technology stocks attracted $9 billion in net inflows in one week, the largest single-week inflow since October 2025; U.S. Treasury bonds attracted $10.8 billion in net inflows, the highest in nine weeks; while cryptocurrencies faced the largest single-week net outflow of $1.5 billion since February 2026, with emerging market stocks experiencing net outflows for six consecutive weeks, and European stocks also facing capital outflows for six consecutive weeks.

Bull & Bear Indicator Triggers Sell Signal, Sentiment Indicators Remain Strongly Positive

The Bank of America Bull & Bear Indicator rose from 7.8 to 8.0 this week, officially crossing the threshold for a bearish signal. Looking at the components, the Fund Manager Survey (FMS) position component is at the 95th percentile, indicating extreme bullishness; hedge fund positions, bond fund inflows, and credit market technical indicators are all at the 74th to 75th percentile, showing a bullish stance; global stock market breadth is at the 74th percentile.

Bank of America's同步 tracking of the FMS cash indicator shows that fund manager cash holdings have dropped to 3.9%, also triggering a sell signal, and this signal has persisted for four weeks. The report notes that the FMS stock allocation saw a record monthly increase, combined with declining cash levels, is the core driver behind the rise in the Bull & Bear Indicator.

Data from Bank of America private clients further confirms this extreme optimism: As of the latest statistics, Bank of America private clients manage $4.5 trillion in assets, with stock allocations rising to 65.7%, an all-time high; bond allocations dropped to 17.3%, the lowest since March 2022; and cash allocations fell to 9.9%, also an all-time low.

Fund Flows: Bonds and Tech Attract Capital, Emerging Markets and Europe Continue to Lose Funds

This week, global fund flows showed a pattern of "strong bonds and tech, while emerging markets and Europe continue to face pressure."

In terms of bonds, this week saw net inflows of $3.05 billion, continuing for 56 consecutive weeks. U.S. Treasury bonds had net inflows of $10.8 billion, the highest in nine weeks; investment-grade bonds had net inflows for seven consecutive weeks; TIPS had net inflows for 16 consecutive weeks.

In terms of stocks, this week saw net inflows of $2.4 billion, with ETFs attracting $20.6 billion in net inflows and actively managed mutual funds seeing $18.1 billion in net outflows. Technology stocks attracted $9 billion in net inflows in one week, the largest since October 2025; U.S. stocks have seen eight consecutive weeks of net inflows, the longest streak since December 2025.

In contrast, emerging market stocks saw net outflows of $7.9 billion this week, continuing for six consecutive weeks, the longest streak since November 2024; European stocks saw net outflows of $2.3 billion, continuing for six consecutive weeks, the longest streak since February 2025. Financial stocks saw net outflows of $2.4 billion, the largest in ten weeks; materials stocks saw net outflows of $2.9 billion, the largest in eight weeks. Cryptocurrencies saw net outflows of $1.5 billion, the largest single-week outflow since February 2026.

title: UBS Deep Report: China's Chemical Industry at the Start of a New Major Cycle
summary: 2026 may mark the beginning of a new cycle for China's chemical industry. UBS noted that slowing capital expenditure, strict policy controls on new capacity, and the exit of high-cost overseas production are driving the sector into a recovery phase from its 2025 profit bottom. The Middle East situation has pushed oil prices higher, further enhancing the cost advantages of low-cost routes such as coal-to-olefins and light hydrocarbon cracking. Current sector valuations and holdings remain low, with investor focus shifting towards leading companies with global competitiveness, scale effects, and cost moats. Segments such as polyurethane, agrochemicals, and refrigerants show significant elasticity.
content:
The Chinese chemical industry is standing at the beginning of a new major cycle.

A recent 100-page in-depth report by UBS indicates that as capital expenditure growth slows, overseas outdated capacity accelerates its exit, and policies tighten control over new capacity, the industry will see a structural upturn after 2026.

The report states that the industry's profitability hit a historical low in 2025 and is now showing clear signs of recovery. The accelerated closure of high-cost facilities in Europe, combined with voluntary production cuts in multiple domestic segments, is gradually improving supply-demand dynamics, providing substantial support for the restoration of chemical company profit margins.

While short-term uncertainty in global supply chains has increased due to Middle East geopolitical tensions, UBS believes this is merely a temporary disturbance rather than a structural turning point. This situation has raised the oil price benchmark, significantly enhancing the cost advantages of alternative production routes such as coal-based chemical processes and light hydrocarbon cracking, prompting market funds to concentrate on assets with raw material advantages.

Currently, the valuation of the Chinese chemical sector remains at a historically relatively low level. In terms of investment strategy, market focus is shifting from concerns about short-term cost inflation and supply chain disruptions to cyclical improvement, with industry leaders possessing global competitiveness, scale effects, and significant cost advantages becoming the core direction for fund allocation.

Declining Capital Expenditure and Policy Tightening Drive Cyclical Reversal

Historical data shows a high correlation between capital expenditure and profit margins in the chemical industry. High profits typically drive capital expenditure and capacity expansion, while a significant decline in capital expenditure often signals an upcoming profit recovery. UBS pointed out that after a period of concentrated capacity deployment, capital expenditure growth in China's chemical industry is slowing down, which will provide momentum for profit recovery in the next one to two years.

Policy tightening is another core element driving this major cycle reversal. During the 14th Five-Year Plan period, the government is expected to tighten approval for new petrochemical capacity. As the carbon peaking target approaches after 2030, the difficulty of approving new chemical capacity will increase significantly. At the same time, the "double control" of total carbon emissions and intensity, along with the promotion of updating and transforming old capacity, will accelerate the elimination of outdated capacity.

In addition, adjustments in import and export policies are also reshaping the industry structure. Starting from April 1, 2026, China has abolished export tax rebates for several chemical products and implemented controls on the export of refined oil and fertilizers. This series of policy measures mean that the Chinese chemical industry is officially entering a new cycle characterized by optimizing existing capacity and high-quality development.

Geopolitical Conflicts Disrupt Supply, Cost Advantages Redefine Market Focus

Since the outbreak of the Middle East conflict, concerns about rising costs and supply interruptions have intensified.

UBS expects the average price of Brent crude oil in 2026 and 2027 to reach $86 per barrel and $80 per barrel respectively, with the benchmark higher than pre-conflict levels.

The high oil price directly changed the profitability of different chemical production routes.

For example, traditional naphtha cracking routes for basic petrochemical products like ethylene and propylene face profit squeezing due to rising crude oil costs, and some new overseas plants even face long-term losses and potential exit risks.

By contrast, China's coal-to-olefins (CTO) and ethane cracking (EDH) routes have shown significant cost advantages.

Baofeng Energy, as the largest coal-to-olefins enterprise in China, directly benefits from the expansion of the oil-coal price difference. Shenzhen Satellite Chemical relies on imported US ethane for light hydrocarbon cracking, building a deep cost moat.

UBS believes that geopolitical risks will prompt companies to pay more attention to the security of raw material supply, and future expansion of naphtha-based petrochemical capacity will be more cautious. As geopolitical risks gradually ease, the investment focus will return to fundamentals, focusing on companies that can achieve low-cost expansion through alternative raw material routes.

Segmentation Divergence, Polyurethane and Agrochemicals Show Recovery Elasticity

Among the more than 20 chemical sub-sectors covered, UBS points out that the recovery rhythm of each sector shows significant divergence.

The fundamental aspects of the polyurethane (PU) industry continue to improve. MDI and TDI industries have extremely high technical and capital barriers, with global supply presenting a oligopoly pattern. Industry leaders such as Wanhua Chemical have strong pricing power, maintaining profits during market downturns, and future new capacity will mainly be concentrated among the leaders, ensuring a stable supply-demand structure.

In the agrochemical sector, pesticides and potash show strong recovery elasticity. Glyphosate, the most widely used herbicide globally, has limited domestic new capacity. Notably, in 2026, President Trump of the United States signed an executive order protecting domestic phosphorus and glyphosate production, which enhances the global strategic importance of this product.

In the fertilizer sector, changes in China's export policies for urea and phosphate fertilizers will directly affect corporate profits, while potash needs to closely monitor the progress of overseas new capacity投放.

Yakang International, with its vast potassium salt reserves in Laos, has significant production growth potential; Xinhecheng has broken foreign technology monopolies in vitamins and methionine, possessing industry-leading cost advantages.

In the fluorosilicon chemical and refrigerant sectors, third-generation refrigerants continue to see prices rise under quota systems, with solid fundamentals. At the same time, driven by the new energy vehicle and energy storage markets, downstream demand for electrolytes, industrial silicon, and PVDF remains rapidly growing.

In contrast, products highly related to real estate, such as titanium dioxide (TiO2), PVC, and soda ash, still face significant demand and profit pressures in the short term due to weak domestic real estate demand and overseas anti-dumping pressures.

Valuation at Historical Low, Focusing on Global Competitive Leaders

UBS's quantitative analysis shows that the price-earnings ratio (PE) of chemical stocks is negatively correlated with chemical product prices, while the price-to-book ratio (PB) is positively correlated with prices.

Currently, valuations and institutional holdings in the Chinese chemical sector are at a trough, offering a good layout window for long-term funds.

UBS advises investors to focus on the long term, favoring Chinese chemical industry leaders with global competitiveness, integrated industrial chains, and absolute cost advantages.

title: UAE Joins Saudi Arabia in Urging Trump to Avoid Restarting US-Iran Conflict
summary: The UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar are pressuring President Trump to avoid military action against Iran, with core concerns about potential disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz and renewed economic losses in the Gulf. The most significant shift is from the UAE, which has moved from advocating for a strong response to Iran to actively promoting peace, due to the high economic costs of conflict. Despite differences in the intensity of pressure on Iran, the three countries have a clear common bottom line: avoid a second round of military confrontation.
content:
The UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar are jointly pressuring U.S. President Trump to leave room for diplomatic negotiations and avoid military action against Iran. This move marks an unusual coordination among the three most important U.S. allies in the Gulf region, with the most significant change coming from the UAE - a country that had previously advocated for a joint counterattack against Iran and paid a heavy price for it.

On Friday local time, according to reports from multiple sources, the leaders of the three countries recently spoke separately with Trump, clearly stating that military action would not achieve the long-term goals of the United States against Iran and urging Washington to give negotiations a chance. According to CCTV International News, today, U.S. Secretary of State Rubio stated that there has been "some progress" in U.S.-Iran negotiations, but the U.S. "fundamental position remains unchanged," that "Iran must not have nuclear weapons".

The direct background of this mediation effort is the concern that if hostilities resume, Iran's retaliation could plunge the Gulf economy into chaos.

The market implications of this diplomatic campaign cannot be ignored. The Strait of Hormuz was previously closed due to war, leading to a surge in energy prices, blocking oil and gas exports for Gulf countries, and causing billions of dollars in losses to ports and energy infrastructure. If the situation escalates again, these impacts will be repeated. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said last Friday that negotiations had made "minor progress", and Iranian media also sent similar signals.

UAE's Sharp Shift: From War Hawk to Peacemaker

This shift in the UAE's stance contrasts sharply with its earlier hardline approach.

Financial media reports previously noted that after the U.S. and Israel launched a military strike against Iran on February 28, UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed immediately held intensive calls with Gulf leaders such as Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, advocating for a collective response to Iran. His core assessment was that only collective action could form an effective deterrent, citing the historical context of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), established in 1981, whose original purpose was to counter Iranian threats.

However, Saudi Arabia responded: "This is not our war." After Qatar's Ras Laffan liquefied natural gas plant was attacked, it briefly considered a response but ultimately chose to play an intermediary role; Bahrain and Kuwait followed Saudi's stance and stayed out of the issue; Oman, due to its closer relations with Iran, was never seen as a potential participant.

After being rejected, the UAE opted for unilateral action, launching limited strikes against Iran without the support of its Gulf allies starting in early March, and striking again in April.

The UAE paid a price for this stance.

This war severely damaged the UAE's aviation, tourism, and real estate sectors, leading to widespread salary cuts and layoffs, damaging its image as an international financial and tourist hub. Just last Sunday, a drone attack targeted a nuclear power plant in the UAE, with Abu Dhabi attributing the attack to Iran-backed Iraqi militias.

Bloomberg Economics analyst Dina Esfandiary pointed out that the Gulf Arab states "are caught between the U.S.-Iran war and bear most of the impact. If a ceasefire does not translate into a permanent agreement, they face the prospect of renewed confrontation, and their image as a stable regional safe haven will be threatened."

Divergent Positions Among the Three Countries, Common Bottom Line Is to Avoid a 'Second Round'

title: $4.5 Per Gallon Drains Middle Class! To Save Money, Americans Can Only Cut Steak and Bars
summary: The national average price of gasoline in the US has surpassed $4.5 per gallon, but consumers face essential travel needs that make it difficult to significantly reduce fuel consumption, forcing them to cut discretionary spending. US gasoline inventories are at their lowest level for the same period in the past twelve years, while demand remains strong, with summer travel season expected to further intensify supply-demand tensions.
content:
Rising oil prices are quietly reshaping the daily budgets of American consumers: cars can't be avoided, so they have to cut back on steak and bar visits.

According to Bloomberg, due to the Iran conflict, the national average price of gasoline has exceeded $4.5 per gallon, with California prices exceeding $6. Despite high prices, consumers have not significantly reduced fuel purchases. For most Americans, driving for commuting and picking up children is a necessity.

Gasoline expenses are almost impossible to cut, so consumers are cutting discretionary spending to balance their budgets. Philadelphia resident Avarisse Crawford said she has reduced entertainment expenses, replacing steak dinners and bar parties with free park activities.

The ongoing situation in the Middle East continues to push up oil prices, with the actual blockade of the Strait of Hormuz causing disruptions in global crude oil transportation. US gasoline inventories have dropped to the lowest level for the same period since 2014, and Morgan Stanley expects them to reach a seasonal historical low by late August.

Faced with rising oil prices, the Trump administration has released strategic petroleum reserves, exempted the Jones Act, and discussed implementing a federal gasoline tax holiday, but the effects have been limited so far. With the Memorial Day weekend marking the start of the summer travel season, upward pressure on demand is likely to further strain already tight inventories.

Rising Oil Prices, Unchanged Demand

The current supply and demand situation provides strong support for gasoline prices. US gasoline inventories are at their lowest level in the past twelve years for this time of year, with imports hovering near the lowest levels for the past decade. Refineries are also continuing to shift capacity toward jet fuel, further reducing gasoline production.

More importantly, demand remains highly resilient - despite the price exceeding $4 per gallon, consumers have not significantly reduced fuel purchases. Over the past four weeks, the average gasoline price reached $4.32 per gallon, yet actual fuel consumption remained higher than the same periods in 2022 and 2025.

Macquarie Global energy strategist Vikas Dwivedi noted, as long as prices remain below $5, demand decline will be minimal, but this also means the supply-demand gap will continue to widen. Carlisle Group's senior advisor and economist Jeff Currie warned that the US energy market is facing an impending crisis, expecting the issue to become apparent in July.

Inelastic Gasoline Demand, Pressure on Discretionary Spending

Faced with high oil prices, many Americans have not reduced travel but instead shifted the pressure to other areas of consumption.

According to Bloomberg, Barclays credit card data shows that within about two months after the Middle East conflict erupted, consumer spending on accommodation, clothing, movie theaters, and groceries was below seasonal levels. The Bank of America Institute found that large home goods spending declined absolutely in April, while air travel and accommodation spending remained largely unchanged.

Although overall travel demand still shows resilience, some indicators have shown signs of weakness. GasBuddy survey showed that the percentage of Americans planning to drive more than two hours this summer is 56%, down from 69% last year. AAA survey showed that about 10% of respondents plan to cancel trips due to high prices, while about one-third said they were unaffected.

California offers a more direct reference. Due to refinery closures, isolated pipelines, and special regulations, California gasoline prices have been consistently high. Elizabeth Graham, CEO of the California Fuel & Convenience Alliance, said that after the state average price rose to $6.14 per gallon, fuel consumption at gas stations has decreased by 9% since the fall of 2025.

Ordinary consumers have already made real changes in their decisions. Philadelphia resident Avarisse Crawford commutes five days a week and drives twice a month to visit relatives, and reducing driving is not an option. She cut her entertainment budget, replaced steak dinners and office party gatherings with park activities, and gave up her planned Florida road trip. She said, "Driving to Florida is no longer an option."

title: ‘New Fed Whisperer’：Trump Nominates Warsh for Rate Cuts, but Markets Begin Betting on Hikes
summary: Amid rising energy prices due to Iran tensions, AI-driven demand, and persistent inflation, market expectations have quickly shifted, with investors now betting on potential rate hikes rather than cuts. Bond yields continue to rise, reflecting a reevaluation of a 'high-interest-rate normal.' Warsh's biggest challenge will not only be managing inflationary pressures but also establishing his own credibility amid Trump's political influence and the Federal Reserve's independence.
content:
President Trump's appointment of Kevin Warsh to lead the Federal Reserve was intended to push for rate cuts. However, as inflation continues to rise and bond markets experience volatility, market bets have quietly shifted—next steps may be hikes rather than cuts.

Warsh is set to be sworn in at the White House on Friday, becoming the first Federal Reserve chair since Alan Greenspan in 1987 to take the oath at the White House. This marks his first public appearance with the president since being nominated by Trump in January.

According to Nick Timiraos, a renowned reporter for The Wall Street Journal and known as the 'New Fed Whisperer,' he is inheriting a high-risk environment: upward pressure on inflation, rising long-term Treasury yields, and an increasing number of investors who believe the Fed's next move could be a rate hike rather than a cut.

The impact of this situation on the market is already evident. In his latest article, Timiraos notes that investors are abandoning bets on Fed rate cuts, pushing up bond yields and thus increasing overall borrowing costs.

When asked this week whether he could accept a Fed led by Warsh that raises rates, Trump gave a vague response: "I will let him do what he wants." According to James Egelhof, chief U.S. economist at BNP Paribas, this statement further widened the range of market expectations for the Fed's policy under Warsh and "supported the re-pricing of the bond market toward rate hikes."

Iran Conflict and AI Boom Create Dual Pressures That Disrupt Rate Cut Plans

The macroeconomic environment Warsh faces upon taking office is vastly different from what Trump originally envisioned.

About a month after Trump nominated Warsh in January, the U.S. launched a war against Iran, leading to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, sustained high energy prices, and increased inflationary pressure. This is the second time the Trump administration has asked the Fed to "look the other way" regarding price pressures tied to its own policies—previously, the government had requested the Fed adopt a similar stance on inflation caused by tariffs.

At the same time, the AI boom is becoming an engine for demand and growth, temporarily raising rather than easing price pressures. Some analysts believe that the bond market's selling not only reflects concerns about inflation but also highlights a "new normal of high interest rates" shaped by expanding government deficits and AI-driven productivity gains.

Joseph Lavorgna, chief economist at SMBC Americas, stated in a recent client report that due to the impact of the Iran conflict, the Fed may need to raise rates by about one percentage point to reverse the three rate cuts implemented in the second half of 2025. He said bluntly: "I don't think anyone with credibility can say the Fed should cut rates now."

White House and Market Diverge, Policy Narrative Shows Cracks

Faced with the gap between rate cut expectations and market realities, two of the Trump administration's top economic officials have recently stepped forward to try to bridge the divide.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC last week that current inflation driven by supply shocks is merely a "temporary supply shock," and the Fed could choose to ignore it, predicting that price pressures would ease significantly after "one or two more hot inflation readings." Kevin Hassett, director of the White House National Economic Council, echoed the same stance on Bloomberg TV a few days ago, saying that "it is likely that we will see rate cuts in 2026 because of Kevin Warsh."

However, bond market trends contradict this narrative. Timiraos cited some economists who pointed out that if the Fed remains inactive while inflation continues to rise, it effectively means monetary policy has become loose in practice.

Steve Englander of Standard Chartered wrote in a recent client report: "If Warsh's independence is unquestionable, we would likely predict a rate hike by the end of 2026 or early 2027." But he believes political constraints have not yet been eliminated and expects rates to remain unchanged until 2027.

Warsh's Political Capital and Independence Test

Whether Warsh can navigate a path of independence between political pressure and economic reality is the core issue currently capturing market attention.

According to The Wall Street Journal, citing three informed sources, Trump called Warsh multiple times before the Senate confirmation hearing last month to inquire about the economic situation. Warsh's allies believe this direct communication channel is a unique advantage he has over his predecessor, Jerome Powell, who never considered influencing the president part of his responsibilities.

Steven Blitz of TS Lombard noted that if Warsh wants to push any policy that Trump might not accept, the key internal move would be to "first secure Bessent's support."

Warsh himself refused to provide any forward guidance on potential policy trade-offs during his confirmation hearing and stated that he would decide on policy based on actual conditions, without making any commitment to rate cuts with Trump.

James Egelhof of BNP Paribas believes the first few weeks and months of Warsh's tenure at the Fed will be exceptionally critical.

Much of Warsh's career has focused on warning central banks to maintain a firm stance against inflation. The current conditions that have pushed the rate cut agenda into a corner represent a historical opportunity for him to prove his credibility. "This is a test," Egelhof said, "but it is also a huge opportunity."

title: SpaceX IPO Sparks Wall Street Frenzy, US Space-Themed ETFs Attract $1.3 Billion in a Month
summary: The expected SpaceX IPO has ignited a surge in space-themed investment, with U.S. space-related ETFs attracting $1.3 billion in new funds over the past month, raising total assets to $3.3 billion. Six new products have launched rapidly, while analysts warn of risks from high portfolio overlap and overvaluation in the sector.
content:
The expectation of SpaceX's IPO has sparked market enthusiasm, leading to explosive growth in space-themed ETFs, but concerns about highly overlapping portfolios have also emerged.

According to Morningstar Direct data, U.S. space-related ETFs attracted $1.3 billion in new funds over the past month, bringing the total assets under management in the sector to $3.3 billion.

The core driver of this fund inflow is the signal from Elon Musk's SpaceX that it plans to go public in 2026.

New product launches are accelerating in parallel. In just the past three months, six new space-themed ETFs have been introduced to the market, with two more expected to launch around the time of SpaceX's anticipated mid-June listing. Some issuers have also submitted applications to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for leveraged and enhanced yield ETFs directly linked to SpaceX. However, analysts warn that existing space-themed ETFs have a portfolio overlap rate exceeding 50%, and investors should be cautious of structural risks behind the hot trend.

Rapid Expansion of Space ETFs

Before this, investors who wanted to focus on the space economy—rather than broader aerospace and defense sectors—had only one option: the Procure Space ETF, launched in 2019.

However, the market landscape has changed rapidly since SpaceX began clearly signaling its IPO intent in the past three months, leading to the emergence of six new funds.

Among them, the Tema Space Innovators ETF, with assets of $1.27 billion, stands out—its asset accumulation in just seven weeks has surpassed the $972 million accumulated by UFO over seven years.

Morningstar ETF analyst Bryan Armour described this phenomenon as a typical reaction to a new hot topic: "Whenever something shiny and new appears in the market, we often see this kind of situation."

New Product Launches Continue, Leveraged Products Loom

The wave of new product launches is far from over.

Two more space-themed ETFs are expected to launch within weeks of SpaceX's IPO. Meanwhile, some issuers have already submitted documents to the SEC, planning to launch leveraged ETFs and enhanced yield ETFs directly tied to SpaceX.

The latest two products—VanEck Space ETF and Corgi Space and Satellite Communications ETF—were launched just days apart in May, collectively attracting $13.6 million in assets.

Nick Frasse, product manager at VanEck, said the company had been closely monitoring this sector, but only in recent months did it conclude that the market had reached a real turning point—"there are enough diversified and pure space economy companies to support the operation of these thematic ETFs."

He also pointed out that SpaceX's listing would drive more related companies into the space economy ecosystem.

Beyond SpaceX, Space Stocks Have Already Soared

Although SpaceX remains the central narrative in the market, ETF managers emphasize that the investment logic of the space economy has already gone beyond the expectation of a single IPO.

Rocket Lab and AST SpaceMobile have risen 393% and 258% respectively over the past 12 months, showing strong performance before SpaceX's official listing.

Andrew Chanin, CEO of Procure, noted that two-thirds of the fund's inflows occurred over the past 12 months, with 20% concentrated in the last month alone.

He recalled that the fund was once rated as the "worst ETF launch of the year" by Morningstar when it was launched in 2019, yet Morningstar data shows that the ETF has returned 49% this year and 133.6% over the past year.

Chanin positioned the space economy as a "tollbooth on the highway of AI," arguing that as satellites and orbital data centers play a key role in the next phase of the communication revolution, the strategic value of the space economy will continue to grow.

High Portfolio Overlap, Analysts Warn of Structural Risks

Amid the frenzy, risks cannot be ignored. Todd Sohn, ETF strategist at Strategas, warned that "chasing SpaceX, space themes, and the next big story" could carry hidden dangers.

A Reuters analysis of the top holdings of the current seven pure space-themed ETFs showed that all funds' top ten holdings included the same four stocks (including Rocket Lab), and the portfolio overlap among funds exceeded 50%.

"When everyone thinks the same way, I start to get worried," Sohn said, "this makes it hard for any single fund manager or product to truly differentiate itself, and ultimately, they can only distinguish themselves through marketing."

He also reminded investors that the space economy is still a very small niche within the broader tech landscape, and recent strong gains should not obscure the recognition of its structural limitations.

Andrew Chanin, CEO of Procure, noted that two-thirds of the fund's inflows occurred over the past 12 months, with 20% concentrated in the last month alone.

He recalled that the fund was once rated as the "worst ETF launch of the year" by Morningstar when it was launched in 2019, yet Morningstar data shows that the ETF has returned 49% this year and 133.6% over the past year.

Chanin positioned the space economy as a "tollbooth on the highway of AI," arguing that as satellites and orbital data centers play a key role in the next phase of the communication revolution, the strategic value of the space economy will continue to grow.

High Portfolio Overlap, Analysts Warn of Structural Risks

Amid the frenzy, risks cannot be ignored. Todd Sohn, ETF strategist at Strategas, warned that "chasing SpaceX, space themes, and the next big story" could carry hidden dangers.

A Reuters analysis of the top holdings of the current seven pure space-themed ETFs showed that all funds' top ten holdings included the same four stocks (including Rocket Lab), and the portfolio overlap among funds exceeded 50%.

"When everyone thinks the same way, I start to get worried," Sohn said, "this makes it hard for any single fund manager or product to truly differentiate itself, and ultimately, they can only distinguish themselves through marketing."

He also reminded investors that the space economy is still a very small niche within the broader tech landscape, and recent strong gains should not obscure the recognition of its structural limitations.

title: 59,800 yuan starting price for battery-swap model, Arc aims to boost sales
summary: Establishment of three brand series.
content:
On the evening of May 22, the new home-use pure electric sedan Beta S3 of Arc was officially launched. This model, which had been highly anticipated since mid-April, secured over 30,000 orders within a month.

76% of the orders were for the version supporting CATL's chocolate battery-swap technology.

This new model has made precise segmentation in pricing and sales models: it offers eight configurations, with the charging version using a conventional battery-buyout model priced between 79,800 yuan and 120,800 yuan. The battery-swap version, on the other hand, has a base price as low as 59,800 yuan, ranging from 59,800 yuan to 71,800 yuan, with a monthly battery rental fee of 599 yuan.

At the launch event, Liu Guanqiao, Party Secretary of Beijing Benz Blue Valley and Chairman of Beijing Benz New Energy, systematically outlined Arc's latest brand sequence for the first time: the 'Wenda' series for high-end flagship positioning, the 'Alpha' series as the technological backbone, and the 'Beta' series focusing on cost-effectiveness and technology penetration.

Looking back at the past few years, Arc faced periods of low sales and lack of hit models in the fierce market competition.

But entering this year, Arc's strategic intent became extremely clear. In addition to Alpha, it is pushing upwards with the 'Wenda' series to elevate brand positioning, and downwards with the 'Beta' series to deepen the lower-tier market and capture sales volume.

In 2026, as the elimination race in the new energy vehicle market intensifies and the Matthew effect becomes more pronounced, the launch of Beta S3 not only represents Arc's price cut into the A-level and A0-level sedan market, but also signals the brand's full-scale effort to break through.

01 Battery Swap Opens Market

In the 60,000-100,000 yuan new energy passenger car market, the traditional product model has long been synonymous with compromise.

To control manufacturing costs, automakers typically offer A0 or even A00 level vehicles. Although these models are low-priced, they often suffer from cramped space, lack of intelligent features, and single charging methods. However, Beta S3 takes an opposite approach with an aggressive, premium strategy.

According to the announced parameters, Beta S3 has a length of 4916mm, a wheelbase of 2876mm, and a golden wheelbase ratio of 1.94. In the era of internal combustion engines, this is a standard B-class mid-size sedan size; but in the new energy sector, Arc has brought its starting price down to as low as 64,800 yuan for pre-sales and 59,800 yuan with limited-time discounts.

This pricing strategy breaks traditional class barriers, directly entering the price range of traditional micro or small city cars like BYD Hai'O and Wuling Bingguo, but offering the space experience of a foreign-made mid-size car.

The real 'killer feature' of Beta S3 is its deep integration with CATL's chocolate battery swap technology. Among the 30,000 pre-sale orders, 76% were for the battery-swap version. This number indicates that power anxiety remains the core concern for mass-market users.

For families without fixed parking spaces or private charging piles, the time spent queuing at public charging stations is a key pain point. The Beta S3 equipped with CATL battery swap technology can complete a fully automatic battery swap in just 99 seconds, faster than refueling.

A car engineer told financial media reports that the successful implementation of the battery-swap model in the 60,000-yuan market is essentially a dual innovation in finance and user experience. On one hand, the battery lease model significantly lowers the initial purchase threshold for users. On the other, battery maintenance is handled by battery operators, completely eliminating concerns about battery health degradation and depreciation of used car value.

Yang Jun, General Manager of CATL's battery swap business, revealed at the event that the number of CATL chocolate battery swap stations will exceed 3,000 by the end of 2026.

This means that Arc does not need to bear the heavy burden of building its own battery swap stations, but can quickly expand a vast charging network by leveraging the infrastructure benefits of industry giants.

With the intensified elimination race in the 2026 automotive market, a simple price war has already left companies exhausted. By introducing the battery-swap model, Beta S3 actually shifts the competitive dimension from purely整车 manufacturing costs to the overall user experience across the entire lifecycle. This is the commercial logic behind its large number of pre-sale orders. However, a successful pre-sale does not equate to brand safety.

02 Brand System Reorganization

Beta S3 represents a comprehensive reorganization of the Arc brand sequence.

Looking back at the history of China's new energy vehicle development, Arc had a very high starting point, being one of the first brands in China to deeply cooperate with Huawei on intelligent driving and introduce Magna's high-end manufacturing system. However, in recent years, due to its high product positioning and misalignment with the mainstream consumer market, Arc has long faced the dilemma of critical acclaim but poor sales, with relatively few hit models.

The turning point came in the past two years. With management adjustments and a comprehensive restructuring of the marketing system, Arc gradually stabilized its position through practical strategies such as 'electricity cheaper than fuel' and 'premium configuration', successfully entering the ten-thousand-unit monthly sales club.

However, facing the extremely harsh industry consolidation in 2026, relying solely on ten-thousand-unit scale is insufficient to ensure the brand's future safety margin. Arc must carry out a comprehensive system expansion.

The clear definition of the three brand series marks Arc's transformation from a single model strategy to a systematic approach.

The Wenda series carries the mission of brand elevation, targeting the high-end flagship position, showcasing cutting-edge technology and luxury quality, aiming to raise the brand's price ceiling and technical image.

The Alpha series serves as the technological backbone of the brand, continuing to firmly establish itself in the mid-range mainstream market of 150,000-250,000 yuan, bearing the core tasks of technology implementation and reputation accumulation.

The core label of the Beta series is 'accessibility' and 'future'. Using extreme cost-effectiveness and cutting-edge technologies, such as ultra-fast battery swapping and advanced intelligent driving, it penetrates the lower-tier market.

The release of Beta S3 at this moment holds decisive strategic significance for the Arc brand.

Firstly, it acts as a traffic-gathering machine for expanding the base of Arc users. The 30,000 orders represent a large real household group, and this scale effect will greatly reduce the overall R&D and supply chain costs of Beijing Benz New Energy.

Secondly, by binding with CATL, Arc has opened up a new battery-swap track outside the intense pure-charging technology route, building a highly differentiated brand moat.

However, objectively speaking, Arc's full-scale efforts still face critical real challenges.

The 76% order ratio for the battery-swap version is both an opportunity and a huge delivery challenge.

The construction progress and geographical distribution of CATL's 3,000 battery-swap stations must align closely with the actual living radius of Beta S3 owners, directly determining subsequent user satisfaction.

Cost control is also an important challenge. At the 60,000-yuan price point, which is extremely sensitive to costs, providing B-class spaciousness, heat pump air conditioning, and a chassis structure supporting ultra-fast battery swapping, Beijing Benz New Energy's supply chain pressure and per-vehicle profitability will face strict scrutiny from the capital market and subsequent financial statements.

Arc has declared its determination to firmly secure its position in the second half of the new energy vehicle elimination race through the clear lineup of 'Wenda, Alpha, Beta'. The horn of systematic counterattack has already sounded, and real delivery data and infrastructure coordination capabilities will continue to test Arc.

title: AI Enters the 'Pay-per-Use and Compute Allocation' Era -- What Anthropic and DeepSeek Are Telling Us
summary: According to market sources, Anthropic's latest fundraising pitch shows that its second-quarter revenue is expected to reach $10.9 billion, with a potential operating profit of $559 million in the June quarter. This is a significant shift from last year's statement that profitability would not be achieved until at least 2028. Meanwhile, DeepSeek has made its API discount permanent, pushing token costs to their lowest level. The two companies are splitting the model layer into two paths: one making individual tokens more expensive, and the other increasing the total volume of tokens. After the shovel has been sold, the real profit war in AI has just begun.
content:
Anthropic's projection shown during a funding round to investors indicates that the company generated $4.8 billion in revenue in the first quarter and is expected to rise to $10.9 billion in the second quarter, with an estimated operating profit of $559 million in the June quarter. Additionally, in the first quarter, for every dollar earned, Anthropic spent 71 cents on compute; by the second quarter, this ratio is expected to drop to 56 cents. Last year, the company told investors that it would take until at least 2028 to achieve annual profitability, but now the profit statement is moving ahead. The driver behind this change is the growing demand from enterprise customers for Claude's programming tools and intelligent agent capabilities.

At the same time, the pricing model for AI has changed.

Renowned tech investor Gavin Baker summarized the situation with a vivid phrase: AI is moving from "all you can eat" to "pay by the drink." He refers to real-world enterprise scenarios: individuals running dozens or even hundreds of intelligent agents simultaneously to run code, retrieve, analyze, and perform multi-step reasoning, making flat-rate monthly plans increasingly difficult to cover the actual consumption.

For enterprises, model selection has shifted from engineering preferences to financial decisions, with price differences between the cheapest and most expensive cutting-edge models reaching tens or even hundreds of times.

The supply side has also given the industry little breathing room. Bridgewater's co-chief investment officer, Greg Jensen, said in an interview that the only thing growing faster than compute supply is compute demand; allocation has already started, through methods including price increases, access restrictions, and even internal lab project suspensions. Compute, power, storage, and rack systems remain under strain, and pay-per-use and access restrictions have begun to emerge simultaneously, which is not surprising.

This brings us to the most important question in the market: after the shovel has taken all the profits, what comes next in the AI transaction?

For this, Goldman Sachs and SemiAnalysis have clear differences. Goldman Sachs analyst James Covello focuses on the revenue-sharing model in the first phase: over the past two years, the most certain profit has remained in upstream sectors such as chips, HBM, advanced packaging, data centers, and power. Cloud providers have taken on capital expenditures themselves, and enterprise ROI has not yet been widely reflected in the profit statements. SemiAnalysis, however, looks at the other side: tokens are no longer just a cost of answering questions, but have become production materials for tasks such as code, research, modeling, charts, and financial analysis. If high-value tasks are willing to pay for stronger models, and cache hit rates, inference optimization, and hardware iteration continue to lower unit costs, the model laboratory will move from a loss-making stage to a profit-generating one.

Anthropic's profitability shows that top-tier model companies are not just telling growth stories. High-value tasks such as code, long-chain intelligent agents, and complex reasoning have already pushed forward both revenue and cost structures. Goldman Sachs was originally most concerned about the downstream profit statements not being solid enough, but Anthropic has provided a clear signal: in the most advanced part of the task, high-value tokens can already generate profit.

But Anthropic is not the entire model layer.

On May 22, DeepSeek announced that it had permanently implemented the 75% discount for its V4-Pro API. After the promotion ended, V4-Pro will be billed at a quarter of the original price: $0.435 per million tokens for uncacheable input and $0.87 for output; V4-Flash is even cheaper, at $0.14 and $0.28 respectively. Cache hit prices have also been reduced. The report specifically mentions that this price is particularly sensitive to agent, coding assistant, customer service, and document workflow scenarios, as these naturally rely on repeated context and caching. DeepSeek is not offering a single low-cost model, but rather a product gradient better suited for routing: Flash handles cheap daily loads, while Pro handles more complex agent coding, long-document reasoning, and high-value automation tasks.

This path is very different from Anthropic's.

Anthropic represents the path of top-tier U.S. model companies: first securing the hardest, most valuable, and most sensitive tasks, then letting high-end workflows prove model premium. It is competing for capability density, for whether enterprises are willing to pay higher prices for stronger reasoning, longer chains, and more stable results.

DeepSeek takes another route. Rather than replicating the same high-margin closed-source logic, it has tried to make unit call costs, product tiers, and cache friendliness as suitable as possible for large-scale deployment. For many applications, price is not just about saving some budget, but about determining whether a feature can be launched or a workflow can be run in production.

Within the debate between Goldman Sachs and SemiAnalysis, these two companies each answer half of the question.

Anthropic proves that high-value tokens can generate profit. DeepSeek proves that low-cost tokens can scale. The former elevates the economic value of each call, while the latter pushes the boundaries of total token volume. Goldman Sachs was most worried that downstream profits were not sufficient to support the profits and capital expenditures already captured by the upstream. However, with the simultaneous emergence of Anthropic and DeepSeek, this judgment changes. The model layer is beginning to show two different business paths, and both are expanding the pie.

This is a more positive signal for the upstream. The reason is simple. Anthropic's path proves that high-value workloads are willing to pay for stronger models; DeepSeek's path proves that once prices fall to a certain level, many previously unviable calls will be released. As long as compute and infrastructure remain in a tight supply state, the upstream will not only capture 'scarcity premium,' but also a larger overall demand. Greg Jensen said that 'allocation' has not ended, but has instead made this clearer: both high-value tokens and low-cost tokens are growing, and supply constraints still exist, making it difficult for the upstream to exit quickly.

More significant changes may come from the middle layer.

When the model layer no longer has only one approach, what enterprises truly buy is not a single model, but scheduling capabilities: which tasks go through Anthropic, which through DeepSeek Flash, which through DeepSeek Pro, which require a high-compliance system, which can be heavily cached, and which should dynamically switch between high and low configurations. The more distinct the model layers are, the more valuable routing, orchestration, workflow entry points, and budget control become.

The concern from Goldman Sachs has not disappeared. Anthropic proves that top-tier model companies can generate profit earlier in high-value scenarios, while DeepSeek proves that low prices can make more products viable. These two things do not equal the fact that ordinary enterprises have already stabilized AI costs into profit statements. DeepSeek's own low-price strategy also comes with profit pressure. This is a strategy of trading profit for reach and scale for platform usage habits. Whether it can succeed depends on architectural efficiency, financial sustainability, developer adoption translating into stable platform usage, and whether geopolitical and compliance restrictions will slow down global enterprise penetration.

However, the main issue in the market has changed. It is no longer just asking who sells the shovel, nor is it just asking when model companies will start to make money. Anthropic and DeepSeek have split the model layer into two paths: one making individual tokens more expensive, and the other increasing the total volume of tokens. As long as these two paths are not isolated cases, SemiAnalysis's view that the profit pool is still expanding will be closer to reality than Goldman Sachs' framework of 'upstream first earns, downstream cannot support.' There is still space for the upstream, not just based on scarcity, but also due to the downstream starting to grow the business in two different ways for the first time.

In the coming quarters, the most important numbers to watch in the earnings reports will be: whether the revenue quality and gross margin improvement of high-end models like Anthropic can be sustained, whether the low-price path like DeepSeek can turn developer adoption into stable call volumes, whether cloud providers can smoothly transition capital expenditures into revenue and contracts, and whether the upstream memory, compute, and rack bottlenecks will continue to push demand forward.

The next round of market divergence is likely to continue along these numbers.

title: Trump Proposes 'Green Card Exit Application' Requirement, New Anti-Immigration Measure
summary: The Trump administration has taken a significant step to restrict legal immigration channels, with new rules requiring the majority of green card applicants to leave the United States and reapply from their home countries, creating long wait times for many, especially students, tech professionals, and spouses of U.S. citizens. For Indian applicants, the waiting period could stretch for decades. LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman called the move harmful to the entire U.S., and the tech industry is already experiencing turbulence.
content:
The Trump administration announced new rules requiring most green card applicants to leave the United States and reapply for permanent residency from their home countries, marking one of the most significant restrictions on legal immigration channels to date.

According to a Friday announcement by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), current green card applicants in the U.S. on temporary visas must return to their home countries and submit applications through U.S. embassies abroad, except for "special circumstances." Previously, many applicants could complete the process within the U.S. The new rule disproportionately affects students, tech industry workers, and spouses of U.S. citizens.

Following the announcement, the tech sector responded quickly and strongly. LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman posted on X, stating that the move would "harm the tech industry, business, and the entire U.S." and questioned whether AI researchers and related professionals might be forced to leave the country and face long waits in the backlog of applications.

Risk investor Nick Davidov called it the "most absurd move" by the Department of Homeland Security and pointed out that for Indian applicants, the waiting time could last decades, while Russian applicants may face an impossible situation—there are no U.S. embassies in Russia at the moment.

New Rule: Foreign Applications Replace Domestic Adjustments

USCIS stated in its statement that the adjustment aims to "return to the original intent of the law," ensuring foreigners use the immigration system according to regulations. Spokesperson Zach Kahler said that non-immigrants who entered the U.S. on student, temporary work, or tourist visas have time-limited purposes for their visits, and "their visits should not be the first step in applying for a green card."

USCIS also said that immigration officers will assess each case and consider relevant factors to determine whether applicants can submit applications within the U.S., but the criteria for identifying "special circumstances" have not yet been further clarified.

The potential impact of the new rule on the U.S. tech industry has drawn widespread attention. Many tech companies rely on temporary work visas such as H-1B to bring in high-skilled foreign talent, and many employees are currently in the green card application process. If they have to leave the country and rejoin the queue, it could disrupt corporate talent planning and lead to critical job vacancies.

Continued Tightening of Legal Immigration Controls

This new rule is the latest measure in the Trump administration's systematic tightening of immigration policies since the start of its second term in January. Previously, the administration's immigration restrictions mainly targeted undocumented immigrants, but their effects have gradually extended to legally sponsored professional groups in the U.S.

In February, the Department of Homeland Security announced it would prioritize assigning H-1B visas to foreign workers with higher salaries and greater skills; in November of last year, the government suspended all asylum applications following the shooting of two National Guard members, and this suspension was lifted only at the end of March this year.

title: Super IPOs of SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic Crowd the Market, Bank of America Warns of a Repeat of the Super Bubble
summary: Bank of America strategist Hartnett issued a warning: technology stocks now account for more than 44% of the S&P 500 weight, and once super IPOs such as SpaceX and OpenAI are launched, the concentration will exceed 48%, surpassing the peak levels of all historical bubbles including the 'Roaring Twenties,' the 'Nifty Fifty' era of the 1970s, the Japanese bubble of the 1980s, and the dot-com bubble of the 1990s. He stated bluntly that 'retail investor frenzy, low volatility, and a strong bubble atmosphere' exist, and he warned that rising yields combined with extremely bullish positions mean the time for profit-taking has arrived.
content:
The concentration of tech stocks is approaching the historical bubble threshold, while a series of mega IPOs are pushing the market to even more dangerous territory.

Michael Hartnett, a strategist at Bank of America, warned in his latest report that if super IPOs such as SpaceX and OpenAI are launched, the weight of tech stocks in stock benchmark indices could easily exceed 48%, surpassing the concentration levels of all major historical bubbles, including the 'Roaring Twenties,' the 'Nifty Fifty' period of the 1970s, the Japanese bubble of the 1980s, and the dot-com bubble of the 1990s.

Currently, the tech sector already accounts for over 44% of the weight in the S&P 500 index. Hartnett described the current market situation as: 'Strong price movements, retail investor enthusiasm, low volatility...a strong bubble atmosphere.'

This warning comes as market sentiment is in an extremely optimistic range. According to Bloomberg, a survey of fund managers released by Bank of America earlier this week showed that investors increased their stock exposure to record levels this month, prompting Hartnett to reiterate his judgment that the stock market faces a correction risk. In his report, he pointed out, 'the consensus has reached an extremely bullish position in terms of both positioning and earnings expectations, and with yields breaking upwards, it means it's time to take profits cautiously.'

Super IPOs Intensify Tech Concentration Risks

SpaceX, owned by Elon Musk, has announced plans for the largest IPO globally, while OpenAI, the developer of ChatGPT, aims to complete its listing before its competitor Anthropic. These mega offerings will further strengthen the market's optimistic sentiment around technology and artificial intelligence, which is driving the S&P 500 to one of the most concentrated rallies in decades.

Hartnett pointed out that once these super IPOs are combined with existing AI giants, the market concentration would easily exceed the peak level of 48% seen in all previous major bubbles. This poses direct pressure on asset allocators—due to risk management constraints, many institutional investors cannot fully track this weight ratio, thereby facing the risk of increased tracking errors.

Additionally, the excessive tilt of the index toward the tech sector may mask structural risks within the market. The potential weaknesses of sectors like consumer and financial services, which have closer ties to the real economy, may be overshadowed by the strength of tech stocks, leading to distorted overall market risk assessments.

Historical Insights from Major IPOs

Hartnett reviewed several major IPO cases in history and drew conclusions that are quite cautionary. The listings of Saudi Aramco and Meta (formerly Facebook) proved to have limited impact on the broader market; however, in some IPOs with clear 'toping characteristics,' such as Visa and AIA Group, the market performance declined within 9 to 12 months after the listing.

This historical pattern suggests that super IPOs themselves may not be the direct trigger for a market crash, but they often coincide with market top phases, offering some reference value for timing decisions.

Bond Yields Are the Key Variable in Ending the Bubble

Hartnett clearly stated that surging bond yields have been a common path to the end of every boom and bubble. He used two State Street ETFs as dual indicators to observe the impact of bond yields on the stock market: if the biotech ETF falls to $120, it indicates that the impact of sustained rising yields is becoming apparent; if the ETF tracking retail stocks rises to $85, it suggests that the impact at the bond level is temporarily postponed.

In terms of policy, Hartnett expects that substantive policy tightening will not occur until CPI reaches 4% to 5% in the coming months. He also noted that before the occurrence of historic IPOs, market participants will not easily reduce their long positions—this partly explains the resilience of the current extremely optimistic sentiment and implies that potential adjustment risks are accumulating rather than being released.

Notably, Hartnett accurately predicted the relative strength of international markets last year, and his bullish view on commodities has already been realized, giving his current warning higher market attention.

title: SpaceX's Starship V3 Completes First Flight, Marking a Critical Test for Musk's IPO Ambitions
summary: SpaceX's latest V3 version of Starship completed its 12th test flight, with mixed results: the upper ship successfully reached orbit and deployed 22 simulated Starlink satellites before splashing down in the Indian Ocean, but the lower super-heavy booster failed to complete re-entry burn and crashed into the Gulf of Mexico. The flight coincided with a critical phase in SpaceX's preparations for its largest-ever IPO, potentially raising up to $75 billion.
content:
SpaceX's latest iteration of its Starship rocket completed a mixed-results test flight, occurring at a sensitive time as the company prepares for its largest-ever IPO, drawing significant market attention.

At 6:30 PM local time on Friday, SpaceX's upgraded Starship V3 launched from the Starbase facility in southern Texas, conducting the 12th test flight in the Starship series.

The upper ship, Ship 39, successfully reached space, deployed 22 simulated Starlink satellites, and then re-entered the atmosphere before splashing down in the Indian Ocean, completing the mission in about an hour. However, the lower "super-heavy booster" failed to complete the re-entry burn as planned and crashed into the Gulf of Mexico.

This flight was significant for SpaceX. The company plans to launch its IPO as early as June, with potential fundraising reaching $50 billion to $75 billion, which could set a record for the largest IPO in history.

The progress of the Starship program directly supports this valuation logic; any major setbacks could undermine investor confidence.

Upper Ship Reaches Orbit, Booster Falls into Sea

This test flight revealed two engine failures.

Of the 33 engines on the super-heavy booster, one failed during the ascent phase; similarly, one of the six engines on the upper ship also stopped working during the flight.

After stage separation, the booster failed to perform the expected re-entry burn and fell rapidly into the Gulf of Mexico.

Notably, this flight was not designed to have the booster return to the launchpad for capture by a mechanical arm, but rather to simulate a water landing approximately 20 miles offshore.

The upper ship relied on the remaining five engines to extend the burn time and successfully reach space.

SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said in a live stream that the spacecraft trajectory was "within acceptable limits," but "it cannot be considered nominal orbital insertion."

Due to the engine failure, SpaceX canceled the planned re-ignition of the Raptor engine in space, a key technology required for future orbital missions.

The original launch was scheduled for Thursday but was postponed to Friday due to a last-minute issue at the launch tower. Previously, SpaceX had planned to launch on Tuesday but faced another delay.

V3 Version: Nearly a New Rocket

Despite technical anomalies, this flight completed several core mission validations.

Ship 39 successfully deployed all 22 simulated Starlink satellites in space, with a faster deployment rate than previous models, which SpaceX attributed as one of the upgrades in the V3 version.

Two of the satellites, internally referred to as "Dodger Dogs," were equipped with cameras that captured footage of the Starship flying in space after deployment, used to test next-generation Starlink satellite technologies.

SpaceX described the V3 version of Starship as "almost a different rocket," with numerous upgrades compared to its predecessor. Key improvements include:

  • New version of the Raptor engine, more streamlined, lighter, yet more powerful;
  • Super-heavy booster now features three larger grid fins instead of four, to optimize guidance during atmospheric re-entry;
  • Upper ship added docking hardware and propellant transfer systems, laying the foundation for future lunar and deep-space missions.

SpaceX stated that the primary objective of this flight was to "validate these new systems in flight conditions for the first time."

Since this flight was suborbital, if successful, the 13th test flight could become the first time Starship reaches orbit around Earth.

IPO Prospects and Valuation Logic

The technical progress of Starship is closely tied to SpaceX's upcoming IPO.

Market sources indicate that SpaceX plans to list as early as June, with potential fundraising ranging from $50 billion to $75 billion, which could set a global IPO record.

The company's current valuation of $1.25 trillion partly rests on Starship's potential to carry out orbital data centers, crewed lunar landings, and even Mars missions.

However, financial disclosures released by SpaceX last Wednesday showed the company incurred a net loss of over $4.9 billion last year, with an operating loss of $657 million in its space business segment.

In this context, the mixed results of this flight—booster recovery failure and multiple test objectives skipped—will make investors more cautious about the commercialization timeline of Starship.

The progress of Starship also affects NASA's Artemis lunar program.

NASA has commissioned a modified version of Starship as a crewed lunar lander, intended to transport astronauts from lunar orbit to the surface.

According to market sources, due to ongoing delays in Starship development, NASA made significant adjustments to the Artemis plan in February: the Artemis III mission will no longer attempt a lunar landing, but instead conduct docking tests between the Orion spacecraft and the lander in Earth orbit.

The first lunar landing target has been postponed to the Artemis IV mission in 2028. Analysts note that this schedule is extremely tight, and any further major setbacks with Starship could have a cascading impact on the entire crewed lunar mission.

title: Qualcomm Surges 12% to New High, AI-Driven Device Wave Reshapes Valuation
summary: According to market sources, Qualcomm is collaborating with OpenAI to develop AI chips for terminal devices powered by AI agents. On Thursday, Qualcomm reached a chip supply agreement with automaker Stellantis, which includes brands such as Alfa Romeo, Chrysler, Jeep, and Maserati. Market bets on AI edge computing devices have driven Qualcomm's stock to rise 75% over the past month.
content:
Driven by investor confidence in the prospects of AI edge computing devices, automotive chips, and data center business, Qualcomm's stock has reached historic highs, with its core position in the "physical AI" wave being re-priced by Wall Street.

On Friday, Qualcomm's stock surged 12% in a single day, hitting a new all-time high, with a cumulative increase of 75% over the past month. The day before, Qualcomm announced a chip supply agreement with the automotive group Stellantis, while reports indicated that Qualcomm is working with OpenAI to develop AI chips for terminal devices powered by AI agents.

Ivan Feinseth, an analyst at Tigress Financial Partners, maintained a buy rating on Qualcomm, stating that investors are "awakening" to the realization that Qualcomm will return to its former glory and lead the next wave of connected device innovation.

He expressed optimism about the upcoming devices resulting from Qualcomm's collaboration with OpenAI, calling them a "smartphone based on an AI-driven operating system capable of performing any task."

From Smartphones to Everything Connected, Qualcomm Strengthens Its Core Position in Edge AI

Although Qualcomm lags behind industry giants like NVIDIA in providing compute power for AI models and cloud workloads, the company is leveraging its long-standing dominance in the smartphone market to extend its reach into various connected devices such as glasses, cars, and robots, building a core ecosystem around "edge AI."

Qualcomm chips are already embedded in Microsoft Surface PCs, as well as smart glasses from Google and Meta.

Its Arm-based processors are known for their energy efficiency, offering a differentiated competitive advantage over traditional central processors from Intel and AMD, which aligns with the low-power computing needs of edge devices.

Automotive Business Accelerates, Stellantis Partnership Takes Shape

Qualcomm's automotive sector expansion continues to deepen. On Thursday, Stellantis announced it would adopt Qualcomm's Snapdragon processors to provide a unified computing platform for its vehicles, covering the cockpit, in-car connectivity, and advanced driver assistance systems.

Stellantis has a wide range of brands, including Alfa Romeo, Chrysler, Dodge, Fiat, Jeep, and Maserati.

Ned Curic, head of product development at Stellantis, stated during Thursday's investor day that customers will be able to enjoy a "smooth, immersive, and safe autonomous driving experience" on both urban and highway roads, with multiple driving modes available.

This agreement is not an isolated case. Qualcomm has previously signed similar partnerships with Bosch, Volkswagen, Hyundai, and BMW. In its latest quarterly report, Qualcomm's automotive business revenue increased 38% year-over-year to $1.3 billion, with more than one million vehicles running its autonomous driving systems on Qualcomm processors.

Breaking Through in Data Center Chips, New Business Opens Imagination

The significant stock jump on Friday also reflected investor enthusiasm for Qualcomm's new business in data center chips.

Qualcomm announced the launch of customized AI acceleration chips AI200 and AI250 last year. Compared to NVIDIA GPUs, these chips offer higher programmable flexibility and are planned for release later this year in full rack systems, similar to NVIDIA's Vera Rubin and AMD's upcoming Helios system.

Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon stated during a April earnings call that the company will begin shipping data center chips to a "large-scale cloud service provider" this year.

Market expectations suggest that Amon will deliver a keynote speech at the Computex event in Taiwan on June 2, where further developments may be disclosed; Qualcomm's investor day is also scheduled for June 24.
