title: Anthropic's Valuation Could Surpass $90 Billion, Exceeding OpenAI, with Up to $30 Billion in Funding Expected to Close Next Week
summary: Sequoia Capital, Dragoneer Investment Group, Altimeter Capital, and Greenoaks Capital Partners are expected to lead the round, with each planning to invest around $2 billion. Existing investors including Peter Thiel's Founders Fund and General Catalyst are also expected to participate.
content:
Anthropic is set to complete a funding round exceeding $30 billion, with its valuation potentially surpassing $90 billion, surpassing competitor OpenAI and becoming the most valuable artificial intelligence startup globally.

According to reports, Sequoia Capital, Dragoneer Investment Group, Altimeter Capital, and Greenoaks Capital Partners are expected to lead the round, which could be finalized as early as next week.

At the same time, existing investors including Peter Thiel's Founders Fund and General Catalyst are also expected to participate. This round has quickly taken shape within weeks, reflecting strong market demand for the developer of Claude.

Strong fundamentals have supported this high-value financing. Anthropic expects second-quarter revenue to reach $10.9 billion, more than doubling from the previous quarter, while also expecting its first profitable quarter. The company has also informed investors that its annualized revenue run rate will exceed $50 billion by the end of next month.

After this round of financing, Anthropic's valuation will surpass OpenAI's latest valuation of $85.2 billion established in March, making it the world's top AI unicorn. The pricing of this round will have significant reference value for subsequent IPO valuations.

Funding Size Exceeds Expectations, Revenue Surges

The four lead institutions plan to invest approximately $2 billion each, totaling about $8 billion. The total subscription amount for this round has already exceeded Anthropic's initial target of $30 billion, with final terms still being negotiated and subject to potential changes.

The speed at which this round has progressed has drawn market attention. According to reports, Anthropic only began evaluating whether to initiate a new round of financing at the end of April this year, and then officially started contacting investors at the beginning of this month, achieving oversubscription within weeks.

Anthropic's financial performance provides strong backing for its high valuation. The company expects second-quarter revenue to reach $10.9 billion, more than doubling from the previous quarter. It also expects to record its first profit in this quarter.

Its annualized revenue run rate is expected to exceed $50 billion by the end of next month. This metric was only $4 billion last July, representing more than tenfold growth in less than a year.

At an industry conference this month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei stated that the company achieved an "80-fold increase" in annualized revenue and usage in the first quarter, and said the company is "fully committed" to securing more computing power to support business expansion.

Major Investments in Computing Power, Suppliers Become Financing Partners

To meet the rapidly rising demand for computing power, Anthropic has made several major infrastructure investments. The company has signed a $4.5 billion agreement with SpaceX, another $1.8 billion deal with Akamai Technologies to expand computing capabilities, and has also purchased chips and cloud services from Google, part of Alphabet.

Notably, Anthropic is transforming some of its suppliers into financing partners.

Google recently committed to an additional $10 billion investment in Anthropic, valued at $35 billion, matching the valuation from its February round. Google also pledged to invest up to an additional $3 billion if Anthropic meets specific performance targets.

Amazon previously stated it would invest $5 billion in Anthropic at a $35 billion valuation, with plans to add up to $2 billion over time. It remains unclear whether Google and Amazon will participate in this round.

Valuation Surpasses OpenAI, IPO Prospects Attract Attention

This round of financing will enable Anthropic to surpass OpenAI with a valuation exceeding $90 billion. OpenAI had a valuation of $85.2 billion in its March round, and is currently expected to file a confidential draft registration statement soon.

Anthropic is also seen as one of the candidates to go public earliest this fall. The company was founded in 2021 by a group of former OpenAI employees, gradually establishing itself as an industry leader through developing AI tools for enterprises, covering areas ranging from code generation to cybersecurity.

If both companies initiate the IPO process, the valuation established in this round will serve as an important benchmark and may further reshape the market's pricing logic for the AI sector as a whole.

title: AI Computing Power Narrative Behind 58.2 Billion Yuan in Revenue, Super Fusion Seeks Growth Enterprise Board IPO
summary: AI computing infrastructure company Super Fusion has officially stepped onto the capital market stage.
content:
AI computing infrastructure company Super Fusion has officially stepped onto the capital market stage.

On the evening of May 22, the application for the Growth Enterprise Market (GEM) IPO of Super Fusion Digital Technology Co., Ltd. (referred to as "Super Fusion") was accepted and posted online.

The core business of Super Fusion is computing power, mainly focusing on products and services such as data center servers, AI servers, and general computing servers.

In 2023, general computing servers were still the largest revenue source for Super Fusion, accounting for 70.39% of total revenue, while AI server revenue accounted for 25.03%.

However, with the rising demand for large model training, inference, and intelligent computing center construction, AI server revenue has rapidly increased. By 2024 and 2025, the proportion of AI server revenue has remained above 50%, becoming the largest revenue source for Super Fusion.

This structural change has directly driven the rapid growth of Super Fusion's performance scale.

From 2023 to 2025, Super Fusion's revenue was 25.092 billion yuan, 44.267 billion yuan, and 58.246 billion yuan respectively.

From a growth logic perspective, Super Fusion has caught the expansion cycle of AI computing infrastructure. In the past two years, demand for AI servers and other computing infrastructure from major internet companies, operators, financial institutions, and intelligent computing center developers has continuously increased, pushing server manufacturers to shift from traditional general computing markets to AI computing markets.

Super Fusion is trying to seize this window of opportunity in the restructuring of computing infrastructure.

However, Super Fusion is not without pressure.

In contrast to the revenue, net profit attributable to shareholders was 507 million yuan, 722 million yuan, and 1.03 billion yuan in 2023, 2024, and 2025 respectively.

During the reporting period, Super Fusion's net profit margin ranged between 1% and 2%.

The core reason is that Super Fusion faces strong pricing pressure from major internet clients, leading to a bottoming out of gross margin, while also having to bear high R&D and sales expenses.

By 2025, Super Fusion's gross margin was only 8.64%, declining by 1.45 percentage points year-on-year.

With gross margin space significantly compressed, Super Fusion still needs to maintain certain levels of operational promotion and technology innovation investment. In 2025, R&D expenses and sales expenses reached 1.178 billion yuan and 1.308 billion yuan respectively, consuming most of the gross margin.

This IPO, Super Fusion plans to raise 8 billion yuan, mainly invested in the construction of new generation computing infrastructure, smart manufacturing parks, and key technologies related to intelligent computing, AI, and power supply architecture.

Notably, Super Fusion is backed by a group of star shareholders.

As of the date of the prospectus signing, the actual controller of Super Fusion is the Henan Provincial State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission, and its shareholders also include ECH, Harmony Health Insurance, Shenzhen Pengfeng, and China Telecom Investment.

Given the ongoing expansion of AI computing demand, Super Fusion's story has sufficient room for imagination. However, under the current constraints of declining gross margin, strong bargaining power of major internet clients, and intensified competition in the server industry, how to maintain profit quality beyond scale expansion will be a longer-term challenge for this Henan computing unicorn after its listing.

title: The 'Roaring Twenties' Return! Bank of America's Hartnett Warns: SpaceX Super IPO Could Trigger a Historic Bubble
summary: Bank of America strategist Michael Hartnett warned that super IPOs such as SpaceX and OpenAI could push the technology sector's weight in stock indices beyond 48%, surpassing the market concentration levels of historical bubbles including the 1920s 'Roaring Twenties,' the 1970s 'Nifty Fifty,' the 1980s Japanese bubble, and the 1990s tech bubble. Historical experience shows that super IPOs may not act as catalysts but rather as peaks of bubbles.
content:
SpaceX is set to list on U.S. stocks, pushing the entire market to the edge of historic euphoria—and this has triggered an alarm from one of Wall Street's most influential strategists.

In his latest report, Bank of America strategist Michael Hartnett warned that once super IPOs like SpaceX and OpenAI are launched, the weight of technology stocks in stock benchmarks could easily exceed 48%, surpassing the market concentration levels of all major historical bubbles, including the 1920s 'Roaring Twenties,' the 1970s 'Nifty Fifty,' the 1980s Japanese bubble, and the 1990s tech bubble.

Earlier, a Bank of America survey of fund managers showed that investors increased their exposure to U.S. stocks this month at a record pace, with market optimism approaching extreme levels, triggering sell signals.

On the market level, the expectation of SpaceX's listing has sparked a rally in space-related stocks. The basket of core space sector stocks tracked by Bank of America has risen 42% year-to-date, outperforming the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 indices. Analysts have compared this phenomenon to Tesla's role in driving the entire electric vehicle sector higher, but there are also warnings that after the hype subsides, whether smaller names can support their valuations based on fundamentals remains uncertain.

Concentration Alert: Technology Weight Approaching Bubble Threshold

The weight of technology stocks in the S&P 500 index has already exceeded 44%. Hartnett noted that once SpaceX and OpenAI complete their listings, combined with the scale of existing artificial intelligence giants, market concentration will "easily surpass" the peak level of around 48% seen in all previous major bubble periods.

"Strong price movements, retail frenzy, and low volatility... the signs of a bubble are evident," Hartnett wrote in his report. "Adding super IPOs to the AI giant portfolio will easily surpass the 48% level seen during the Roaring Twenties, Nifty Fifty era, Japan's 1980s bubble, and the TMT bubble of the 1990s."

This concentration issue poses a particular challenge for asset allocators. Due to risk management constraints, many institutional investors cannot fully track the high-weighted segments of benchmark indices, and the pressure of passive deviation will continue to increase. Moreover, a highly concentrated index may mask structural weaknesses in sectors such as consumer and financial, which are more closely tied to the real economy.

Historical Lessons: Super IPOs May Not Be Catalysts for the Market

After reviewing several major IPO cases in history, Hartnett pointed out that the listings of Saudi Aramco and Meta (formerly Facebook) had limited impact on the broader market, while offerings during the 'top' periods of Visa and AIG actually led to market declines within 9 to 12 months after their listings.

This historical pattern provides an important reference point for today's optimistic sentiment. Hartnett said that a sharp rise in bond yields has been a common trigger for the end of past booms and bubbles.

He also provided two indicators to watch: if the ETF tracking biotech stocks from State Street falls to $120, it would indicate that bond yields are still rising; if the ETF tracking retail stocks rises to $85, it suggests that the bond shock has temporarily eased.

Hartnett also noted that current market consensus has reached a 'maximum bullish' state, with both positions and earnings expectations at high levels, combined with rising yield pressures, suggesting that investors should consider taking some profits. "But before the historic IPO arrives, no one will cut their long positions," he added, and expects policy tightening to truly take effect after CPI reaches 4% to 5% in the coming months.

Space Sector Mania: The SpaceX Effect Repeats the Tesla Moment

SpaceX formally submitted its IPO application this week, with an estimated valuation range between $864 billion and $2.25 trillion, while Tesla and Meta currently have market caps below $1.6 trillion.

This expectation has already triggered strong resonance in space-related stocks.

The basket of space sector stocks tracked by Bank of America has risen 42% year-to-date, with Procure Space ETF and Tema Space Innovators ETF both recording double-digit returns.

Wedbush analyst Dan Ives called SpaceX's IPO the "golden moment" for the entire space industry, drawing a comparison to how Tesla defined the electric vehicle sector: "It's not just about one company, just as Tesla defined electric vehicles, there is a similar opportunity here to create a new sector."

Tech investor Brett Hurt said that SpaceX's listing is a "huge victory" for the space economy, which will drive up the valuations of other companies and enhance their fundraising capabilities.

After the Hype, Can Smaller Stocks Stand on Their Own?

However, another side of the Tesla effect is also worth caution.

During the electric vehicle boom, Rivian's stock has fallen 92% from its November 2021 peak, and XPeng's American depositary receipts have dropped 78% from their November 2020 high. While Tesla has continued to expand and joined the "Big Tech Seven," the fate of its followers has been different.

Eric Diton, president and managing director of The Wealth Alliance, said that after SpaceX's listing, smaller space companies will face the pressure of proving their value independently: "The market will scrutinize each company individually. My first question is—how do you compete with Musk and SpaceX? Do you have a competitive advantage?"

Professor Eric Talley from Columbia Law School pointed out that investors' fervor toward all of Musk's assets is unlikely to fade, but the issue of Musk's multiple roles across companies and his divided attention is also hard to ignore.

Andrew Chanin, co-founder and CEO of ProcureAM, took a relatively optimistic stance, saying that the space sector is not a 'winner-takes-all' scenario, and the sufficiently broad market space can accommodate multiple successful companies, although failures are also inevitable.

title: Salesforce Accused of Deceptive Marketing Over AI Capabilities
summary: Salesforce's flagship AI product, Agentforce, faces scrutiny over claims that its marketing exceeds actual implementation: major clients such as Williams-Sonoma and Finnair were portrayed as exemplars of 'agentic enterprises,' but core AI features remain in demonstration phase. As stock price continues to face pressure and SaaS growth slows, market doubts about the ability of traditional software giants to deliver on AI promises are growing.
content:
Salesforce's flagship AI product, Agentforce, is facing criticism for a significant gap between its marketing and actual implementation, with several key client showcases featuring simulated demonstrations rather than real-world applications. This issue is intensifying concerns about whether this software giant can maintain its position in the AI era.

According to a Bloomberg report on Friday, Salesforce has presented companies such as Williams-Sonoma, Finnair Oyj, and the University of Chicago Medical Center as examples of 'agentic enterprises' in promotional videos and presentations, but the core AI functions showcased in these cases are not yet in use. For instance, the AI voice customer service line for Williams-Sonoma has not yet been integrated with Agentforce, and Finnair's website explicitly states that the featured functions are merely future plans.

This revelation comes at a particularly bad time for Salesforce. The company's stock has declined by 21% in 2025 and has fallen another 30% this year, making it a typical victim of what the market calls the 'SaaSpocalypse' wave. CEO Marc Benioff defended the company's approach, stating that forward-looking marketing is common in the tech industry, saying, \"Every technology we've marketed has ultimately delivered on its promise.\"

Key Clients 'Endorsing' the Product, But Features Remain in PPT

Bloomberg research shows that several high-profile Salesforce cases have significant discrepancies between marketing and reality.

At a user conference in December 2024, Salesforce marketing executive Sanjna Parulekar demonstrated a voice customer service system driven by Agentforce for Williams-Sonoma, showing a seamless AI experience where the AI automatically identified customers and assisted with purchases. However, about half a year later, the retailer's phone customer service system had still not been integrated with Agentforce, and its online chatbot could not complete orders or modify them without human intervention. Currently, its main functions are limited to providing recipes and checking order status. The company's CTO, Sameer Hassan, said the goal is to integrate Agentforce into the phone system before the holiday shopping season this year.

The situation is similar with Finnair. The company appeared in a video released by Salesforce last year, showcasing an Agentforce-driven scenario where the AI automatically rebooked flights for passengers. However, Finnair's website clearly states that such functionality is "only a future development plan." A company spokesperson said the obstacle lies in another software system that "lacks agentic capabilities."

The University of Chicago Medical Center also appeared in a promotional video released by Salesforce in October 2025, showing patients using Agentforce to seamlessly renew prescriptions, schedule appointments, and even get parking advice. However, according to insiders, these features have not yet been implemented due to product technical issues and delays in internal compliance processes within the healthcare system. The medical system pays millions of dollars in software fees to Salesforce annually.

Benioff: Forward-Looking Marketing Is Industry Practice

In response to the criticism, Benioff defended the company's marketing strategy during an interview. He stated that Salesforce always clearly marks forward-looking content in its marketing, saying, \"I don't want any customer to call me and say, 'I thought I was buying this, but it doesn't exist.'\"

Madhav Thattai, the executive vice president in charge of Agentforce at Salesforce, attributed the delayed implementation to the clients' own processes and compliance issues, not the technology itself. \"You'll see clients start with simpler use cases, and as they develop and implement more complex scenarios, they will gradually achieve their vision of full autonomy,\" he said.

Gil Luria, an analyst at DA Davidson & Co., pointed out that this issue is not unique to Salesforce. \"Under pressure to deliver on AI, many companies are promising things beyond their current capabilities. Salesforce just shouts louder,\" he said.

The Bloomberg report also cited historical precedents, noting that exaggerated marketing has long been a practice in the tech industry - Larry Ellison once named his database product's first commercial version 'Oracle 2' to avoid consumer resistance to the term 'first version.' Earlier this month, Apple reached a $250 million settlement over false advertising claims related to the 'Apple Intelligence' feature.

Agentforce's Real Implementation: Limited Capabilities, Success Cases Focused on Information Processing

Despite the controversy, Agentforce has shown practical value in certain scenarios, but mostly in relatively simple tasks such as information collection and distribution.

The appliance brand SharkNinja reported a 20% reduction in service calls after using Agentforce for automatic product fault detection. European HR firm Adecco Group AG uses Agentforce to handle preliminary written screening interviews for thousands of candidates. The small town of Kyle in Texas uses Agentforce to process resident complaints (such as fixing potholes and removing graffiti), increasing its annual Salesforce spending from about $150,000 to $300,000. PepsiCo said that after using Agentforce to assist in expanding small store operations, its overall Salesforce spending increased by 10%.

However, software industry analyst Rebecca Wettemann noted that Agentforce often struggles when asked to perform more complex tasks, with the fundamental reason being enterprise concerns about AI executing high-value operations autonomously. \"People are worried that AI might refund money overnight or generate huge bills,\" she said.

Slowing Growth, Salesforce Bets on AI to Break Through

The marketing pressure around Agentforce reflects deeper business challenges for Salesforce. The company's annual revenue growth has dropped from 25% in fiscal year 2022 to 10% in the most recent fiscal year, with AI seen as the core engine to revitalize growth.

Salesforce has signed 29,000 Agentforce contracts, with the product generating $800 million in annual recurring revenue. The company says that some clients using Agentforce have at least doubled their annual spending.

On a strategic level, Salesforce is quietly shifting direction. Benioff initially emphasized the ease of deploying Agentforce, but recent company statements have shifted to acknowledging that \"building agentic systems is not easy.\" At a meeting earlier this year, multiple sessions advised clients to look for small and precise AI use cases. Meanwhile, Salesforce is offering free or heavily discounted technical support to clients and strengthening its data integration capabilities through an $8 billion acquisition of Informatica - a prerequisite for AI deployment. Additionally, the company has begun linking salespeople's compensation to actual usage of Agentforce by clients, rather than relying solely on contract signing volume.

However, whether these adjustments will convince Wall Street remains uncertain. The core question in the market is: In the face of emerging AI-native competitors and clients building their own tech teams, can traditional SaaS giants like Salesforce hold their ground - and the current gap between marketing and reality only makes this question harder to answer.

raw.title: Salesforce Accused of Deceptive Marketing Over AI Capabilities
raw.summary: Salesforce's flagship AI product, Agentforce, faces scrutiny over claims that its marketing exceeds actual implementation: major clients such as Williams-Sonoma and Finnair were portrayed as exemplars of 'agentic enterprises,' but core AI features remain in demonstration phase. As stock price continues to face pressure and SaaS growth slows, market doubts about the ability of traditional software giants to deliver on AI promises are growing.
raw.content:
Salesforce's flagship AI product, Agentforce, is facing criticism for a significant gap between its marketing and actual implementation, with several key client showcases featuring simulated demonstrations rather than real-world applications. This issue is intensifying concerns about whether this software giant can maintain its position in the AI era.

According to a Bloomberg report on Friday, Salesforce has presented companies such as Williams-Sonoma, Finnair Oyj, and the University of Chicago Medical Center as examples of 'agentic enterprises' in promotional videos and presentations, but the core AI functions showcased in these cases are not yet in use. For instance, the AI voice customer service line for Williams-Sonoma has not yet been integrated with Agentforce, and Finnair's website explicitly states that the featured functions are merely future plans.

This revelation comes at a particularly bad time for Salesforce. The company's stock has declined by 21% in 2025 and has fallen another 30% this year, making it a typical victim of what the market calls the 'SaaSpocalypse' wave. CEO Marc Benioff defended the company's approach, stating that forward-looking marketing is common in the tech industry, saying, \"Every technology we've marketed has ultimately delivered on its promise.\"

Key Clients 'Endorsing' the Product, But Features Remain in PPT

Bloomberg research shows that several high-profile Salesforce cases have significant discrepancies between marketing and reality.

At a user conference in December 2024, Salesforce marketing executive Sanjna Parulekar demonstrated a voice customer service system driven by Agentforce for Williams-Sonoma, showing a seamless AI experience where the AI automatically identified customers and assisted with purchases. However, about half a year later, the retailer's phone customer service system had still not been integrated with Agentforce, and its online chatbot could not complete orders or modify them without human intervention. Currently, its main functions are limited to providing recipes and checking order status. The company's CTO, Sameer Hassan, said the goal is to integrate Agentforce into the phone system before the holiday shopping season this year.

The situation is similar with Finnair. The company appeared in a video released by Salesforce last year, showcasing an Agentforce-driven scenario where the AI automatically rebooked flights for passengers. However, Finnair's website clearly states that such functionality is "only a future development plan." A company spokesperson said the obstacle lies in another software system that "lacks agentic capabilities."

The University of Chicago Medical Center also appeared in a promotional video released by Salesforce in October 2025, showing patients using Agentforce to seamlessly renew prescriptions, schedule appointments, and even get parking advice. However, according to insiders, these features have not yet been implemented due to product technical issues and delays in internal compliance processes within the healthcare system. The medical system pays millions of dollars in software fees to Salesforce annually.

Benioff: Forward-Looking Marketing Is Industry Practice

In response to the criticism, Benioff defended the company's marketing strategy during an interview. He stated that Salesforce always clearly marks forward-looking content in its marketing, saying, \"I don't want any customer to call me and say, 'I thought I was buying this, but it doesn't exist.'\"

Madhav Thattai, the executive vice president in charge of Agentforce at Salesforce, attributed the delayed implementation to the clients' own processes and compliance issues, not the technology itself. \"You'll see clients start with simpler use cases, and as they develop and implement more complex scenarios, they will gradually achieve their vision of full autonomy,\" he said.

Gil Luria, an analyst at DA Davidson & Co., pointed out that this issue is not unique to Salesforce. \"Under pressure to deliver on AI, many companies are promising things beyond their current capabilities. Salesforce just shouts louder,\" he said.

The Bloomberg report also cited historical precedents, noting that exaggerated marketing has long been a practice in the tech industry - Larry Ellison once named his database product's first commercial version 'Oracle 2' to avoid consumer resistance to the term 'first version.' Earlier this month, Apple reached a $250 million settlement over false advertising claims related to the 'Apple Intelligence' feature.

Agentforce's Real Implementation: Limited Capabilities, Success Cases Focused on Information Processing

Despite the controversy, Agentforce has shown practical value in certain scenarios, but mostly in relatively simple tasks such as information collection and distribution.

The appliance brand SharkNinja reported a 20% reduction in service calls after using Agentforce for automatic product fault detection. European HR firm Adecco Group AG uses Agentforce to handle preliminary written screening interviews for thousands of candidates. The small town of Kyle in Texas uses Agentforce to process resident complaints (such as fixing potholes and removing graffiti), increasing its annual Salesforce spending from about $150,000 to $300,000. PepsiCo said that after using Agentforce to assist in expanding small store operations, its overall Salesforce spending increased by 10%.

However, software industry analyst Rebecca Wettemann noted that Agentforce often struggles when asked to perform more complex tasks, with the fundamental reason being enterprise concerns about AI executing high-value operations autonomously. \"People are worried that AI might refund money overnight or generate huge bills,\" she said.

Slowing Growth, Salesforce Bets on AI to Break Through

The marketing pressure around Agentforce reflects deeper business challenges for Salesforce. The company's annual revenue growth has dropped from 25% in fiscal year 2022 to 10% in the most recent fiscal year, with AI seen as the core engine to revitalize growth.

Salesforce has signed 29,000 Agentforce contracts, with the product generating $800 million in annual recurring revenue. The company says that some clients using Agentforce have at least doubled their annual spending.

On a strategic level, Salesforce is quietly shifting direction. Benioff initially emphasized the ease of deploying Agentforce, but recent company statements have shifted to acknowledging that \"building agentic systems is not easy.\" At a meeting earlier this year, multiple sessions advised clients to look for small and precise AI use cases. Meanwhile, Salesforce is offering free or heavily discounted technical support to clients and strengthening its data integration capabilities through an $8 billion acquisition of Informatica - a prerequisite for AI deployment. Additionally, the company has begun linking salespeople's compensation to actual usage of Agentforce by clients, rather than relying solely on contract signing volume.

However, whether these adjustments will convince Wall Street remains uncertain. The core question in the market is: In the face of emerging AI-native competitors and clients building their own tech teams, can traditional SaaS giants like Salesforce hold their ground - and the current gap between marketing and reality only makes this question harder to answer.

title: Samsung AI Chip Workers Get 40 Times More in Bonuses, Sparking Internal Frustration
summary: A temporary compensation agreement at Samsung Electronics links bonuses to departmental profit contributions, resulting in some memory division employees receiving up to 600 million won (about $440,000), while workers in smartphone, TV, and home appliance divisions receive around 6 million won (about $4,400), creating a nearly 100-fold difference. This disparity has quickly sparked strong reactions within the company, with some employees wearing black ribbons as a form of protest. The Samsung Electronics union began an electronic vote on the temporary pay agreement on May 22.
content:
A bonus agreement temporarily halted a strike at Samsung, but the massive gap in rewards is causing deep internal divisions among employees.

According to Bloomberg, the Samsung Electronics union reached a temporary agreement just 90 minutes before the strike was set to begin, agreeing to distribute 10.5% of operating profits in stock and 1.5% in cash as bonuses, with the allocation directly tied to each business unit's profit contribution.

Under this rule, the gap in bonuses between departments has widened sharply. Some employees in the memory division could receive about 600 million won (approximately $440,000), while workers in the smartphone, TV, and home appliance divisions get only about 6 million won (around $4,400), a hundredfold difference. The huge disparity has quickly triggered strong reactions within the company, with some employees even wearing black ribbons as a form of protest.

According to Xinhua News Agency, the Samsung Electronics union began an electronic vote on a temporary pay agreement on May 22. According to the plan, the electronic voting will continue until 10 a.m. on May 27, with an estimated 89,000 union members participating. If more than half of the members participate and a majority support the agreement, it will be formally implemented; otherwise, the labor-management parties will need to renegotiate.

The union members include nearly 90% chip workers, and the union leadership has declared the negotiation a 'victory'—under the agreement, employees in the memory division are expected to receive about $340,000 in bonuses on average. This labor dispute, which could affect global semiconductor supply, is evolving into an internal battle over interests.

Once a Financial Safety Net, Now a Margin for Bonus Feasts

The huge discrepancy in bonus distribution has become the spark for internal conflicts at Samsung Electronics.

Lee Ho-seo, head of a small union under the Digital Experience (DX) division responsible for smartphones, TVs, and home appliances, said: "Samsung Electronics is one company. Every time we face a crisis, we work together to overcome it. Now that the performance is strong, yet only the departments that generate performance can get bonuses, this doesn't make sense at all."

Behind this controversy lies the long-standing interdependence between Samsung's business units. For decades, the DX division centered around the Galaxy smartphone has been the company's financial safety net. Whenever the semiconductor division enters a downturn, high fixed costs and sharp fluctuations in memory prices often put the chip business under pressure or even cause losses.

During the severe oversupply in the memory market in early 2023, it is reported that the chip division borrowed 20 trillion won from the Samsung Display division to maintain large-scale investments in equipment and R&D. It was the stable profits from the Galaxy series that supported Samsung's continued factory expansion during periods when the chip business was unprofitable, ultimately placing it in a favorable position in the current AI boom cycle.

Division Within the Chip Department Too

The conflict is not limited to the chip and non-chip departments. Within the semiconductor division itself, employees in loss-making business lines such as foundry and system LSI received significantly lower bonuses due to lower performance allocation ratios, leading to criticism of unfairness. These employees argue that they provided an indispensable technical foundation for the success of the memory division.

Samsung Semiconductor CEO Jun Young-hyun wrote in an internal memo this Thursday that the company hopes to "put this period of conflict behind," and urged employees to "stand together again based on mutual respect and trust to achieve greater progress."

title: Xiaohongshu Intensifies Video Content, Fully Launches 'RED Preferred Program'
summary: Traffic allocation shift.
content:
On May 22, Xiaohongshu fully launched the 'RED Preferred Program.'

Different from previous routine iterations, this adjustment involves a restructure of the traffic distribution logic and an upgrade of the product infrastructure: the platform has begun to officially certify high-quality videos and provide traffic allocation advantages; the product side has entered a small-scale internal test for a horizontal video container, displaying videos, text, and comments simultaneously on screen; on the technical side, the platform has fully launched 4K ultra-high-definition and Dolby Atmos surround sound across all functions.

Additionally, the UGC reference and forwarding function was also launched simultaneously.

A relevant official from Xiaohongshu revealed that since the launch, the average exposure of RED Preferred videos has increased from 500,000 to 2.7 million.

Beneath the surface-level product changes and data growth, this platform-level strategic shift is essentially a necessary ecological restructuring by Xiaohongshu ahead of its capital market debut, aimed at supporting its high valuation.

From a content perspective, Xiaohongshu's long-standing image as a 'planting grass' (UGC) platform has created a significant community barrier, but the low entry threshold of the text-and-image format has also led to concerns about content homogenization, duplication, and the prevalence of water armies. Launching 4K and Dolby audio effects, and testing a horizontal long-video container, are typical examples of 'heavy asset' infrastructure construction.

This move points to two business objectives.

First, it raises the content creation threshold. By using technical standards and targeted traffic support, such as single certification marks and exclusive channels on the discovery page, the platform is trying to shift distribution weight from low-barrier general text-and-image content toward high-precision PGC/PUGC video teams, thereby securing the supply of high-quality content in the community.

Second, it extends user dwell time. The design of the horizontal container aims to change users' consumption habits in the text-and-image era—'search and leave' or 'quick scrolling'—and increase the playback duration of medium and long videos.

The UGC reference and forwarding function attempts to establish a social viral and public discussion path within the community, which previously leaned more toward one-way browsing.

The intensification of the video ecosystem reflects the scrutiny of Xiaohongshu's commercialization capabilities by the capital market.

Recent information from the primary market indicates that Xiaohongshu's valuation in the old share transfer market has exceeded $30 billion, with some transactions even reaching a valuation of $50 billion.

Sustaining such a massive valuation would not be sufficient based solely on traditional text-and-image feed advertising and the still-developing 'buying agent e-commerce' model.

Comparing with industry peers, ByteDance can support a valuation of hundreds of billions of dollars, primarily due to the efficient transaction loop built through short videos and live streaming; Bilibili maintains a highly engaged youth-oriented community and brand long-term marketing value through medium and long videos.

The reality Xiaohongshu faces is that video ads have significantly higher premium capacity than text-and-image content, and medium and long videos can better accommodate complex brand marketing requirements.

Comprehensively focusing on video, even experimenting with horizontal medium-length videos, is a necessary piece of the puzzle for Xiaohongshu when telling a new story about 'community, e-commerce, and commercialization.' It not only relates to expanding current ad inventory, but also serves as the cornerstone for future development of live-stream e-commerce and high-ticket brand placements.

Transitioning from a strong text-and-image mindset to a dual-driven approach of text-and-image and video is a relatively aggressive step for Xiaohongshu. Using traffic allocation and technological upgrades to forcibly shift user mindsets tests not only the accuracy of algorithmic distribution but also the platform's ability to balance 'commercialization efficiency' with the original community tone.

This is both a strategic upgrade in product development and a clear move under IPO expectations to meet the capital market's imagination of commercialization ceilings.

title: Decoding ZeeBot: The Logistics Tech Ledger Behind a 'Climbing Robot'
summary: The future will not blindly pursue humanoid designs
content:
Author | Huang Yu

"The payback period domestically is about 18 months, while overseas it could take 5 to 10 years."

This is according to financial media reports, which learned from Bi Jianghua, vice president and general manager of the logistics technology division at Cainiao, about the payback time required for the newly launched ZeeBot climbing robot equipment among domestic and overseas clients.

Looking at this set of data alone, Cainiao should focus its expansion of ZeeBot on the domestic market. However, Bi Jianghua's answer is the opposite: more conservative domestically, but more aggressive overseas.

This seemingly contradictory choice reveals some competitive differences in the logistics technology market between domestic and international markets:

Domestic clients may achieve higher ROI by investing in climbing robots, but the price competition for automation equipment is intense domestically. Overseas clients have a longer payback period, but they calculate total cost of ownership (TCO), and are willing to pay for stability, after-sales service systems, and complete solutions. If the ROI makes sense, their sensitivity to price is relatively lower.

Against the backdrop of global supply chain restructuring, a war has been quietly taking place below the surface. This war is not in the transportation or tariff negotiation phases, but in warehouse efficiency, picking efficiency, and other areas.

Since 2023, Cainiao has entered its 3.0 era, emphasizing marketization and globalization while also making the output of logistics technology capabilities an important business.

Logistics technology is no longer just an internal efficiency tool for Cainiao, but has moved to the front line of market competition. ZeeBot is an important piece of Cainiao's current logistics technology capabilities puzzle, but it also faces intense competition.

Redefining Warehouse ROI

Over the past decade, global warehouse automation has undergone several rounds of technological evolution.

Initially, it was the fixed track shuttle car solution, then Amazon popularized the "goods-to-person" system with underfloor AGVs, followed by CTU (container storage robots) and flying box solutions. They all aim to solve two core issues in warehousing: storage density and picking efficiency.

However, these solutions always had a common shortcoming: low space utilization and lack of flexibility.

For example, the traditional CTU solution relies on the collaboration of a large vehicle and a small one to complete box retrieval and transportation. The large vehicle handles high-level storage, while the small one transports on the ground.

Wang Zhihao, head of the logistics robot team in the logistics technology department at Cainiao, pointed out that the efficiency bottleneck in traditional automated warehouses often lies not in single-machine performance, but in "handover" processes. These include handovers between stackers and conveyors, AGVs and elevators, and robots and people, which are both efficiency loss points and areas of high failure rates.

The core idea of ZeeBot is to integrate "horizontal movement" and "vertical climbing" into a single robot.

According to data published by Cainiao, ZeeBot can move horizontally at a speed of 4 meters per second, and climb vertically to a five-story-high shelf within 10 seconds, significantly increasing storage space utilization by 40% in warehouses.

The Dongguan Muyong Cainiao cross-border warehouse is the first test site for ZeeBot. It was launched in January this year and officially started operations in March. It is still in the "climbing phase" now.

According to financial media reports, as of now, 126 climbing robots have been deployed in the warehouse, with about 60 to 70 actually running. It is expected that during the 618 shopping festival this year, the number of robots will reach 134, marking the first major stress test.

Of course, climbing robots are not the first from Cainiao. Some companies both domestically and internationally have tried similar concepts, but the barriers remain relatively high. Additionally, due to technical instability, and the need for warehouse system upgrades to accommodate climbing robots, specific requirements exist for shelf structure, height, and layout specifications. As a result, the large-scale implementation of climbing robots is still in its early stages.

For Cainiao, this year marks the beginning of large-scale commercial deployment of climbing robots.

Wang Zhihao revealed that in the 2027 fiscal year (April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027), there will be several million-dollar projects for climbing robots within Alibaba alone, and many external projects, with over a dozen companies involved.

According to financial media reports, the main bottleneck for Cainiao's large-scale expansion of climbing robots is not orders, but the inability to meet the production and delivery capacity.

From a market expansion perspective, the greater opportunities for Cainiao's climbing robots lie overseas.

Bi Jianghua told financial media reports that price is a very important factor in the domestic market, but Cainiao does not want to sacrifice too much profit to expand scale in the short term. In the overseas market, the sensitivity to price is not as high, and most companies prioritize a complete after-sales service system and capability, followed by product quality and stability, and finally price.

Accelerating Logistics Technology

About five years ago, Cainiao established an independent logistics technology business unit to accelerate the expansion of external operations.

Within Cainiao, the logistics technology business is currently divided into two major segments: automation and logistics robots, and digitalization and logistics AI applications.

From an application perspective, one category is the sorting scenarios for express delivery, while the other involves dense storage scenarios around industries, retail, and services, as well as automated solutions for e-commerce shipping and collection warehouses.

The logistics automation industry is highly competitive, with companies such as JiZhiJia, Haihe Innovation, Kuaicang, and Hikvision Robotics expanding globally, while Amazon's robotics system continues to iterate.

Despite this, facing the trend of warehouse automation upgrades, increasing investment in logistics robots is an essential path for Cainiao to build core competitiveness.

What Cainiao aims to do is use a single robot to complete all tasks in the warehouse as much as possible.

"We design our products according to the logic of human work in the warehouse," said Bi Jianghua. In the future, the focus will be on AI training to solve the challenge of autonomous picking in non-standard scenarios for robotic arms.

Regarding whether robots in the future warehouse will be humanoid, Bi Jianghua stated that Cainiao designs robot product forms based on logistics operation logic and mode, and will not blindly pursue humanoid designs.

Wang Zhihao told financial media reports that many warehouses are designed for humans, but in a dark factory, those human-operated aspects would not be considered. That is to say, in the future fully automated factories, humanoid robots would abandon some human-like features, such as legs, which are not useful in logistics.

It is easy to imagine: if fast ground movement is needed, it would be wheel-based; if vertical climbing is needed, it would be a climbing arm; and if item retrieval is needed, it would be a specialized gripper or suction cup.

Full automation and unmanned operation are a huge trend in the future of logistics and warehousing.

Bi Jianghua pointed out that the goal is not only to reduce costs, but also to reduce error rates through standardized operations, improve fulfillment certainty, and better address the challenges of labor shortages and management difficulties in overseas markets. "We can see that overseas reliance on robots or automation will be higher."

Financial media reports learned that Cainiao's logistics technology initially focused on domestic expansion, but later also began to push hard overseas. After five years, Cainiao's logistics technology business has already opened up in the overseas market.

Since 2025, Cainiao's logistics technology has accelerated its global expansion, and upgraded its organizational structure into four major regions: Asia-Pacific (including Southeast Asia), Europe, Americas, and Middle East and Africa, and increased the deployment of personnel and local recruitment to ensure project delivery in overseas markets.

As of April 2026, Cainiao's logistics technology has been implemented in nearly 1,100 projects across 29 countries and regions globally.

This means that the target set by Cainiao in 2024 to complete the delivery of 1,000 global technology projects has been achieved ahead of schedule and exceeded.

For Cainiao, ZeeBot is not just a warehouse robot product, but a new breakthrough point in its global logistics technology competition.

However, challenges remain significant. First, the industry's technological iteration is still very rapid, and there is no truly "final product" in the current warehouse robot industry. Whether it is flying boxes, CTU, or climbing robots, they are all still in a phase of rapid evolution.

Second, there are significant challenges in localizing solutions in overseas markets. The differences in warehouse standards across countries are enormous, and it is not easy to truly replicate Chinese efficiency in automation solutions.

Global supply chains are entering a new infrastructure upgrade cycle, and logistics technology is destined to be the core of future competition. Cainiao cannot afford to fall behind in this race.

According to financial media reports, as of now, 126 climbing robots have been deployed in the warehouse, with about 60 to 70 actually running. It is expected that during the 618 shopping festival this year, the number of robots will reach 134, marking the first major stress test.

Of course, climbing robots are not the first from Cainiao. Some companies both domestically and internationally have tried similar concepts, but the barriers remain relatively high. Additionally, due to technical instability, and the need for warehouse system upgrades to accommodate climbing robots, specific requirements exist for shelf structure, height, and layout specifications. As a result, the large-scale implementation of climbing robots is still in its early stages.

For Cainiao, this year marks the beginning of large-scale commercial deployment of climbing robots.

Wang Zhihao revealed that in the 2027 fiscal year (April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027), there will be several million-dollar projects for climbing robots within Alibaba alone, and many external projects, with over a dozen companies involved.

According to financial media reports, the main bottleneck for Cainiao's large-scale expansion of climbing robots is not orders, but the inability to meet the production and delivery capacity.

From a market expansion perspective, the greater opportunities for Cainiao's climbing robots lie overseas.

Bi Jianghua told financial media reports that price is a very important factor in the domestic market, but Cainiao does not want to sacrifice too much profit to expand scale in the short term. In the overseas market, the sensitivity to price is not as high, and most companies prioritize a complete after-sales service system and capability, followed by product quality and stability, and finally price.

Accelerating Logistics Technology

About five years ago, Cainiao established an independent logistics technology business unit to accelerate the expansion of external operations.

Within Cainiao, the logistics technology business is currently divided into two major segments: automation and logistics robots, and digitalization and logistics AI applications.

From an application perspective, one category is the sorting scenarios for express delivery, while the other involves dense storage scenarios around industries, retail, and services, as well as automated solutions for e-commerce shipping and collection warehouses.

The logistics automation industry is highly competitive, with companies such as JiZhiJia, Haihe Innovation, Kuaicang, and Hikvision Robotics expanding globally, while Amazon's robotics system continues to iterate.

Despite this, facing the trend of warehouse automation upgrades, increasing investment in logistics robots is an essential path for Cainiao to build core competitiveness.

What Cainiao aims to do is use a single robot to complete all tasks in the warehouse as much as possible.

"We design our products according to the logic of human work in the warehouse," said Bi Jianghua. In the future, the focus will be on AI training to solve the challenge of autonomous picking in non-standard scenarios for robotic arms.

Regarding whether robots in the future warehouse will be humanoid, Bi Jianghua stated that Cainiao designs robot product forms based on logistics operation logic and mode, and will not blindly pursue humanoid designs.

Wang Zhihao told financial media reports that many warehouses are designed for humans, but in a dark factory, those human-operated aspects would not be considered. That is to say, in the future fully automated factories, humanoid robots would abandon some human-like features, such as legs, which are not useful in logistics.

It is easy to imagine: if fast ground movement is needed, it would be wheel-based; if vertical climbing is needed, it would be a climbing arm; and if item retrieval is needed, it would be a specialized gripper or suction cup.

Full automation and unmanned operation are a huge trend in the future of logistics and warehousing.

Bi Jianghua pointed out that the goal is not only to reduce costs, but also to reduce error rates through standardized operations, improve fulfillment certainty, and better address the challenges of labor shortages and management difficulties in overseas markets. "We can see that overseas reliance on robots or automation will be higher."

Financial media reports learned that Cainiao's logistics technology initially focused on domestic expansion, but later also began to push hard overseas. After five years, Cainiao's logistics technology business has already opened up in the overseas market.

Since 2025, Cainiao's logistics technology has accelerated its global expansion, and upgraded its organizational structure into four major regions: Asia-Pacific (including Southeast Asia), Europe, Americas, and Middle East and Africa, and increased the deployment of personnel and local recruitment to ensure project delivery in overseas markets.

As of April 2026, Cainiao's logistics technology has been implemented in nearly 1,100 projects across 29 countries and regions globally.

This means that the target set by Cainiao in 2024 to complete the delivery of 1,000 global technology projects has been achieved ahead of schedule and exceeded.

For Cainiao, ZeeBot is not just a warehouse robot product, but a new breakthrough point in its global logistics technology competition.

However, challenges remain significant. First, the industry's technological iteration is still very rapid, and there is no truly "final product" in the current warehouse robot industry. Whether it is flying boxes, CTU, or climbing robots, they are all still in a phase of rapid evolution.

Second, there are significant challenges in localizing solutions in overseas markets. The differences in warehouse standards across countries are enormous, and it is not easy to truly replicate Chinese efficiency in automation solutions.

Global supply chains are entering a new infrastructure upgrade cycle, and logistics technology is destined to be the core of future competition. Cainiao cannot afford to fall behind in this race.

title: After GPUs, Huang Renxun Aims to Build a 'CPU Empire'
summary: NVIDIA unveils its first self-developed CPU 'Vera,' expected to generate $20 billion in revenue this year. Analysts note that although the figure may include system integration and complementary memory value, its scale is still sufficient to challenge Intel and AMD's dominance.
content:
NVIDIA, which has dominated the AI chip market with GPUs, is now setting its expansion sights on a field it has never before entered—CPU market.

NVIDIA Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress said during this week's earnings call that the company's first standalone CPU product for artificial intelligence, Vera, opens up a "new" potential market worth as much as $200 billion. She added that NVIDIA already has visibility of nearly $20 billion in revenue from its CPU business this year, and Vera is "driving us to become a leading global CPU supplier."

This statement quickly drew attention from Wall Street. Several analysts pointed out that if the $20 billion projection is fulfilled, it would place NVIDIA directly among the leaders in the CPU market and surpass AMD's revenue in the cloud CPU segment. At the same time, it also means NVIDIA will extend its reach into a market long dominated by Intel, AMD, and Arm.

For competitors such as Arm and Qualcomm who rely on independent CPU architectures, NVIDIA's entry could squeeze already tight capacity and bring substantial impact.

Vera Opens a $20 Billion New Market

Vera was officially launched this March, marking NVIDIA's first standalone CPU product, designed specifically for AI inference and agent workloads, using the Arm architecture. Kress said during the earnings call that hyperscale cloud computing clients and AI system vendors have begun deploying the chip, noting that CPU is a market area NVIDIA has "never before entered."

According to Kress, NVIDIA already has near $20 billion in revenue visibility for its CPU business this year. If this number proves accurate, it would exceed UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri's forecast of about $16 billion in AMD's CPU revenue this year—while AMD currently holds over 50% of the cloud CPU market share.

Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon wrote in a report on Thursday that NVIDIA "seems poised to become a king in the CPU space, with a business size that may even surpass more traditional competitors in the market."

Wall Street: The $20 Billion Figure Needs Interpretation

Analysts generally believe that the $20 billion figure allows for some interpretation and should not be directly compared to traditional CPU revenue metrics.

Arcuri noted that Vera can be used either as an independent chip paired with non-NVIDIA AI chips or sold as a complete system solution including CPU and memory components. Since expensive memory chips are also included in the latter package, the $20 billion projection is "not as straightforward as it seems." He estimates that Vera accounts for approximately 30% of the value in the full system and has lowered his prediction for NVIDIA's actual CPU revenue this year to between $5 billion and $7 billion.

Rasgon, meanwhile, believes the high $20 billion figure may stem from NVIDIA's pricing model based on rack units rather than individual chips. Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore also shares a similar view, saying that the figure "may include CPUs delivered alongside GPU cards, which counts but is relatively easy to achieve." Although Moore acknowledges that the $20 billion target would put NVIDIA at the threshold of market leadership, he notes that his revenue modeling for Intel's data center business (including some network products) remains slightly higher than NVIDIA's.

The Inference Wave Revives CPU Demand

The timing of NVIDIA's move into the CPU market coincides with the accelerating shift of AI applications from model training to inference and agent-based AI paradigms. Unlike the training phase, which heavily relies on GPUs, the inference phase has seen a significant resurgence in demand for server CPUs.

This trend has already brought signs of recovery for Intel, which has been struggling, while Arm Holdings also announced earlier this year its first self-developed CPU chip, specifically targeting inference and agent AI workloads.

Moore said that the Arm architecture CPU NVIDIA is entering differs from the x86 architecture CPU used by Intel, and for x86 chips, it would bring "no additional negative impact."

In the broader competitive landscape, Arcuri warned that NVIDIA's large-scale entry into the CPU space will further consume already tight wafer and memory capacity, having a "negative impact" on the market expansion of companies like Arm and Qualcomm.

Arcuri particularly pointed out that Arm's relationships with wafer foundries and memory suppliers are relatively less mature than NVIDIA's, so the impact may be more direct. Meanwhile, Moore believes that NVIDIA's years of accumulated supply chain bargaining power and procurement priority will allow it to maintain strong competitiveness even in a constrained capacity environment.

title: Microsoft's GitHub Faces Collapse After Years of Downtime and Cyberattacks
summary: GitHub is facing a survival crisis due to leadership vacuum, talent attrition, frequent outages, and security breaches. As AI coding competitors like Cursor erode its market share, developer trust in the platform has plummeted, with internal integration failures leading to 'GitHub's death in name only.' If Microsoft's CoreAI team fails to reverse the trend, GitHub may lose its strategic position as a core infrastructure for global developers.
content:
Eight years after Microsoft's $7.5 billion acquisition of GitHub, the world's largest code hosting platform is now facing a survival crisis. A triple threat of frequent outages, security vulnerabilities, and key talent attrition, compounded by the rapid evolution of AI coding tools, has put its strategic position at risk.

Over the past few weeks, GitHub has experienced multiple major service disruptions and disclosed a critical remote code execution vulnerability; this week, it was revealed that 3,800 internal code repositories had been compromised, stemming from an employee installing a maliciously tampered VS Code plugin. According to interviews with current and former GitHub employees by The Verge, the company is widely suffering from a leadership vacuum and a complete loss of direction.

The turmoil began with the departure of former CEO Thomas Dohmke last summer. Since then, Microsoft has not appointed a successor, forcing GitHub's leadership to report directly to Microsoft's CoreAI team. This structural change has triggered continuous talent attrition—Julia Liuson, Elizabeth Pemmerl, and Jared Palmer have all announced departures or reassignments, with one employee stating, "basically there is no GitHub company anymore."

GitHub's challenges are being seen as an opportunity by competitors. Cursor and Claude Code are already eating into GitHub Copilot's market share; according to The Information, Jay Parikh, the head of the Microsoft CoreAI team overseeing GitHub, has privately warned colleagues that GitHub faces a "serious threat." Meanwhile, developers who had previously been neutral about Microsoft's acquisition are now expressing their dissatisfaction through actions—Ghostty terminal developer Mitchell Hashimoto announced the project's migration away from GitHub, saying, "After 18 years, I have to leave."

Leadership Vacuum, Talent Leaving Rapidly

GitHub's current difficulties can largely be traced back to Thomas Dohmke's departure last summer. Microsoft subsequently integrated GitHub under the CoreAI team, led by Jay Parikh, a former Meta engineering chief brought in by Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. According to media reports citing insiders, Parikh has a poor reputation within Microsoft, and the decision to not appoint a new CEO was his own.

GitHub employees have long prided themselves on their independent culture, calling themselves "Hubbers," but they now have to report directly to teams within Microsoft's system, which has been a difficult adjustment. With revenue functions merged into Microsoft's MCAPS (Customer and Partner Solutions) division and product work split across the Developer Division, some insiders feel the company has already lost its identity. "There is basically no GitHub company anymore," one employee told The Verge last month:

"It's all Microsoft, and the company is collapsing—whether looking at the outages that have severely damaged its reputation or the constant exodus of leadership."

The executive exodus continues to expand. Julia Liuson, who had 34 years of Microsoft experience and previously oversaw GitHub's revenue and engineering operations, left last month. GitHub's former Chief Revenue Officer Elizabeth Pemmerl also submitted her resignation the same month, with Dan Stein, former head of Microsoft's MCAPS division, taking over. In October last year, Jared Palmer joined GitHub as a senior vice president, but he has since announced a move to Xbox, where he will serve as engineering vice president and technical advisor to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. Notably, this new Xbox leader has been recruiting several former Microsoft CoreAI executives, with many interpreting this as a signal that these individuals are eager to escape Parikh's leadership.

Talent attrition has also created direct competitive threats. Thomas Dohmke, after leaving GitHub, founded a new developer platform called Entire, which currently has 30 employees, at least 11 of whom previously worked at GitHub, and its product direction directly competes with GitHub.

Frequent Downtime, CTO Apologizes Publicly

Service stability issues have been particularly prominent over the past year, prompting GitHub CTO Vladimir Fedorov to publicly apologize for recent incidents. Fedorov acknowledged that the surge in pull requests, code commits, and new repository creations has placed a heavy burden on GitHub's infrastructure. "Our priorities are clear: availability first, capacity second, and new features third," he said, adding, "We are reducing unnecessary work, improving caching, isolating critical services, eliminating single points of failure, and migrating performance-sensitive paths to systems specifically designed for such workloads."

Fedorov joined GitHub last year, having spent nearly eight years at Microsoft and over 12 years at Facebook. Shortly after joining, he launched a project to migrate GitHub to Azure servers to address data center capacity bottlenecks, but the complexity of GitHub's MySQL clusters made the risk of outages during migration difficult to eliminate.

Frequent outages have exhausted external developers' patience. Ghostty terminal developer Mitchell Hashimoto wrote in an open letter last month: "GitHub is letting me down every day, which feels very personal... I want to keep writing code, but I can't write code on GitHub anymore. After 18 years, I have to leave." Ghostty then announced its migration away from GitHub.

Outside of service stability, security issues are also putting pressure on GitHub. In March, security firm Wiz Research discovered a critical vulnerability in GitHub's internal git infrastructure using an AI model, allowing attackers to access millions of public and private code repositories. GitHub fixed the issue within six hours.

This week's security incident was even more severe: 3,800 internal code repositories at GitHub were compromised, caused by an employee installing a maliciously altered VS Code plugin. A Microsoft employee pointed out that VS Code frequently pushes notifications for plugin installations, and several plugins with hundreds of thousands of downloads have been removed from the VS Code marketplace after being found to contain cryptocurrency mining programs.

Copilot's Competitiveness Slides, Billing Reform Sparks Backlash

GitHub Copilot once held a first-mover advantage in AI coding assistants, but it has clearly fallen behind its competitors over the past year. According to The Information, Parikh has issued internal warnings about this. Microsoft reportedly considered acquiring Cursor to close the gap and has canceled numerous internal licenses for Claude Code, aiming to encourage its own developers to use GitHub Copilot to accelerate product improvements.

Meanwhile, GitHub is set to introduce a usage-based billing model for Copilot, triggering renewed backlash from developers. Under the new plan, each subscription will include a monthly AI credit allowance, with additional usage requiring separate payment. Unlike the current approach, which automatically downgrades users to lower-capability models upon exceeding limits, the new system will cut off access entirely, raising the cost barrier and causing dissatisfaction among some developers.

As Microsoft faces internal challenges, competitors are accelerating their efforts to target GitHub's developer ecosystem. Entire, Cursor, and Claude Code are all strengthening their product capabilities, viewing GitHub's struggles as an opportunity to reshape the market landscape.

For Microsoft, GitHub's strategic importance goes beyond just a product. It is the decades-long investment in the developer ecosystem that has laid the foundation for Microsoft's status as a software giant. If the CoreAI team fails to effectively reverse the current decline, Microsoft may continue to lose this crucial group that gives it its core competitiveness.

title: AI Giants Line Up for IPOs, Could This Be the Last Party on Wall Street?
summary: This unprecedented wave of IPOs represents the ultimate stress test for AI investment logic and will be the biggest variable in the direction of risk assets this year.
content:
An IPO feast comparable to the peak of the internet bubble is taking shape. Three AI giants, OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX, are racing toward the public market, each with valuations targeting over $1 trillion, and their combined scale could reshape the U.S. stock market.This unprecedented IPO wave is not only the ultimate stress test for AI investment logic but also the biggest variable in the direction of risk assets this year.

On May 22, according to financial media reports, OpenAI has prepared to submit a confidential IPO application to regulators, potentially listing as early as September this year, with a target valuation exceeding $1 trillion and aiming to raise about $60 billion, surpassing Saudi Aramco's 2019 record of $25.6 billion by more than double.

Meanwhile, competitor Anthropic is also advancing its own IPO plans and disclosed that second-quarter revenue is expected to more than double to $10.9 billion, potentially achieving its first quarterly operating profit. Deutsche Bank noted in a research report thatthe way these two IPOs are executed could become a major factor in the direction of risk assets this year, a macro-level theme that must be closely monitored.

However, under the dazzling valuations, the financial fundamentals of the two companies are vastly different. OpenAI generated $5.7 billion in revenue in the first quarter, but its adjusted operating profit margin was -122%, meaning it lost $1.22 for every dollar of revenue, and is expected to achieve positive cash flow as early as 2029 or 2030.Anthropic had $4.8 billion in revenue during the same period, with second-quarter revenue expected to jump to $10.9 billion and an estimated operating profit of about $559 million, having already reached the profit threshold.

Analysts point out that the two companies competing on the same stage exhibit radically different business models, presenting public market investors with a rare dilemma.

The Largest IPO in History: How Shocking Are the Numbers?

Deutsche Bank noted in a report that either OpenAI or Anthropic's IPO would exceed Saudi Aramco's 2019 fundraising amount by more than double, and even after adjusting for inflation, it would easily become the largest IPO in history.

In another report, Deutsche Bank said thatif OpenAI achieves a valuation of over $1 trillion, it would become the 14th largest company in the world, just below Berkshire Hathaway, surpassing Eli Lilly.

Compared to that, Berkshire generated over $370 billion in revenue last year and $67 billion in net income; Eli Lilly had sales of over $65 billion and $21 billion in profit. However, OpenAI is not yet profitable, with annualized revenue of about $30 billion and a workforce of just thousands of employees.

From a market size perspective, Deutsche Bank believes thatthe current U.S. stock market capitalization is about $70 trillion, five times that of the peak of the dot-com bubble, and the market's capacity to absorb is far stronger than in the late 1990s.

At that time, nearly 500 companies went public each year, while in this decade, the average is about 120 companies, and today's listed companies are generally more mature.

Additionally, a $60 billion single IPO is slightly less than the total U.S. IPO fundraising in 1999 and 2000 (both around $65 billion), equivalent to half of the record $119 billion in 2021.

The 'Siphon Effect' of the Giants and Passive Fund Rebalancing

As these giants move into the public market, their liquidity siphoning effect has raised high concerns on Wall Street.

The concentration of SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic's IPOs, combined with Nasdaq's new 'fast-tracking' mechanism, is brewing an unprecedented passive fund rebalancing, i.e., the siphon effect of AI giants.

According to financial media reports, JPMorgan calculated that if SpaceX reaches a $2 trillion valuation and 50% of its shares are publicly traded, passive funds would have to sell approximately $95 billion of existing holdings in the eight major tech stocks on Wall Street (NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Broadcom, Meta, and Tesla) to make room.

Todd Sohn, chief ETF strategist at Strategas, pointed out that due to the typically low initial public offering share ratio of only 5%, and ETFs tracking tens of billions of dollars in assets, this extreme supply-demand imbalance will cause the index inclusion process to be 'somewhat chaotic,' and passive investors may have no choice but to buy at high prices.

Valérie Noël, trading director at Syz Group, stated that the market has already begun betting on pressure on existing large-cap stocks.

According to information disclosed on March 28 this year, OpenAI's public listing would be a substantive vote of confidence in the entire AI investment logic. The information showed that OpenAI's revenue reached $13.1 billion in 2025, but it is expected to post a net loss of $14 billion in 2026.

At the same time, OpenAI has committed to investing about $140 billion in infrastructure construction by 2033.If S&P Global, FTSE Russell, and Nasdaq adopt the fast-tracking rules, it may force about $24 billion to $48 billion in passive funds to buy immediately after the IPO.

Faced with such massive fund restructuring, whether active or passive, ordinary investors' portfolios will be passively reshaped with the change in rules.
