title: JPMorgan's On-the-Ground Research: The 'Monetization Moment' for China's AI Has Arrived, with Workflows Outpacing Base Models
summary: The investment logic in China's AI sector is quietly shifting—model rankings are no longer the core focus, and who controls customer data, workflow access points, and pricing power has become critical. JPMorgan's latest research shows that vertical scenarios with heavy processes and rich data, such as insurance risk control, enterprise data integration, and cross-border marketing, are first to demonstrate commercial value; computing power and infrastructure have become the most certain main line due to increasing model substitutability; consumer-level AI still lacks a solid revenue proof.
content:
The investment logic in China's AI industry is undergoing a subtle shift: markets previously focused on model capabilities, parameters, and rankings, but now should pay more attention to who controls customer data, workflow access points, deployment capabilities, and pricing power. Eight meetings covering autonomous driving, independent model development, enterprise workflow software, and vertical AI applications have provided a common signal: models remain important, but in some enterprise scenarios, models are beginning to act like replaceable input items.

According to market observers, JPMorgan Securities (China) analysts Yao Cheng and others stated in their May 22 report on the Chinese AI industry that "some AI applications are showing early signs of commercial value, particularly in vertical areas with intensive workflows and abundant data." The key point of this statement is not that AI applications finally can generate revenue, but rather where this revenue begins to emerge: not in general chat or simple API calls, but in scenarios such as insurance and financial risk, enterprise data integration, and cross-border marketing, which are process-heavy, data-rich, and result-measurable.

This also changes some assumptions about autonomous driving and application layers. Previously, a more conservative framework was: "Robotaxi is more of a cost center in the short term, and AI application monetization is still early; the clearest public market exposure lies in infrastructure and computing power." Now, ADAS is closer to mass production and scaling, and there are claims of city-level economic improvements in some L4 autonomous driving deployments. Vertical AI applications are also beginning to show early evidence of recurring revenue, value-based pricing, and operational profitability. However, these evidences mostly come from management statements, and many companies are not yet publicly listed, so they are still far from auditable and replicable public market validation.

The investment implications have become more concentrated: computing power, AI infrastructure, domestic chips, memory, and storage are the least risky directions that do not require betting on the success of a single large model. For the application layer, look at proprietary data, workflow ownership, customer retention, and pricing power; model companies must prove they are not just being called upon, but can control high-value workflows. Consumer-level AI and intelligent e-commerce have not yet provided sufficient hard evidence of payment, retention, and transaction growth, and valuation stories still need to be discounted.

Model capabilities remain important, but the moat of pure API selling is thinning

The most consistent signal comes from enterprise scenarios: customers care about whether tasks can be completed, whether they can be embedded into existing processes, and whether they can leverage their own data, rather than necessarily using the largest model.

Some companies are already allocating requests to different domestic models and cutting-edge models based on price, performance, and specific tasks. Some companies have admitted that the switching cost of pure APIs is not high, and what truly keeps customers is enterprise data integration, workflow transformation, and post-deployment business stickiness.

This is uncomfortable for model layer valuations. Usage growth can continue to exist, but whether the rent stays with model vendors becomes another issue. If customers can switch models with low friction, the pricing pressure of general APIs will become increasingly obvious.

Of course, models are not without value. In tasks such as coding, intelligent agents, and enterprise software automation, reliability, context length, tool calling ability, and multi-step task completion rate directly affect business outcomes. If model companies can control user interfaces, workflow memory, and data feedback loops, they still have the opportunity to retain economic value in high-value scenarios.

The earliest monetizable applications are not general AI, but vertical scenarios with heavy processes and rich data

Insurance and financial services risk, enterprise data integration, and cross-border marketing are the strongest signals in this round. Their commonality is clear: customers pay not because they "used AI," but because of reduced risk, improved efficiency, better marketing conversion, and automated decision-making.

These scenarios are easier to value. As long as results are measurable, suppliers have the opportunity to convert AI capabilities into recurring revenue, rather than one-time project fees.

However, it is not possible to directly apply traditional software valuation logic. Some businesses may still have strong service attributes: high concentration of major clients, small share in the client's wallet, and early deployment requiring significant manual implementation or assistance. If these costs are fully accounted for, gross margins and scalability may not appear as good as they seem.

Therefore, a more accurate judgment is: some AI applications have moved from narrative to early commercial validation, but have not yet proven they possess sustainable, scalable software economics.

The computing power mainline is actually clearer: the more replaceable the model, the more infrastructure becomes a common winner

If enterprises use multiple models, the exclusivity of models will decrease, but the demand for computing power, storage, memory, cloud orchestration, and inference infrastructure will not disappear.

This is where the infrastructure logic becomes clearer. Regardless of which model eventually leads, training, inference, enterprise deployment, ADAS development, simulation, data processing, and managed services all consume computing resources. Model competition may even increase the frequency of experiments and deployments, thereby driving up inference and supporting infrastructure demand.

The key assumption is task volume elasticity. An optimistic scenario requires AI task volume growth to outpace the decline in per-task costs. If model efficiency, sparse computing, edge inference, or architectural improvements cause unit computing power consumption to drop faster, the benefits to infrastructure could be weakened.

Currently, this framework leans more towards the former: demand is expanding from cutting-edge training to inference, domestic technology stack adaptation, memory, storage, and enterprise workflow execution. For the public market, this remains the clearest AI exposure.

Autonomous driving is no longer just a cost center, but L4 is not yet ready

The change in autonomous driving lies in the fact that the previous narrative of pure money burning is starting to loosen.

ADAS and L4 Robotaxi should be viewed separately. ADAS, relying on vehicle manufacturers' mass production, real road data cycles, and software-style bulk profit potential, is closer to scaling. Suppliers can follow car manufacturers' adoption rates to form more visible revenue contributions.

L4 Robotaxi is still much earlier. Some operators have claimed improvements in city-level economics, lower vehicle costs, and better economic viability for overseas deployment, but company-level profitability remains a later goal, and regulatory thresholds have not disappeared. Successfully operating in one city does not mean it can be replicated across different geographies, weather conditions, and regulatory environments.

For L4 companies, the evidence that can truly change investment feasibility is very specific: city-level audit-able unit economics, license expansion to new cities, continuous reduction in vehicle costs, safety records, and regulatory continuity. Any accident that triggers a license suspension could push the commercialization process back by several quarters.

Neutral professional companies can enter carmakers and enterprises, but platforms may not dominate the application layer

Platforms originally had cloud, traffic, ecosystems, and distribution interfaces, and appeared to be able to capture most of the value of AI applications. However, neutrality is becoming a variable in enterprise and automotive procurement.

Some non-platform models or application companies are able to enter整车厂 (vehicle manufacturers) and enterprise orders not because they have a larger ecosystem, but because customers view them as more customizable and neutral suppliers. Platform clouds, maps, and infrastructure can still be used as input layers, but deployment contexts and customer workflows may be controlled by neutral professional companies.

This does not weaken the logic of platforms like Tencent and Alibaba benefiting from cloud, maps, computing, and data infrastructure. What needs to be clearly distinguished is: when platforms act as infrastructure suppliers, and when they take orders in the application layer, these are two separate things.

When customers prioritize neutrality, customization, and deep integration, platform models may not have an inherent advantage. Procurement decisions will depend more on trust, integration depth, and vertical delivery capabilities.

Consumer-level AI and intelligent e-commerce still lack a solid revenue proof

Current evidence for consumer-level AI is weak. Common issues include low user loyalty, fierce competition, insufficient willingness to pay, and rapid product imitation.

Intelligent e-commerce and AI advertising are also in an earlier stage. In cross-border marketing, current optimization is mainly driven by recommendation algorithms, and large language model-driven intelligent agent commercialization has not yet provided sufficient verifiable revenue evidence.

What needs to be observed here is not download numbers, product launches, or demonstration effects, but retention rates, payment conversion rates, repeat usage rates, gross margins, and measurable transaction increments. Without these metrics, the story of consumer-level AI will struggle to support higher valuations.

The real test is retention, pricing, and gross margin, not the AI narrative itself

For model companies, the key question over the next few quarters is: after customers route through multiple models, can the model layer continue to capture value? An optimistic scenario requires seeing rising net retention, stable or improving pricing, low churn, and stable gross margins in the face of multi-model competition.

Coding may be the clearest test scenario. It is frequent, its value is quantifiable, and it has potential for developer interface lock-in. Model-leading entities like Zhipu and MiniMax cannot rely solely on benchmark test performance, but must also prove vertical scenario capabilities, workflow control, and repeatable usage quality.

For application companies, the key metrics are revenue quality, customer concentration, implementation intensity, net retention, pricing structure, and true gross margin after deducting customer support and manual assistance.

For infrastructure companies, the key is whether they can more clearly attribute growth to inference, deployment, and domestic chip compatibility. If task volume expansion continues to outpace the cost reduction from efficiency improvements, computing power, domestic chips, memory, and storage will remain the clearest AI mainline.

title: Iran's Parliament Speaker: Iranian Armed Forces Reorganized During Ceasefire
summary: Iran's Islamic Parliament Speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, met with visiting Pakistani Army Chief General Muhammad Asim Munir on Tuesday. According to Iranian sources, the two sides discussed the latest developments in negotiations. Ghalibaf stated that during the previous ceasefire mediated by Pakistan, the United States 'betrayed' the process by launching a maritime blockade. Additionally, Ghalibaf said that during this temporary ceasefire, the Iranian armed forces underwent reorganization and restructuring. Ghalibaf also warned the United States that if the U.S. government made another mistake and restarted the war, it would face more severe consequences.

title: 3 Trillion Yuan Era: Quantitative Hedge Funds Enter a Survival Competition
summary: Zhejiang Securities noted that the 3 trillion yuan threshold has been crossed, and quantitative hedge funds have officially transitioned from a race to a survival competition. The median excess return of the 500 index enhancement strategies is approaching zero, with the gap between the 90th and 10th percentile managers expanding to 20%. Top institutions are consuming their own excess returns through scale expansion, and the ongoing drawdowns in quantity and price factors have yet to be repaired. Where will the excess returns come from, and why are the drawdowns occurring? These questions have become more critical screening criteria than historical rankings.
content:
The scale of quantitative hedge funds has passed a key threshold. Calculations show that by the end of 2025, the scale of quantitative funds reached 3.22 trillion yuan, accounting for over 43% of private securities investment funds; in 2020, this scale was only 0.76 trillion yuan. The fastest-growing segment is equity quantitative strategies: index enhancement, stock neutrality, and quantitative stock picking account for over 80%.

Chen Olin and colleagues from Zhejiang Securities' financial engineering team pointed out in a report on May 21: "At the 3 trillion yuan scale, the current phase has shifted from a race to a survival competition, and the stability of strategy excess returns may be the core competitiveness of fund managers." The focus is not on the scale itself, but on the changes that follow: excess returns are no longer easily obtainable, and the gaps between fund managers are rapidly widening.

The most striking data comes from the divergence. Under estimated calculations for the first half of 2026, the difference in excess returns between the 90th and 10th percentile managers of private 500 index enhancement products has widened to about 20%, while the gap between the 70th and 30th percentiles is also close to 8%. More importantly, the median is near zero, indicating that a significant portion of products are not outperforming the price index.

Drawdowns have also become harder to explain. Since 2024, the volatility and frequency of excess returns in index enhancement products have increased. By August 2025, low volatility, momentum, small-cap, and liquidity factors all showed significant drag, while the growth factor contributed positive excess returns. It is no longer sufficient to summarize performance differences with just one or two style tags.

The Larger the Scale, the Thinner the Excess

From 2020 to 2025, the total scale of private securities investment funds rose from 4.3 trillion yuan to 7.45 trillion yuan. Quantitative funds were the main source of growth, increasing from 0.76 trillion yuan to 3.22 trillion yuan; non-quantitative funds rose from 3.54 trillion yuan to 4.23 trillion yuan, experiencing years of contraction in between.

Within quantitative strategies, index enhancement remains the largest strategy line, with a scale of about 1.19 trillion yuan at the end of 2025, accounting for nearly 40% of the total quantitative strategy scale. Stock neutrality reached about 0.74 trillion yuan, quantitative stock picking about 0.54 trillion yuan. Quantitative CTA reached 0.37 trillion yuan, while quantitative arbitrage and quantitative options reached 0.11 trillion yuan and 0.03 trillion yuan respectively.

After the scale expansion, pressure on excess returns began to emerge.

From early 2019 to February 2026, the cumulative excess returns of the three major broad-based index enhancement strategies remained upward: 1000 index enhancement about 141%, 500 index enhancement about 109%, and 300 index enhancement about 94%. However, since 2024, the fluctuations have become significantly larger: the 300 index enhancement had negative excess returns in 2024, while the 500 index enhancement experienced continuous drawdowns after July 2025, and the slope of the 1000 index enhancement's excess returns also slowed down.

This change coincided closely with the scale expansion rhythm. From 2020 to 2021, the quantitative scale doubled from 0.76 trillion yuan to 1.46 trillion yuan, and the excess returns of the three major index enhancements fell across the board, with the 1000 index enhancement's excess return dropping from 18.2% to 6.6%. From 2022 to 2023, the scale remained relatively stable, and the excess returns recovered somewhat. In 2024, the scale approached 2 trillion yuan, and the 300 index enhancement's excess return turned negative, while the 500 and 1000 excess returns also dropped to low levels. In 2025, the scale jumped to 3.22 trillion yuan, and the three major index enhancements' excess returns rebounded, but this was largely masked by the extreme small-cap style in the first half of the year.

Advantages of Leading Managers Can Also Be Eaten by Scale

Scale is an enemy of excess returns, and this holds true even for leading managers.

Take H Quantitative as an example. During its explosive performance period from 2019 to 2021, its relative excess return to the same strategy average reached a peak of about 30%. But as the management scale topped out, the excess return narrowed significantly after 2022, returning to near the industry average.

K Investment followed a similar path. During its rapid scale expansion from 2023 to 2024, it still maintained a clear excess return advantage, but after 2025, its relative advantage began to decline, gradually approaching the average of similar strategies; entering 2026, it even showed a slight underperformance compared to the industry average.

This means that the logic of selecting based on top-tier labels is becoming ineffective. The bigger the scale, the harder it is to avoid issues like strategy capacity, trading congestion, and factor decay. Whether a manager can generate excess returns is one thing, and whether they can maintain those returns after expansion is another.

Divergence Is Not Just at the Extremes, the Middle Layer Is Also Beginning to Diverge

In the estimated data for the first half of 2026, the most noteworthy aspect is not the gap between the strongest and weakest, but that the middle layer is also beginning to diverge.

Among private 500 index enhancement products, the difference in excess returns between the 90th and 10th percentiles is approximately 20%, which has approached or even exceeded the extreme level of the same period in 2024. The gap between the 70th and 30th percentiles is about 8%, indicating that the gap is not limited to a few tail-end products but has spread to a broader range.

The median being near zero indicates that the cost of choosing the wrong product has increased. The core selling point of index enhancement products in the past was stable excess returns, but this premise is no longer solid. Simply looking at historical annualized excess returns can misinterpret style dividends as management ability; focusing only on short-term rankings can lead to purchasing drawdowns after style switches.

A more effective question becomes: where do the excess returns come from? When drawdowns occur, is it due to factor failure, or is the portfolio exposure too concentrated? If the latter, the recovery speed usually does not depend solely on market rebounds.

Alpha Sources Are Narrowing, Quantity and Price Factors No Longer Favorable

Behind the performance divergence lies a change in alpha factor structure.

Before 2026, among the four categories of factors—fundamental, analyst expectation, quantity and price, and high-frequency and low-frequency—usually at least three could provide stable positive excess returns. When multiple factors were effective simultaneously, managers using different methodologies could find sources of returns, and thus the performance gaps naturally would not be large.

In recent years, the situation has changed. Those still maintaining positive excess returns are mainly fundamental factors and analyst expectation factors; quantity and price factors, along with high-frequency and low-frequency factors, have been in continuous drawdown since August 2025 and have yet to show a trend toward recovery.

The central tendency of excess returns has also clearly declined. Before the third quarter of 2025, the annualized excess returns of the CSI 500 and CSI 1000 index enhancement strategies were approximately 10% and 13%, respectively; since the third quarter of 2025, the CSI 500 index enhancement has dropped to about 0.75%, and the CSI 1000 index enhancement only about 4.5%.

This directly amplifies differences between fund managers. Combinations with higher proportions of fundamental factors and more balanced factor structures recover from drawdowns faster. For example, Fund Manager Y: with over 30% fundamental factors and about 50% quantity and price factors, the current excess drawdown has recovered to around 0.7%. In contrast, combinations represented by K have tens of thousands of real-time factors, with over 90% being quantity and price factors; when quantity and price factors experienced drawdowns after August 2025, the excess drawdown was greater than the market average and has yet to complete the recovery.

The Main Cause of Drawdowns Is Often Not That the Factors Have Failed

To explain the index enhancement drawdown, simply looking at factor movements is insufficient. A more direct approach is to categorize the stock pool by size and residual volatility: large-cap, mid-cap, small-cap, then overlay high-volatility and low-volatility to form six style domains. This allows the excess drawdown to be split into two parts: deviation of the stock pool, and the factor excess within the stock pool.

Taking the CSI 500 enhancement as an example, the excess drawdown in the drawdown period from August 8 to September 30, 2025, was -4.13%. Within the same period, the low-volatility factor had a drawdown of -8.32%, momentum factor -6.95%, small-cap factor -7.22%, and liquidity factor -5.33%; while the growth factor was +2.60%.

This indicates that the drawdown is not due to all factors failing simultaneously. The directional differences among different factors are significant, and the composition of the portfolio determines how much impact the net value ultimately suffers.

The breakdown of the liquidity factor better illustrates the issue. From August 8 to September 1, 2025, the related portfolio had a drawdown of -3.75%, of which the deviation of the stock pool contributed -3.11%. The deviation within the CSI 500 alone contributed -3.77%, while allocation to other stock pools contributed +0.66%. Looking at the factor excess within the stock pool, the total was -0.70%, while the other stock pools totaled -0.14%.

In other words, this drawdown was primarily not due to the liquidity factor failing severely across all stock domains, but rather the deviation of the portfolio relative to the benchmark dominated the losses, especially the deviation within the benchmark itself.

The Next Round of Screening for Quantitative Hedge Funds Will Be More Rigorous

After reaching 3 trillion yuan, quantitative hedge funds will still be an important force in private securities funds, but the turning point of the industry has changed.

The previous core issue was whether excess returns could be generated, but now there are two additional layers of questions: whether the excess returns rely on a single style, and whether they can be maintained after scale expansion; when drawdowns occur, are they short-term factor disturbances, or has the portfolio structure exposed unmanageable deviations?

This is the meaning of the survival competition. Not all managers will disappear, but under the same index enhancement label, the product curves may be completely different. Excess return stability, risk control capabilities, and factor structure balance will be more important than historical rankings.

It is necessary to retain a boundary: the above returns and drawdowns are calculated based on specific testing periods and samples, and do not represent future results. If the future market data distribution differs from historical patterns, the model may also fail. This article does not constitute a recommendation for fund products, nor does it involve recommendations for any holding stocks.

title: ECB Council Member: Central Bank May Unavoidably Raise Rates to Safeguard Policy Credibility
summary:
Yannis Stournaras, a member of the European Central Bank's Governing Council, said at a European finance ministers' meeting in Nicosia, Cyprus, that safeguarding the ECB's policy credibility is a strong rationale for raising interest rates next month.

"Raising rates comes with costs - for ordinary people and employment alike - which is why I sincerely hope we don't have to get to this point. But if the current impasse continues while we remain inactive, the consequences would be disastrous. For the ECB's credibility and our response mechanism, we may have to raise rates in June," he said.

title: Micron CEO: Memory Shortage May Last Beyond 2026, New Capacity Won't Be Fully Available Until 2028
summary: Recently, Sanjay Mehrotra, CEO of US memory chip manufacturer Micron, warned in an interview with foreign media that the current global memory shortage could last beyond 2026, and the industry's true large-scale new capacity release will not be available until at least 2028. "Building the factory infrastructure is currently the longest and most challenging part of the cycle. Even after the civil construction is completed, the equipment installation and commissioning also require a long period," Mehrotra admitted during an interview at his company's Manassas, Virginia plant. The factory has just launched the first DRAM mass production using the '1-alpha' process node in the US, which marks a key step for Micron to bring advanced memory manufacturing back to the domestic market.

content:
On May 23, Changzhi City, Shanxi Province held a press conference to provide details on the gas explosion accident at Lushenyu Coal Mine of Tongzhou Group.
At the meeting, relevant officials stated that the nature of this accident is extremely serious and its impact is extremely negative. We will deeply reflect and remain highly alert, and comprehensively carry out a sweeping inspection in the coal industry.
First, strictly investigate the gas extraction system, focusing on inspecting the extraction equipment and facilities to ensure the integrity of the extraction system, and strictly enforce the principle of 'no extraction, no mining' and 'no production if extraction standards are not met'.
Second, strictly investigate the safety monitoring system, ensuring the system is connected 24 hours a day, data is uploaded in real time, sensors are intact and effective, and it is strictly prohibited to delete monitoring data.
Third, strictly investigate the ventilation system and facilities, ensuring an independent, stable, and reliable ventilation system is established, and it is strictly prohibited to work under conditions of no air flow, weak air flow, or recirculated air flow.
Fourth, conduct a thorough inspection of all underground tunnels, chambers, mined-out areas, coal zones, and old mined-out areas, focusing on verifying whether there are hidden working faces not included in the system, personnel without positioning cards, and areas not covered by monitoring.
Fifth, focus on special inspections in key industries such as hazardous chemicals, non-coal mines, road traffic, and fire safety, and further promote the investigation and rectification of risk hazards.
At 7:29 PM on May 22, a gas explosion occurred at Lushenyu Coal Mine of Tongzhou Group in Qinyuan County, Changzhi City, Shanxi Province, causing major casualties.

title: Jiu'an Medical: No Separate AI Business Charges, Diabetes Care Revenue Makes Up a Small Share
summary: Jiu'an Medical announced on May 25 that its stock price fluctuation exceeded 20% over three consecutive trading days, constituting an abnormal trading situation. The company's diabetes diagnostic and care business and the 'AIoT Diabetes Home Healthcare Assistant' project involve the application of AI tools, but they are not separately charged and do not constitute a standalone business segment. In 2025, revenue from this business was approximately 122 million yuan, accounting for 8.93% of total revenue, which is relatively low and does not significantly impact the company's performance.

title: Xingyun Technology: Subsidiary Xingyun CunSuan Signs 322 Million Yuan Equipment Sales Framework Agreement with Zhejiang Shenhu
summary: Xingyun Technology announced that its subsidiary Xingyun CunSuan (Shenzhen) Technology Co., Ltd. has signed a 'Equipment Sales Framework Agreement' with Zhejiang Shenhu Technology Co., Ltd., under which Xingyun CunSuan plans to sell enterprise-grade SSD drives to Zhejiang Shenhu, with a total tax-inclusive amount of 322 million yuan.

title: Global Confidence in Germany is Fading: Foreign Investment Projects Hit Lowest Level Since 2009, Eight-Year Decline Continues
summary: According to EY data, foreign investors announced only 548 new projects in Germany in 2025, a 10% decrease compared to the previous year, marking the eighth consecutive year of decline and reaching the lowest level since 2009. The leader of the German Alternative Party (AfD) stated, 'The world is losing trust, and foreign companies are investing less in Germany.' Structural issues such as high tax burdens and expensive energy costs continue to erode Germany's competitiveness, with reforms showing little progress, leading to a rapid loss of foreign investment appeal.

title: Joint Statement Between the People's Republic of China and the Republic of Serbia on Jointly Promoting the Implementation of the Four Global Initiatives
summary: Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to continuously advance the process of economic globalization, safeguard the stability of global industrial chains and supply chains, uphold an open, inclusive, transparent, and non-discriminatory multilateral trading system centered on the World Trade Organization, support the evolution of world trade rules, and promote the liberalization and facilitation of trade and investment.

title: The Hidden Truth Behind the AI Boom: The 'Cyclical Billing Game' Behind Trillions in Cloud Revenue
summary: Technology giants and AI startups are forming a 'cyclical revenue loop': investment funds flow back through cloud service contracts, creating new cloud revenue and profit growth. Over half of the $2 trillion cloud orders from Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Oracle are dependent on OpenAI and Anthropic, while balance sheet profits have risen sharply, but free cash flow has deteriorated significantly. This investment-consumption cycle has amplified the AI boom narrative, raising concerns about the authenticity of profits and systemic bubble risks.

title: Philippines and EU Aim to Complete Free Trade Agreement Talks in June
summary: According to reports, the Philippines and the European Union plan to conclude negotiations on a free trade agreement (FTA) in June and aim to announce the signing of the pact by the end of the year. Raul Guinevere, Deputy Secretary of the Department of Trade and Industry, stated that both sides are currently conducting the sixth and final round of talks, and have 'substantially completed' several chapters, including those on small and medium enterprises, transparency, anti-fraud rules, sustainable food systems, good regulatory practices, and trade and sustainable development.

title: Storage Capacity Can't Keep Up! Micron Warns of Supply Shortages Beyond 2026
summary: At the JPMorgan Technology Summit, Micron indicated that supply tightness for HBM, DRAM and NAND is expected to persist beyond 2026, driven by strong AI demand. Structural bottlenecks in performance improvements, larger die sizes and EUV ramp-up constraints are limiting supply expansion. Even with aggressive capacity building efforts, it will be difficult to quickly close the supply gap created by AI demand in the short term.

title: Philippines Needs Additional 20 GW of Renewable Energy to Meet 2040 Target
summary: According to market sources, to achieve a target of 50% renewable energy supply by 2040, the Philippines Department of Energy stated that, in addition to approved projects, the country needs to add an extra 20 gigawatts (GW) of renewable energy capacity. Currently, clean energy accounts for only 25% of the power mix, falling short of the 35% intermediate target for 2030. To address this, the government is accelerating the Green Energy Auction (GEA) program to attract private investment. This year's bidding will focus on offshore wind, biomass, and waste-to-energy sectors, with an emphasis on Mindanao and the Visayas region to meet growing electricity demand and optimize the national grid structure.

title: PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng Meets with French Central Bank Governor De Guingand
summary: PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng met with French Central Bank Governor De Guingand on May 25, exchanging views on global and economic conditions in China and France, Sino-French and Sino-EU economic and financial cooperation, as well as global financial governance. Pan Gongsheng stated that under the strategic guidance of the leaders of China and France, Sino-French relations and cooperation have achieved positive progress in recent years. Currently, the global economy faces multiple challenges including geopolitical conflicts, and Sino-French and Sino-EU efforts should strengthen strategic communication to jointly safeguard multilateralism and work together to build a more fair, just, inclusive, and resilient global financial governance system. China remains committed to advancing the opening-up of its financial sector and welcomes financial institutions from countries including France to deepen their presence in the Chinese market. The PBOC is willing to continue deepening exchanges and cooperation with the French Central Bank to promote Sino-French and Sino-EU financial cooperation to new heights.

US stocks will be closed for one day due to a holiday.
Syzran Oil Refinery suspended operations following an attack.

title: 6G Trial Frequencies Approved, 6G Expected to Enter Commercial Use by the Early 2030s
summary: Recently, the 6GHz frequency band has been approved by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, making China the first country in the world to approve trial frequency usage for 6G. Following this approval, 6G technology research and development will move from laboratory simulations and indoor prototype testing to real-world scenarios such as cities and industries for performance validation. According to the schedule, China has completed the first phase of key 6G technology trials between 2022 and 2025, and is now launching the second phase of technical solution trials. In the future, international efforts will need to finalize the first version of the 6G standard. Industry experts generally expect that 6G could enter commercial use by the early 2030s.

title: Veteran Market Analyst Jeff Currie Warns: Asian Oil Market Is Near 'Tanker Bottom,' Europe to Follow
summary: Senior market strategist Jeff Currie warned that global surface stock data may be misleading, as most of the oil stored globally cannot be immediately put into use. Currie, chief strategy officer for Carlyle's energy transition division and co-chairman of Abaxx Markets, noted that the Asian oil market is already very close to these so-called minimum operating levels, with Europe likely to follow soon, while the U.S. may face supply shortages by July. The remarks further highlight the energy shock caused by the Iran conflict.

title: China's Chamber of Commerce President Ren Hongbin Meets with Singapore Minister for Law and Home Affairs Tang Zhenhui
summary: China's Chamber of Commerce President Ren Hongbin met with a delegation led by Singapore Minister for Law and Home Affairs Tang Zhenhui in Beijing. The two sides exchanged views on promoting exchanges between Chinese and Singaporean business communities, enhancing cooperation in commercial law, and jointly organizing the sixth China-Singapore International Commercial Dispute Resolution Forum. Both sides signed a Memorandum of Understanding on legal and dispute resolution cooperation between the China Chamber of Commerce and the Ministry of Law of Singapore. Deputy President Liu Jianan attended the meeting.

title: Mexico's exports hit record high of 72 billion dollars in April
summary: Mexico's trade surplus expanded to 4.52 billion dollars in April, far exceeding the estimated median of 476.35 million dollars. Export volumes rose to the highest level since data recording began in 1980, increasing by 32.6% year-on-year to 72.04 billion dollars. Imports grew by 24.1% to 67.52 billion dollars, also reaching a historical high; among them, intermediate product imports increased by 29.8% to 54.23 billion dollars.

Ararat Mirzoyan, Armenia's Foreign Minister, clarified that Armenia has no intention of severing political and economic ties with Russia. We hope and will continue to work to maintain and deepen our normal relations. (Interfax, Russian International News Agency)
The European Stoxx 50 index rose 2%, erasing all losses since the outbreak of the Iran conflict.

title: Trump Urges Saudi Arabia to Recognize Israel as Part of Iran Deal
summary: Trump is pressuring Saudi Arabia and Qatar to recognize Israel by joining the Abraham Accords. Trump stated that this would complement his interim peace agreement with Iran. Trump said Saudi Arabia and Qatar should sign the Abraham Accords immediately, and other countries including Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, and Jordan should follow suit. Trump also mentioned that Iran could join the Abraham Accords, but this is almost impossible under the current regime.

title: Brazilian President Undergoes Preventive Radiation Therapy
summary: The medical team of Brazilian President Lula released a medical report today (May 25) stating that Lula has begun receiving supplementary superficial radiation therapy for a scalp lesion one month after the removal of a skin lesion. The report also indicated that Lula will continue to maintain his daily activities without restrictions. Lula underwent a minor surgical procedure on April 24 in São Paulo to remove a skin lesion on his scalp. Brazilian media reported that the lesion removed was a basal cell carcinoma, and the treatment process went smoothly without any complications. Such lesions are typically associated with prolonged sun exposure and do not spread to other parts of the body.

title: Oil and LNG tankers depart Hormuz Strait for Pakistan and other destinations
summary: Vessel tracking data shows that LNG carriers Fuwairit, Al Rayyan, and Al Hamra have recently passed through the strait en route to Pakistan and India. Additionally, the super tanker (VLCC) Eagle Verona, which had been滞留 for nearly three months, has also departed.

title: Trump Says Iran Nuclear Talks 'Going Well,' Agreement Seems Near
summary: Trump stated that the temporary agreement negotiations with Iran regarding the extension of the ceasefire and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz are 'going well'. An Iranian delegation has traveled to Doha to hold discussions with Qatari senior officials on the talks, including the discussion of unfreezing frozen Iranian funds. The US and Iran still need to finalize some key details, including whether vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz will be allowed to travel freely, and when the several billion dollars in Iranian funds will be unfrozen.
Germany's DAX index rose 2% to 25,388.27 points. France's CAC index climbed 2% to 8,279.02 points.

title: Last-Minute Halt: SEC Suspends 'Tokenized U.S. Stocks' Initiative
summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has postponed a planned regulatory exemption for 'tokenized stocks,' which would have allowed third parties to issue digital tokens tracking stock prices without approval from the underlying companies. The initiative, if implemented, could lead to multiple token versions of the same stock, fragmenting market liquidity.

title: Coking Coal Futures Rise 9% Overnight, Coking Coal Gains Over 5%, Pure Benzene, Styrene, and Fuel Oil Drop Over 2%
summary: Most domestic futures markets closed lower overnight, with pure benzene and styrene falling 2.55%, and fuel oil declining 2.12%. Asphalt, low sulfur fuel oil, caustic soda, polypropylene, methanol, para-xylene, glass, and LPG declined by up to 1.99%. Iron ore fell 0.94%, while canola meal, rebar, hot rolled coil, soybean No.1, corn, soybean meal, plastic, synthetic rubber, short fiber, soybean No.2, rapeseed oil, PTA, PVC, sugar, and soybean oil declined by up to 0.90%. Refined rice and cotton closed flat overnight, while cotton yarn, 20# rubber, bottle flakes, ethylene glycol, paper pulp, and palm oil rose by up to 0.60%. Coking coal gained 5.14%, and coking coal futures rose 9.05%.

title: Honor 600 Series Launch: Balancing Configuration Amid Rising Costs
summary: On the evening of May 25, Honor launched the Honor 600 series in Xiamen, including three models: Yuanqi Edition, Super Edition, and Pro. The most anticipated aspect of the Honor 600 series was its pricing.

Mexican President Sheinbaum stated that after the U.S. expressed its disinterest in hosting a football match related to Iran, the Mexican government agreed to allow the Iranian national football team to stay in Mexico during the World Cup.

title: Honor 600 Series Officially Launched, Starting at 2,294.15 CNY with National Subsidy
summary: Honor 600 series was officially launched, featuring full-range 4K Live shooting and multiple eye-care technologies, along with a maximum 8600mAh battery. The Honor 600 series offers three models: Pro version, Super version, and Youth version, starting at 2,294.15 CNY with national subsidy.

title: Iranian Delegation Concludes Talks in Qatar, to Return to Tehran
summary: According to a report, the Iranian delegation led by Ali Vaez, speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, has concluded its meeting in Doha, the capital of Qatar, and will return to Tehran tonight. It is reported that the delegation's agenda in Qatar has been completed.

title: Man Sprays Unknown Substance in Tokyo's Ginza, Causing Multiple People to Feel Unwell
summary: According to police reports cited by Kyodo News on the 25th, a man sprayed an unknown substance near a commercial facility in Tokyo's Ginza district on the same day, resulting in at least one person being hospitalized and approximately 20 others experiencing physical discomfort. Local police received a call at noon regarding a "irritating odor" near a commercial facility in Ginza. Several people reported sore throats. A man had previously sprayed an unknown substance near the scene. Police stated that the man had left the location. Authorities are currently searching for his whereabouts and conducting a detailed investigation. (Global Times)

title: Iran's Supreme Leader's Advisor: Our Fingers Are on the Trigger While Negotiating with the US
summary: On May 24, Iran held an event to commemorate the Battle of Khorramshahr during the Iran-Iraq War. At the event, Mohsen Rezaei, the military advisor to the Supreme Leader, stated that Iran has its fingers on the trigger while negotiating with the United States. If the US chooses to continue the conflict, Iran will cause the US economy to collapse. Rezaei said that Iran has presented the most cost-effective path to the US, and is prepared for a fair negotiation. The US killed Iran's Supreme Leader and commander, yet Iran remains willing to engage in dialogue with the US, and the US should view negotiations with Iran as a 'valuable opportunity'.
Iran demands to transfer uranium to China, according to market sources.
